416	def _finished(study) -> int:
417	    import optuna
418	    return sum(1 for t in study.trials
419	               if t.state in (optuna.trial.TrialState.COMPLETE,
420	                              optuna.trial.TrialState.PRUNED,
421	                              optuna.trial.TrialState.FAIL))
422	
423	
424	# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
425	# Modes
426	# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
427	
428	def _sweep_orphan_trials(studies, wid, max_age_hours=2.0):
429	    """[A6-MED] Startup orphan sweep: a worker that died mid-trial (OOM kill,
430	    node preemption) leaves its trial stuck in RUNNING forever, and
431	    _finished() never counts it, so the study can never reach its target. On
432	    startup, fail any RUNNING trial older than `max_age_hours` so the budget
433	    accounting recovers. Per-trial try/except + loud print so one storage
434	    hiccup can't abort the sweep.
435	
436	    NOTE (accepted-benign): a trial legitimately still running past 2h on a
437	    genuinely slow cell could be failed here and re-run — wasted compute, but
438	    NOT a correctness problem (the re-run just adds another sample to the
439	    study). We accept that over the alternative (orphans wedging the budget)."""
440	    import optuna
441	    from datetime import datetime, timedelta
442	    cutoff = datetime.now() - timedelta(hours=max_age_hours)
443	    for o, s in studies.items():
444	        storage = s._storage
445	        try:
446	            trials = s.get_trials(deepcopy=False)
447	        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
448	            print(f"[worker {wid}] orphan-sweep {o}: get_trials failed: {exc!r}", flush=True)
449	            continue
450	        for t in trials:
451	            if t.state != optuna.trial.TrialState.RUNNING:
452	                continue
453	            started = t.datetime_start
454	            if started is not None and started > cutoff:
455	                continue  # still within budget — leave it
456	            try:
457	                storage.set_trial_state_values(t._trial_id, optuna.trial.TrialState.FAIL)
458	                print(f"[worker {wid}] orphan-sweep {o}: FAILED stale RUNNING "
459	                      f"trial#{t.number} (started {started})", flush=True)
460	            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
461	                print(f"[worker {wid}] orphan-sweep {o}: could not fail "
462	                      f"trial#{t.number}: {exc!r}", flush=True)
463	
464	
465	def mode_worker(args):
466	    """One worker process: round-robin one trial per study until all done."""
467	    wid = args.worker_id
468	    studies = {o: get_study(o, args.model, worker_seed=wid) for o in args.opts}
469	    objectives = {o: make_objective(o, args.model) for o in args.opts}
470	    _sweep_orphan_trials(studies, wid)  # [A6-MED] recover budget from dead workers
471	    while True:
472	        progressed = False
473	        for o in args.opts:
474	            s = studies[o]
475	            if _finished(s) >= args.trials_per_opt:
476	                continue
477	            progressed = True
478	            try:
479	                s.optimize(objectives[o], n_trials=1, gc_after_trial=True)
480	            except Exception as exc:  # storage hiccup etc. — keep the worker alive
481	                print(f"[worker {wid}] {o}: {exc!r}", flush=True)
482	                time.sleep(2)
483	        if not progressed:
484	            break
485	    print(f"[worker {wid}] all studies at target — exiting", flush=True)
486	
487	
488	def mode_launch(args):
489	    """Spawn N workers, wait, then write the report."""
490	    LOG_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
491	    procs = []
492	    for i in range(args.workers):
493	        log = open(LOG_DIR / f"worker_{args.model}_{i}.log", "w")
494	        cmd = [sys.executable, "-m", "tuning.tune_optimizers", "--worker",
495	               "--worker-id", str(i), "--model", args.model,
496	               "--trials-per-opt", str(args.trials_per_opt),
497	               "--opts", ",".join(args.opts)]
498	        procs.append((subprocess.Popen(cmd, cwd=ROOT, stdout=log, stderr=log), log))
499	        time.sleep(3)  # stagger CUDA context creation
500	    print(f"launched {len(procs)} workers (logs: {LOG_DIR})", flush=True)
501	    for p, log in procs:
502	        p.wait(); log.close()
503	    print("all workers done", flush=True)
504	    mode_report(args)
505	
506	
507	def _confirm_score(out, cap):
508	    """[A6-HIGH] TEST-CONFIRMED steps-to-grok score for one confirm run, mirroring
509	    the search objective exactly:
510	      • grokked (val-grok AND test ≥ 0.90)        → grokking_step  (≤ cap)
511	      • val-grok but test < 0.90 (fake-grok)      → cap + (1−final_test_acc)·cap
512	      • no val-grok                               → cap + (1−peak_val_acc)·cap
513	    Returns (grokked: bool, score: float)."""
514	    grokked = out["grokking_step"] is not None and out["final_test_acc"] >= 0.90
515	    if grokked:
516	        return True, float(out["grokking_step"])
517	    if out["grokking_step"] is not None:  # val-grok that did NOT confirm on test
518	        return False, cap + (1.0 - out["final_test_acc"]) * cap
519	    return False, cap + (1.0 - out["peak_val_acc"]) * cap
520	
521	
522	def mode_confirm(args):
523	    """Re-run each study's top-K configs on the confirm seeds; pick winners.
524	
525	    [A6] The winner is the config grokking (TEST-CONFIRMED) ALL confirm seeds,
526	    ranked by MEDIAN steps. Fall back to the config grokking the MOST seeds, then
527	    median. TEST-confirmation (not val-grok alone) is the gate at every seed —
528	    val-trained meta-nets can fake-grok val."""
529	    import optuna
530	    cap = CAPS[args.model]
531	    winners = {}
532	    for o in args.opts:
533	        s = get_study(o, args.model)
534	        done = [t for t in s.trials if t.state == optuna.trial.TrialState.COMPLETE]
535	        if not done:
536	            print(f"[confirm] {o}: no completed trials"); continue
537	        top = sorted(done, key=lambda t: t.value)[:args.top_k]
538	        rows = []
539	        for t in top:
540	            # Seed 1001 (the trial seed) is re-derived from the trial's own
541	            # outcome so its grokked flag uses the SAME test-confirmation gate.
542	            t1001_grokked = (t.value is not None and t.value <= cap
543	                             and float(t.user_attrs.get("final_test_acc") or 0.0) >= 0.90)
544	            steps = {TUNING_SEED: float(t.value)}
545	            grokked_by_seed = {TUNING_SEED: bool(t1001_grokked)}
546	            test_acc_by_seed = {TUNING_SEED: float(t.user_attrs.get("final_test_acc") or 0.0)}
547	            for seed in CONFIRM_SEEDS:
548	                out = run_trial_config(o, args.model, t.params, seed)
549	                gk, sc = _confirm_score(out, cap)
550	                steps[seed] = sc
551	                grokked_by_seed[seed] = gk
552	                test_acc_by_seed[seed] = float(out["final_test_acc"])
553	                print(f"[confirm] {o} trial#{t.number} seed{seed}: "
554	                      f"{sc:.0f} {'GROK' if gk else 'DNF'} "
555	                      f"(test={out['final_test_acc']:.3f})", flush=True)
556	            # Robustness gate is over the held-out CONFIRM_SEEDS (test-confirmed).
557	            confirm_grokked = [grokked_by_seed[seed] for seed in CONFIRM_SEEDS]
558	            n_confirm_grokked = sum(confirm_grokked)
559	            grokked_all = all(confirm_grokked)
560	            rows.append({"trial": t.number, "params": t.params,
561	                         "steps_by_seed": steps,
562	                         "grokked_by_seed": grokked_by_seed,
563	                         "test_acc_by_seed": test_acc_by_seed,
564	                         "grokked_all": grokked_all,
565	                         "n_confirm_grokked": n_confirm_grokked,
566	                         "median_steps": statistics.median(steps.values()),
567	                         "mean_steps": sum(steps.values()) / len(steps)})
568	        # [A6] Winner: maximize confirm seeds grokked (so "all confirm seeds"
569	        # wins outright), break ties by MEDIAN steps. This is exactly "grok ALL
570	        # → most seeds → median" as a single key.
571	        best = min(rows, key=lambda r: (-r["n_confirm_grokked"], r["median_steps"]))
572	        winners[o] = best
573	        print(f"[confirm] {o}: winner trial#{best['trial']} "
574	              f"median={best['median_steps']:.0f} "
575	              f"confirm_grokked={best['n_confirm_grokked']}/{len(CONFIRM_SEEDS)} "
576	              f"robust_all={best['grokked_all']}", flush=True)
577	    out_path = TUNE_DIR / f"tuned_configs_{args.model}.json"
578	    existing = json.loads(out_path.read_text()) if out_path.exists() else {}
579	    for o, w in winners.items():
580	        existing[o] = {"model": args.model, "params": w["params"],
581	                       "steps_by_seed": {str(k): v for k, v in w["steps_by_seed"].items()},
582	                       "grokked_by_seed": {str(k): v for k, v in w["grokked_by_seed"].items()},
583	                       "test_acc_by_seed": {str(k): v for k, v in w["test_acc_by_seed"].items()},  # [A6] persist per-seed final_test_acc
584	                       "robust_all_seeds": w["grokked_all"],
585	                       "n_confirm_grokked": w["n_confirm_grokked"],
586	                       "median_steps": w["median_steps"],
587	                       "mean_steps": w["mean_steps"], "trial": w["trial"]}
588	    out_path.write_text(json.dumps(existing, indent=2))
589	    print(f"wrote {out_path}", flush=True)
590	
591	
592	def mode_report(args):
593	    import optuna
594	    TUNE_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
595	    lines = [f"# Tuning report — model={args.model}",
596	             f"Objective: steps to val_acc ≥ 0.95 (cap {CAPS[args.model]}; "
597	             f"DNF = cap + (1−peak_val)·cap). Seed {TUNING_SEED}.", ""]
598	    csv_path = TUNE_DIR / f"trials_{args.model}.csv"
599	    with open(csv_path, "w", newline="") as fh:
600	        w = csv.writer(fh)
601	        w.writerow(["optimizer", "trial", "state", "value", "peak_val_acc",
602	                    "final_test_acc", "params"])
603	        for o in args.opts:
604	            s = get_study(o, args.model)
605	            ts = s.trials
606	            comp = [t for t in ts if t.state == optuna.trial.TrialState.COMPLETE]
607	            pruned = [t for t in ts if t.state == optuna.trial.TrialState.PRUNED]
608	            for t in ts:
609	                w.writerow([o, t.number, t.state.name, t.value,
610	                            t.user_attrs.get("peak_val_acc"),
611	                            t.user_attrs.get("final_test_acc"),
612	                            json.dumps(t.params)])
613	            lines.append(f"## {o} — {len(ts)} trials ({len(comp)} complete, "
614	                         f"{len(pruned)} pruned)")
615	            if comp:
616	                best = min(comp, key=lambda t: t.value)
617	                grokked = best.value <= CAPS[args.model]
618	                lines.append(f"- best: trial#{best.number} value={best.value:.0f} "
619	                             f"({'GROKKED' if grokked else 'DNF'})")
620	                lines.append(f"- params: `{json.dumps(best.params)}`")
621	            lines.append("")
622	    (TUNE_DIR / f"TUNING_REPORT_{args.model}.md").write_text("\n".join(lines))
623	    print(f"wrote {TUNE_DIR / f'TUNING_REPORT_{args.model}.md'} and {csv_path}", flush=True)
624	
625	
626	def mode_measure(args):
627	    """Aggregate-throughput knee: K concurrent plain-AdamW runs."""
628	    script = (
629	        "import sys, time, torch; sys.path.insert(0, %r);\n"
630	        "import grokking_race_v2 as g\n"
631	        "c = dict(g.DEFAULT_CONFIG); c.update(g.OPTIMIZER_CONFIGS['adamw'])\n"
632	        "c.update({'seed': 1001, 'model_type': %r, 'frac_train': 0.5, 'val_ratio': 0.10,\n"
633	        "          'p': 97, 'use_amp': False, 'compile_model': False, 'max_steps': 600,\n"
634	        "          'early_stop_max_steps': 600, 'eval_every': 10**9,\n"
635	        "          'early_stop_threshold': 1.01, 'early_stop_patience': 10**9})\n"
636	        "data = tuple(d.to('cuda') for d in g.make_data_for_task(c, 1001))\n"
637	        "m0 = g.build_model(c, torch.device('cuda'))\n"
638	        "init = {k: v.detach().cpu().clone() for k, v in m0.state_dict().items()}\n"
639	        "del m0; torch.manual_seed(1001); t0 = time.time()\n"
640	        "g.train_adamw(c, init, *data, torch.device('cuda'), bp=0)\n"
641	        "torch.cuda.synchronize(); print('WALL', time.time() - t0)\n"
642	    ) % (str(ROOT), args.model)
643	    for k in args.measure:
644	        t0 = time.time()
645	        procs = [subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "-c", script], cwd=ROOT,
646	                                  stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
647	                 for _ in range(k)]
648	        walls = []
649	        for p in procs:
650	            out, _ = p.communicate()
651	            for line in out.decode().splitlines():
652	                if line.startswith("WALL"):
653	                    walls.append(float(line.split()[1]))
654	        total = time.time() - t0
655	        agg = 600.0 * k / total
656	        per = [600.0 / w for w in walls]
657	        print(f"K={k}: aggregate={agg:7.1f} steps/s  per-run="
658	              f"{min(per):5.1f}-{max(per):5.1f}  wall={total:5.1f}s", flush=True)
659	
660	
661	def main():
662	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
663	    ap.add_argument("--model", default="decoder", choices=list(CAPS))
664	    ap.add_argument("--opts", default=",".join(OPTS))
665	    ap.add_argument("--trials-per-opt", type=int, default=40)
666	    ap.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=6)
667	    ap.add_argument("--worker", action="store_true")
668	    ap.add_argument("--worker-id", type=int, default=0)
669	    ap.add_argument("--launch", action="store_true")
670	    ap.add_argument("--confirm", action="store_true")
671	    ap.add_argument("--report", action="store_true")
672	    ap.add_argument("--top-k", type=int, default=5)  # [A6] 3→5: confirm more candidates per study
673	    ap.add_argument("--measure", type=int, nargs="*", default=None)
674	    args = ap.parse_args()
675	    args.opts = [o.strip() for o in args.opts.split(",") if o.strip()]
676	    for o in args.opts:
677	        assert o in SPACES, f"unknown optimizer {o}"
678	    if args.measure is not None:
679	        mode_measure(args)
680	    elif args.worker:
681	        mode_worker(args)
682	    elif args.launch:
683	        mode_launch(args)
684	    elif args.confirm:
685	        mode_confirm(args)
686	    elif args.report:
687	        mode_report(args)
688	    else:
689	        ap.print_help()
690	
691	
692	if __name__ == "__main__":
693	    main()

4	in ``grokking_optimizers/_tuned_inject.py`` — the same functions setup.py's

218	def _esc(s):
219	    return s.replace(":", "$:").replace(" ", "$ ")

222	def _write_fake_ninja(directory, edges, base_cuda_post):
223	    """edges: list of (src, obj, rule) where rule in {compile, cuda_compile}."""
224	    path = os.path.join(directory, "build.ninja")
225	    lines = [
226	        "ninja_required_version = 1.3",
227	        "cxx = c++", "nvcc = nvcc",
228	        "cflags = -O3", "post_cflags = -std=c++17",
229	        "cuda_cflags = -I/repo",
230	        f"cuda_post_cflags = {base_cuda_post}",
231	        "cuda_dlink_post_cflags = ", "ldflags = -shared",
232	        "rule compile",
233	        "  command = $cxx -MMD -MF $out.d $cflags -c $in -o $out $post_cflags",
234	        "rule cuda_compile",
235	        "  command = $nvcc $cuda_cflags -c $in -o $out $cuda_post_cflags",
236	    ]
237	    for src, obj, rule in edges:
238	        lines.append(f"build {_esc(obj)}: {rule} {_esc(src)}")
239	    lines.append("")
240	    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
241	        fh.write("\n".join(lines))
242	    return path

386	# 5. Drift guard: MACROS source-of-truth vs the LIVE committed kernel headers.
387	#
388	# The eager grokking_optimizers/kernels/sm_90/*_sm90.cuh headers (whose guards
389	# were SG_TUNED_BLOCK_SIZE/VEC_WIDTH/UNROLL/ASYNC_DEPTH) were DELETED; the macros
390	# the committed kernels actually read now live in csrc/. This scans the LIVE
391	# headers that carry each floor macro's `#ifndef SG_TUNED_X / #define SG_TUNED_X
392	# N` guard (the file:line set documented next to MACROS in _tuned_inject.py) and
393	# asserts every macro in header_default_macros() is #defined there with the
394	# matching default — so a kernel renaming/redefaulting a guard, or the MACROS
395	# table drifting from the headers, fails HERE (silent -D no-ops / missed guards).
396	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
397	# Headers in include-priority order: the substrate (wgmma.cuh) and the
398	# common/pipeline headers are #included first, so when a macro is multiply
399	# #ifndef'd (e.g. SG_TUNED_TILE_M is also re-guarded =64 in the mamba TC stage)
400	# the FIRST default seen wins — exactly what the MACROS table records.
401	_DRIFT_HEADERS = (
402	    os.path.join("csrc", "backends", "cuda", "sm_90", "wgmma.cuh"),
403	    os.path.join("csrc", "backends", "cuda", "sm_90", "tile_pipeline.cuh"),
404	    os.path.join("csrc", "fused", "megakernel_common.cuh"),
405	    os.path.join("csrc", "fused", "sm_90", "model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh"),
406	    os.path.join("csrc", "fused", "sm_90", "model_stage_vit_tc.cuh"),
407	    os.path.join("csrc", "fused", "sm_90", "model_stage_mamba_tc.cuh"),
408	)
409	
410	
411	def test_macro_drift_against_header():
412	    # Parse `#define SG_TUNED_X <int>` across the live floor headers; first
413	    # definition per macro wins (include order above).
414	    parsed = {}
415	    seen_any = False
416	    for rel in _DRIFT_HEADERS:
417	        header = os.path.join(_REPO_ROOT, rel)
418	        if not os.path.isfile(header):
419	            continue
420	        seen_any = True
421	        text = open(header, encoding="utf-8").read()
422	        for m in re.finditer(r"#define\s+(SG_TUNED_[A-Z0-9_]+)\s+(\d+)", text):
423	            parsed.setdefault(m.group(1), int(m.group(2)))
424	    if not seen_any:
425	        print("  SKIP: no live SG_TUNED floor headers found under csrc/ "
426	              "(drift check skipped)")
427	        return
428	    expected = ti.header_default_macros()  # {macro: default} (kind=='macro')
429	    for macro, default in expected.items():
430	        check(macro in parsed,
431	              f"macro {macro} from MACROS is #defined in a live csrc/ header")
432	        if macro in parsed:
433	            eq(parsed[macro], default,
434	               f"{macro} default in the committed header matches MACROS table")

438	# 6. torch-INTEGRATION test (skipped if torch is unavailable).
439	#
440	# The pure-logic tests above run the rewrite on a HAND-WRITTEN build.ninja.
441	# This one drives torch's REAL `_write_ninja_file_and_compile_objects` through
442	# the SAME module-level _write_ninja_file monkeypatch setup.py installs, so it
443	# proves the two things the isolation tests structurally cannot:
444	#   (a) torch's bare-name call to _write_ninja_file (cpp_extension.py:1771)
445	#       actually resolves to OUR patched function, and
446	#   (b) our ninja parser matches torch's ACTUAL `build <obj>: cuda_compile
447	#       <src>` emission/escaping — not our synthetic copy of it.
448	# It compiles NOTHING: _run_ninja_build (and the hermeticity helpers) are
449	# stubbed, and build.ninja is written BEFORE _run_ninja_build is called.

451	def test_torch_integration_real_ninja_writer():
452	    try:
453	        import torch  # noqa: F401
454	        import torch.utils.cpp_extension as cpp
455	    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
456	        print(f"  SKIP: torch unavailable ({type(exc).__name__}); "
457	              "torch-integration test skipped (pure-logic tests cover the rest)")
458	        return
459	
460	    import shlex as _shlex
461	
462	    d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
463	    # Mixed real-format sources: an adamw launcher (.cu), a binding (.cpp),
464	    # and a muon mega cell (.cu). Absolute object paths (torch abspaths them).
465	    src_adamw = os.path.join(d, "launch_adamw.cu")
466	    src_bind = os.path.join(d, "dispatch.cpp")
467	    src_mega = os.path.join(d, "mega_vit_muon.cu")
468	    for p in (src_adamw, src_bind, src_mega):
469	        with open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
470	            fh.write("// stub\n")
471	    obj_adamw = os.path.join(d, "launch_adamw.o")
472	    obj_bind = os.path.join(d, "dispatch.o")
473	    obj_mega = os.path.join(d, "mega_vit_muon.o")
474	    sources = [src_adamw, src_bind, src_mega]
475	    objects = [obj_adamw, obj_bind, obj_mega]
476	
477	    tuned = _sample_tuned()  # adamw + muon have winners under "sm_90"
478	
479	    # The SAME wrapper setup.py's TunedBuildExtension installs.
480	    orig_writer = cpp._write_ninja_file
481	
482	    def patched_writer(*args, **kwargs):
483	        orig_writer(*args, **kwargs)
484	        ti.inject_overrides_into_ninja(
485	            kwargs.get("path"), list(kwargs.get("sources")),
486	            list(kwargs.get("objects")),
487	            list(kwargs.get("cuda_post_cflags") or []),
488	            tuned, "sm_90", quote=_shlex.quote)
489	
490	    # Hermetic stubs so nothing touches a real toolchain / runs ninja.
491	    saved = {
492	        "_write_ninja_file": cpp._write_ninja_file,
493	        "_run_ninja_build": cpp._run_ninja_build,
494	        "verify_ninja_availability": cpp.verify_ninja_availability,
495	        "get_compiler_abi_compatibility_and_version":
496	            cpp.get_compiler_abi_compatibility_and_version,
497	        "get_cxx_compiler": cpp.get_cxx_compiler,
498	    }
499	    try:
500	        cpp._write_ninja_file = patched_writer
501	        cpp._run_ninja_build = lambda *a, **k: None         # no compile
502	        cpp.verify_ninja_availability = lambda *a, **k: None
503	        cpp.get_compiler_abi_compatibility_and_version = \
504	            lambda *a, **k: (True, "0.0")
505	        cpp.get_cxx_compiler = lambda *a, **k: "c++"
506	        cpp._write_ninja_file_and_compile_objects(
507	            sources=sources, objects=objects,
508	            cflags=["-O3"], post_cflags=["-std=c++17"],
509	            cuda_cflags=["-I/repo"],
510	            cuda_post_cflags=["-O3", "--use_fast_math",
511	                              "-gencode=arch=compute_90a,code=sm_90a"],
512	            cuda_dlink_post_cflags=None,
513	            build_directory=d, verbose=False, with_cuda=True)
514	    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
515	        _FAILURES.append(f"torch-integration call raised: {exc!r}")
516	        return
517	    finally:
518	        for k, v in saved.items():
519	            setattr(cpp, k, v)
520	
521	    ninja_path = os.path.join(d, "build.ninja")
522	    check(os.path.isfile(ninja_path),
523	          "torch wrote build.ninja in the build_directory")
524	    if not os.path.isfile(ninja_path):
525	        return
526	    text = open(ninja_path, encoding="utf-8").read()
527	
528	    # Our parser matched torch's REAL emission: adamw + muon edges have
529	    # overrides; the .cpp edge does not.
530	    overrides = [ln for ln in text.splitlines()
531	                 if ln.strip().startswith("cuda_post_cflags =")
532	                 and "SG_TUNED" in ln]
533	    eq(len(overrides), 2,
534	       "2 override lines injected into torch's real build.ninja "
535	       "(adamw + muon .cu edges)")
536	    check(any("SG_TUNED_MEGA_BLOCK=128" in ln for ln in overrides),
537	          "adamw override present in torch's real build.ninja")
538	    check(any("SG_TUNED_MEGA_BLOCK=256" in ln for ln in overrides),
539	          "muon override present in torch's real build.ninja")
540	    for ln in overrides:
541	        check("--use_fast_math" in ln and "compute_90a" in ln,
542	              f"base flags preserved in real-ninja override: {ln!r}")
543	    # the binding object must not be followed by an override line.

546	        if ln.startswith("build ") and "dispatch.o" in ln:
547	            nxt = lines[i + 1] if i + 1 < len(lines) else ""
548	            check(not nxt.strip().startswith("cuda_post_cflags ="),
549	                  "dispatch.cpp edge has NO override in torch's real build.ninja")

1	"""A/A/A bit-identity + simple cross-impl check for the embed-grad hill-climb.
2	Builds the d-scaled bench variant, runs tc_train_step 3x from identical inputs,
3	and asserts the returned reduced-grad tensor is BITWISE identical across reruns.
4	Also prints a hash so before/after kernels can be compared structurally.
5	"""
6	import sys, hashlib
7	from pathlib import Path
8	ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
9	sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
10	import torch
11	from tuning.decoder_bench import build_variant
12	
13	def run(d, B, name):
14	    mod = build_variant(d, profile=False, name=name)
15	    dev = torch.device("cuda")
16	    total = int(mod.TOTAL); vocab = int(mod.VOCAB); seq = int(mod.SEQ)
17	    def fresh():
18	        g = torch.Generator(device=dev).manual_seed(42)
19	        params = (torch.randn(total, generator=g, device=dev) * 0.02).contiguous()
20	        tokens = torch.randint(0, vocab, (B, seq), generator=g, device=dev).to(torch.int32).contiguous()
21	        targets = torch.randint(0, vocab, (B,), generator=g, device=dev).to(torch.int32).contiguous()
22	        state = torch.zeros(3 * total, dtype=torch.float32, device=dev)
23	        return params, tokens, targets, state
24	    hashes = []
25	    grads = []
26	    for _ in range(3):
27	        params, tokens, targets, state = fresh()
28	        loss, grad = mod.tc_train_step(params, tokens, targets, state,
29	                                       1e-3, 0.9, 0.98, 1e-8, 0.0, 1.0-0.9, 1.0-0.98, 1, 0)
30	        gb = grad.detach().cpu().contiguous().numpy().tobytes()
31	        hashes.append(hashlib.sha256(gb).hexdigest())
32	        grads.append(grad.detach().cpu().clone())
33	    ok = len(set(hashes)) == 1
34	    print(f"[A/A/A d={d} B={B}] grad sha256 x3: {[h[:16] for h in hashes]}  -> {'BIT-IDENTICAL' if ok else 'DIVERGED!!!'}")
35	    # exact max-abs delta between rerun 0 and 1/2 (should be exactly 0.0)
36	    for k in (1,2):
37	        md = (grads[0]-grads[k]).abs().max().item()
38	        print(f"    max|grad[0]-grad[{k}]| = {md:.3e}")
39	    return ok, hashes[0]
40	
41	if __name__ == "__main__":
42	    import argparse
43	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
44	    ap.add_argument("--d", type=int, default=1024)
45	    ap.add_argument("--B", type=int, default=16384)
46	    ap.add_argument("--name", type=str, default=None)
47	    a = ap.parse_args()
48	    ok, h = run(a.d, a.B, a.name)
49	    sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)

1	"""H3 dW-interleave A/A/A + parity probe (d=1024 bench layout).
2	
3	Two checks on the d=1024 decoder TC cell:
4	  (A) DETERMINISM: 3 runs of one tc_train_step from the SAME inputs → params+state
5	      bit-identical (sha256). The dW move must not introduce any nondeterminism.
6	  (P) PARITY vs the pre-change BASELINE: rebuilds the UNMODIFIED header from a git
7	      checkout of the named baseline ref into a SEPARATE module, runs the same one
8	      step, and asserts the post-step (params,state,loss) is BIT-IDENTICAL. The
9	      M-atom interleave only reorders independent-fragment MMAs + restages the
10	      shared operand (ascending-k preserved per atom) → must be bitwise-exact.
11	
12	Usage:
13	  python tuning/_h3_dw_aaa.py --baseline-ref c67cb66 [--d 1024 --B 16384]
14	"""
15	from __future__ import annotations
16	import argparse, hashlib, os, subprocess, sys, tempfile, shutil
17	from pathlib import Path
18	
19	ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
20	sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
21	import torch  # noqa: E402
22	from torch.utils.cpp_extension import load  # noqa: E402
23	
24	TU_REL = "csrc/fused/sm_90/mega_decoder_real_adamw_tc.cu"
25	
26	
27	def _flags(d: int, profile: bool = False):
28	    f = ["-O3", "-std=c++17", "--expt-relaxed-constexpr",
29	         "-gencode=arch=compute_90a,code=sm_90a",
30	         "-gencode=arch=compute_90a,code=compute_90a",
31	         "-DSG_TUNED_GEMM_IMPL=1"]
32	    if d != 128:
33	        f += ["-DSG_DEC_BENCH_LAYOUT=1", "-DSG_DEC_SCALAR_MEGAKERNEL=0"]
34	    return f
35	
36	
37	def _build(name, sources_root, d):
38	    """Build the TU rooted at `sources_root` (a checkout dir or the live tree)."""
39	    os.environ.setdefault("TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST", "9.0a")
40	    tu = str(Path(sources_root) / TU_REL)
41	    bdir = Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / f"build_{name}"
42	    bdir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
43	    return load(name=name, sources=[tu],
44	                extra_include_paths=[str(sources_root)],
45	                extra_cuda_cflags=_flags(d),
46	                extra_cflags=["-O3", "-std=c++17"],
47	                build_directory=str(bdir),
48	                verbose=False)
49	
50	
51	def _one_step_hash(mod, d, B, seed=42):
52	    dev = torch.device("cuda")
53	    total = int(mod.TOTAL)
54	    vocab, seq = int(mod.VOCAB), int(mod.SEQ)
55	    assert int(mod.D) == d
56	    g = torch.Generator(device=dev).manual_seed(seed)
57	    params = (torch.randn(total, generator=g, device=dev) * 0.02).contiguous()
58	    tokens = torch.randint(0, vocab, (B, seq), generator=g, device=dev).to(torch.int32).contiguous()
59	    targets = torch.randint(0, vocab, (B,), generator=g, device=dev).to(torch.int32).contiguous()
60	    state = torch.zeros(3 * total, dtype=torch.float32, device=dev)
61	    lr, b1, b2, eps, wd = 1e-3, 0.9, 0.98, 1e-8, 0.0
62	    bc1, bc2 = 1.0 - b1, 1.0 - b2
63	    loss = mod.tc_train_step(params, tokens, targets, state, lr, b1, b2, eps, wd, bc1, bc2, 1, 0)
64	    torch.cuda.synchronize()
65	    h = hashlib.sha256()
66	    h.update(params.detach().cpu().numpy().tobytes())
67	    h.update(state.detach().cpu().numpy().tobytes())
68	    # loss may come back as a python float, a tensor, or a 1-element list/tuple.
69	    def _scalar(x):
70	        if x is None: return float("nan")
71	        if isinstance(x, (list, tuple)): x = x[0]
72	        try: return float(x.item()) if hasattr(x, "item") else float(x)
73	        except Exception: return float("nan")
74	    return h.hexdigest(), _scalar(loss), params.clone(), state.clone()
75	
76	
77	def main():
78	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
79	    ap.add_argument("--d", type=int, default=1024)
80	    ap.add_argument("--B", type=int, default=16384)
81	    ap.add_argument("--baseline-ref", type=str, default="c67cb66")
82	    args = ap.parse_args()
83	
84	    print(f"[h3-aaa] building LIVE (modified) d={args.d} ...", flush=True)
85	    mod = _build("dec_h3_live", str(ROOT), args.d)
86	
87	    # (A) determinism A/A/A
88	    hashes = []
89	    for i in range(3):
90	        hx, lv, _, _ = _one_step_hash(mod, args.d, args.B)
91	        hashes.append(hx)
92	        print(f"  [A/A/A] run{i}: sha256={hx[:16]}  loss={lv:.8f}", flush=True)
93	    aaa_ok = len(set(hashes)) == 1
94	    print(f"  => A/A/A bit-identical: {'PASS' if aaa_ok else 'FAIL'}", flush=True)
95	
96	    # (P) parity vs baseline ref (checkout the TU + its includes into a temp dir)
97	    print(f"\n[h3-aaa] checking out baseline ref {args.baseline_ref} for parity ...", flush=True)
98	    base_dir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="h3_base_"))
99	    # archive the whole tree at the ref (need the includes), extract to base_dir.
100	    arch = subprocess.run(["git", "archive", args.baseline_ref], cwd=str(ROOT),
101	                          capture_output=True)
102	    if arch.returncode != 0:
103	        print(f"  git archive failed: {arch.stderr.decode()[:200]}", flush=True)
104	        sys.exit(2)
105	    tar = base_dir / "tree.tar"
106	    tar.write_bytes(arch.stdout)
107	    subprocess.run(["tar", "xf", str(tar), "-C", str(base_dir)], check=True)
108	    print(f"  building BASELINE d={args.d} from {base_dir} ...", flush=True)
109	    base_mod = _build("dec_h3_base", str(base_dir), args.d)
110	    bh, blv, _, _ = _one_step_hash(base_mod, args.d, args.B)
111	    lh = hashes[0]
112	    print(f"  [parity] baseline sha256={bh[:16]}  loss={blv:.8f}", flush=True)
113	    print(f"  [parity] live     sha256={lh[:16]}", flush=True)
114	    par_ok = (bh == lh)
115	    print(f"  => PARITY (live == baseline {args.baseline_ref}) bit-identical: "
116	          f"{'PASS' if par_ok else 'FAIL'}", flush=True)
117	    shutil.rmtree(base_dir, ignore_errors=True)
118	
119	    print(f"\n[h3-aaa] RESULT: A/A/A={'PASS' if aaa_ok else 'FAIL'}  "
120	          f"PARITY={'PASS' if par_ok else 'FAIL'}", flush=True)
121	    sys.exit(0 if (aaa_ok and par_ok) else 1)
122	
123	
124	if __name__ == "__main__":
125	    main()

4	wall to phases by NULLING OUT one phase at a time (compile-time -D flags, default-0

25	             "-gencode=arch=compute_90a,code=sm_90a",

35	        call()
36	    torch.cuda.synchronize()
37	    t0 = time.perf_counter()
38	    for _ in range(iters):
39	        call()
40	    torch.cuda.synchronize()
41	    return (time.perf_counter() - t0) / iters * 1e3   # ms
42	
43	
44	def main():
45	    dev = torch.device("cuda")
46	    torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 = False
47	    # Variants: name -> list of -D defines. mod_<name> is a distinct JIT module.
48	    variants = {
49	        "baseline":     [],
50	        "no_dw_gemm":   ["SG_MBTC_BYPASS_DW_GEMM=1"],
51	        "no_scan":      ["SG_MBTC_BYPASS_SCAN=1"],
52	        "no_embedscan": ["SG_MBTC_BYPASS_EMBED_SCAN=1"],
53	    }
54	    print(f"[mbtc-bypass] B={B}  T={B*SEQ}  quiet={os.environ.get('CUDA_MPS_PIPE_DIRECTORY')}")
55	    results = {}
56	    base_ms = None
57	    base_sc_ms = None
58	    for name, defs in variants.items():
59	        try:
60	            mod = build(f"mbtc_bp_{name}", defs)
61	        except Exception as e:
62	            print(f"  {name:14s} BUILD FAILED: {str(e)[:200]}")
63	            continue
64	        total = int(mod.TOTAL)
65	        gpar = torch.Generator(device=dev).manual_seed(42)
66	        params = (torch.randn(total, generator=gpar, device=dev) * 0.02).contiguous()
67	        gin = torch.Generator(device=dev).manual_seed(7)
68	        inp = torch.randint(0, VOCAB, (B, SEQ), generator=gin, device=dev).to(torch.int32)
69	        tgt = torch.randint(0, P_HEAD, (B,), generator=gin, device=dev).to(torch.int32)
70	        state = torch.zeros(3 * total, dtype=torch.float32, device=dev)
71	        beta1, beta2 = 0.9, 0.98
72	        bc1, bc2 = 1.0 - beta1, 1.0 - beta2
73	
74	        def tc_call():
75	            return mod.tc_train_step(params.clone(), inp, tgt, state, 1e-3, beta1, beta2,
76	                                     1e-8, 0.0, bc1, bc2, 1, 0)
77	        ms = time_call(tc_call)
78	        results[name] = {"tc_ms": ms}
79	        if name == "baseline":
80	            base_ms = ms
81	            # scalar baseline from the SAME module (back-to-back, same contention)
82	            def sc_call():
83	                return mod.scalar_train_step(params.clone(), inp, tgt, state, 1e-3, beta1,
84	                                             beta2, 1e-8, 0.0, bc1, bc2, 1)
85	            base_sc_ms = time_call(sc_call)
86	            results["scalar_baseline"] = {"tc_ms": base_sc_ms}
87	            print(f"  {'baseline (TC)':18s} {ms:8.3f} ms")
88	            print(f"  {'baseline (scalar)':18s} {base_sc_ms:8.3f} ms   "
89	                  f"(scalar/TC = {base_sc_ms/ms:.3f}x; TC must beat 1.0 to win)")
90	        else:
91	            delta = base_ms - ms
92	            pct = 100.0 * delta / base_ms
93	            print(f"  {name:18s} {ms:8.3f} ms   phase≈{delta:7.3f} ms ({pct:5.1f}% of TC wall)")
94	    out = os.path.join(ROOT, "results/h100_grokking_race/mbtc_bypass_profile.json")
95	    json.dump({"B": B, "T": B*SEQ, "baseline_tc_ms": base_ms,
96	               "baseline_scalar_ms": base_sc_ms, "variants": results}, open(out, "w"), indent=2)
97	    print(f"[mbtc-bypass] wrote {out}")
98

101	    main()

1	"""Prodigy P2.6 owner-block UNIT test — the d-MOVEMENT arithmetic the multi-step
2	parity cannot reach.
3	
4	WHY THIS EXISTS. The in-kernel Prodigy d-estimate (P2.6, fused_{vit,decoder}_
5	megakernel_tc) reduces cross-ALL-tensors (r,s), decays the PERSISTED (r_ema,s_ema)
6	by beta3, folds d_coef into the candidate, and updates d = max(d_prev,
7	d_coef·r_ema/|s_ema|). At production d0=1e-6/d_coef=1.0 this owner-block is INERT
8	for BOTH decoder + vit — the slow real trajectory <g,p0−p> never trips the
9	candidate over d0 in <80 steps (eager's d does not move here either). And
10	trajectory-FORCING is unstable (small d0 won't bootstrap; large d0·lr blows the
11	model to NaN). So the multi-step PARITY, while green, does NOT exercise the
12	r_ema/s_ema/d_coef/persist arithmetic: when d is inert, max(d_prev,~0)=d_prev
13	regardless of whether the persist line is right (a kernel that wrongly persisted
14	the d_coef-SCALED r_ema would pass every inert gate). INTEGRATION-OPTSTAGES §8's
15	CPU oracle only covers the INSTANTANEOUS phaseA/phaseB; the beta3-EMA + d_coef +
16	persist is the §2 host-side part reimplemented in-kernel — novel code unseen there.
17	
18	THE TEST. Snapshot the step-2-ENTRY params p_e, then INJECT a controlled anchor
19	param_init = p_e + delta (so p0 − p_e = delta is nonzero + EXACT), reset the
20	persisted scalars to the cold start (r_ema=s_ema=0, d_lr=d0), run ONE more kernel
21	step, and read the kernel's PERSISTED [r_ema | s_ema | d_lr]. Compare to the
22	canonical prodigy.h math in fp64 on the SAME captured TC-reduced grad g_e and the
23	SAME delta and d_prev=d0:
24	    r     = Σ_i d0²·g_e[i]·delta[i]               (prodigy.h:11; degree-2 scale-free)
25	    s     = Σ_i d0²·|g_e[i]|                       (the L1 norm)
26	    r_ema = beta3·0 + r,  s_ema = beta3·0 + s      (persisted scalar EMA, fresh)
27	    d     = max(d0, d_coef·r_ema/|s_ema|)          (prodigy_update_d; d_coef on candidate)
28	d_coef ≠ 1 makes the "persist UNSCALED, scale only the candidate" line LOAD-BEARING;
29	the controlled delta makes d genuinely MOVE off d0, exercising the max() branch.
30	
31	Run: CUDA_MPS_PIPE_DIRECTORY=/nonexistent PYTHONPATH=. python \
32	        tuning/_prodigy_owner_block_unit.py --model vit
33	     (--model decoder validates the sibling lane's SAME owner-block.)
34	"""
35	import argparse
36	import os
37	import sys
38	
39	sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
40	
41	import torch  # noqa: E402
42	
43	TOL = 5e-4   # fp32 reorder over a cross-ALL-tensors d²-scaled reduction
44	
45	
46	def main(model="vit", d_coef=3.0, d0=1e-6, delta_scale=1e-2):
47	    from tests.hw.test_l3tc_tail_gate import _build_cell
48	    from grokking_optimizers.dispatch import (has_l3_real, gemm_impl_for_cell,
49	                                              canonicalize_model, fused_train_step)
50	    canon = canonicalize_model(model)
51	    assert has_l3_real(canon, "prodigy"), f"{model}×prodigy is not L3-REAL"
52	    assert gemm_impl_for_cell(canon, "prodigy", "bf16") == "wgmma", "engine != wgmma"
53	
54	    g, c, m, data, dev = _build_cell(model)
55	    tx, ty = data[0], data[1]
56	    named = [(n, p) for n, p in m.named_parameters() if p.requires_grad]
57	    total = sum(p.numel() for _, p in named)
58	
59	    opt = g.Prodigy(m.parameters(), lr=c.get("prodigy_lr", 1.0),
60	                    weight_decay=c["weight_decay"], betas=(c["beta1"], c["beta2"]),
61	                    d0=d0, d_coef=d_coef)
62	    beta3 = float(c["beta2"]) ** 0.5
63	
64	    # Step 1: populate the cache (seeds param_init=params_0). d inert (r=0).
65	    cache = {}
66	    fused_train_step(canon, "prodigy", m, opt, tx, ty, state_cache=cache, step=1,
67	                     return_grad=True, gemm_impl="wgmma")
68	    state = cache[canon]["state"]
69	    # p_e = the step-2-ENTRY params = the params AFTER step 1 (the cache `flat` now holds
70	    # the updated params; the kernel will re-pack the SAME current params at step-2 entry,
71	    # so p_e == flat here, AND == the live module params m.named_parameters()).
72	    p_e = cache[canon]["flat"].clone()
73	
74	    # INJECT param_init = p_e + delta (controlled, reproducible). Reset persisted
75	    # scalars to the cold start so step 2 is a clean first d-update from d0.
76	    gen = torch.Generator(device=dev).manual_seed(12345)
77	    delta = (torch.rand(total, generator=gen, device=dev) - 0.5) * 2.0 * delta_scale
78	    state[3 * total + 1:4 * total + 1].copy_(p_e + delta)
79	    cache["param_init_seeded"] = True
80	    state[4 * total + 1] = 0.0     # r_ema
81	    state[4 * total + 2] = 0.0     # s_ema
82	    state[4 * total + 3] = d0      # d_lr (persisted d_prev)
83	
84	    # Step 2: the kernel re-packs the CURRENT params (== p_e) into flat, so p0 − p = delta
85	    # EXACTLY for the P2.6 reduction. Capture g_e = the reduced grad the P2.6 used.
86	    _loss2, g_e = fused_train_step(canon, "prodigy", m, opt, tx, ty,
87	                                   state_cache=cache, step=2, return_grad=True,
88	                                   gemm_impl="wgmma")
89	    k_r = float(state[4 * total + 1].item())
90	    k_s = float(state[4 * total + 2].item())
91	    k_d = float(state[4 * total + 3].item())
92	
93	    # CANONICAL reference (fp64) — r/s with d_prev=d0, EMA from a fresh (0,0).
94	    ge = g_e.double()
95	    dl = delta.double()
96	    d0d = float(d0)
97	    r = (d0d * d0d) * float((ge * dl).sum().item())
98	    s = (d0d * d0d) * float(ge.abs().sum().item())
99	    r_ema = beta3 * 0.0 + r
100	    s_ema = beta3 * 0.0 + s
101	    cand = float(d_coef) * r_ema / (abs(s_ema) + 0.0 if s_ema != 0 else 1.0)
102	    d_ref = max(d0d, cand)
103	
104	    def rel(a, b):
105	        return abs(a - b) / (abs(b) + 1e-30)
106	
107	    r_rel = rel(k_r, r_ema)
108	    s_rel = rel(k_s, s_ema)
109	    d_rel = rel(k_d, d_ref)
110	    d_moved = k_d > d0 * (1.0 + 1e-6)
111	
112	    print(f"[prodigy-owner-unit] model={model} d0={d0:.1e} d_coef={d_coef} "
113	          f"delta_scale={delta_scale:.1e}", flush=True)
114	    print(f"  kernel persisted: r_ema={k_r:.6e} s_ema={k_s:.6e} d_lr={k_d:.6e}", flush=True)
115	    print(f"  canonical ref:    r_ema={r_ema:.6e} s_ema={s_ema:.6e} d={d_ref:.6e}", flush=True)
116	    print(f"  rel: r={r_rel:.3e} s={s_rel:.3e} d={d_rel:.3e}  (tol {TOL:.1e})", flush=True)
117	    print(f"  d MOVED off d0 (owner-block branch exercised): {d_moved} "
118	          f"(candidate d_coef·r/|s| = {cand:.6e} vs d0 {d0:.1e})", flush=True)
119	
120	    ok = (r_rel < TOL and s_rel < TOL and d_rel < TOL and d_moved
121	          and k_r == k_r and k_s == k_s and k_d == k_d)   # finite
122	    print(f"  => {'PASS — in-kernel d-update (beta3-EMA + d_coef + persist) matches canonical' if ok else 'FAIL'}",
123	          flush=True)
124	    sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)
125	
126	
127	if __name__ == "__main__":
128	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
129	    ap.add_argument("--model", default="vit", help="vit | decoder")
130	    ap.add_argument("--d-coef", type=float, default=3.0)
131	    ap.add_argument("--d0", type=float, default=1e-6)
132	    ap.add_argument("--delta-scale", type=float, default=1e-2)
133	    a = ap.parse_args()
134	    main(a.model, d_coef=a.d_coef, d0=a.d0, delta_scale=a.delta_scale)

1	"""Multi-step parity for the CONVERTED decoder×grokadamw L3-TC cell.
2	
3	WHY THIS EXISTS (the honest-registration gate): the single-step state-aware
4	tail_gate is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT for grokadamw. It is BLIND to two of
5	the three eager mechanisms at step 1:
6	  * (ii) the GLOBAL grad-norm clip is INERT at step 1 (‖g‖₂≈0.72 < grad_clip=1.0),
7	  * (iii) adaptive-α never fires (no losses are fed to .step()).
8	The codebase explicitly names registering on that green single-step gate a
9	"HOLLOW PASS". This test closes the gap: it runs the REAL TC megakernel and an
10	eager GrokAdamW reference SIDE-BY-SIDE for ~80 steps (long enough that the clip
11	fires — the documented divergence onset is ~step 50), feeding BOTH the kernel's
12	own TC-reduced grad each step (so the optimizer TAIL is isolated across steps),
13	and asserts the kernel's params + [m|v|ema] state track eager to fp32-reorder
14	tolerance the WHOLE way.
15	
16	It also runs a CONTROL: the SAME eager grad set with the clip DISABLED. If the
17	clip-disabled eager diverges from the clip-enabled eager (it does, once the norm
18	exceeds the threshold), that PROVES (ii) is load-bearing — and the kernel
19	matching the clip-ENABLED eager proves the kernel implements it faithfully.
20	
21	Run: CUDA_MPS_PIPE_DIRECTORY=/nonexistent PYTHONPATH=. python \
22	        tuning/_grokadamw_multistep_parity.py
23	"""
24	import os
25	import sys
26	
27	sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
28	
29	import torch  # noqa: E402
30	
31	
32	N_STEPS = 80          # past the ~step-50 clip-onset (the gate-blind regime)
33	# TOL must be TIGHTER than the control signatures or the gate can't fail a dropped
34	# mechanism: the kernel-vs-eager error is ~1e-7 (fp32 reorder), while a static-α
35	# regression shows ~1.3e-3 and a no-clip regression ~2.4e-3. 1e-4 passes the real
36	# kernel with 3 orders of margin and FAILS either dropped mechanism.
37	TOL = 1e-4
38	CTRL_MIN_DIVERGENCE = 1e-3   # each control (clip-OFF / static-α) must diverge ≥ this
39	
40	
41	def _flat(named):
42	    return torch.cat([p.data.reshape(-1) for _, p in named])
43	
44	
45	def _inject_grad(named, flat_grad):
46	    off = 0
47	    for _, p in named:
48	        n = p.numel()
49	        p.grad = flat_grad[off:off + n].reshape(p.shape).clone()
50	        off += n
51	
52	
53	def _gather_state(opt, named, total, dev):
54	    m = torch.zeros(total, device=dev)
55	    v = torch.zeros(total, device=dev)
56	    ema = torch.zeros(total, device=dev)
57	    off = 0
58	    for _, p in named:
59	        n = p.numel()
60	        st = opt.state.get(p, {})
61	        if "exp_avg" in st:
62	            m[off:off + n].copy_(st["exp_avg"].reshape(-1))
63	        if "exp_avg_sq" in st:
64	            v[off:off + n].copy_(st["exp_avg_sq"].reshape(-1))
65	        if "ema" in st:
66	            ema[off:off + n].copy_(st["ema"].reshape(-1))
67	        off += n
68	    return m, v, ema
69	
70	
71	def _rel(a, b):
72	    return (a - b).abs().max().item() / (b.abs().max().item() + 1e-30)
73	
74	
75	def main(model="decoder", grad_clip_override=None):
76	    from tests.hw.test_l3tc_tail_gate import _build_cell, _grokadamw_factory
77	    from grokking_optimizers.dispatch import (has_l3_real, gemm_impl_for_cell,
78	                                              canonicalize_model, fused_train_step)
79	
80	    opt = "grokadamw"
81	    canon = canonicalize_model(model)
82	    assert has_l3_real(canon, opt), f"{model}×grokadamw is not L3-REAL (register it)"
83	    assert gemm_impl_for_cell(canon, opt, "bf16") == "wgmma", "engine != wgmma"
84	
85	    # grad_clip_override (mechanism (ii) FORCED-FIRE for low-grad-norm models): the
86	    # P2.5 global grad-norm clip is INERT for vit at the production grad_clip=1.0
87	    # (vit's grad-norm peaks ~0.85 < 1.0, so the clip never bites — clip_fired=None,
88	    # the control can't demonstrate load-bearing, and the P2.5 code path is exercised
89	    # by NOTHING). To validate the kernel's P2.5 ACTUALLY clips correctly when active
90	    # (a hand-port could read kDecTotalElems or mis-offset the CTA range and pass every
91	    # inert gate), the caller lowers grad_clip BELOW the model's peak grad-norm so the
92	    # clip FIRES — then the clip-ON kernel must still track the clip-ON eager to fp32
93	    # tol AND the clip-OFF control must diverge. This is NOT suppression: lowering a
94	    # threshold to ACTIVATE + verify a mechanism is the no-fake discipline. The
95	    # production grad_clip=1.0 result (clip inert for vit) is reported separately.
96	    def _clip(cc):
97	        if grad_clip_override is not None:
98	            cc = dict(cc); cc["grokadamw_grad_clip"] = float(grad_clip_override)
99	        return cc
100	
101	    g, c0, m_k, data, dev = _build_cell(model)
102	    c = _clip(c0)
103	    tx, ty = data[0], data[1]
104	    named_k = [(n, p) for n, p in m_k.named_parameters() if p.requires_grad]
105	    total = sum(p.numel() for _, p in named_k)
106	
107	    # The eager REFERENCE model — identical init (same seed build) — driven by the
108	    # kernel's reduced grad each step. Two eager optimizers share the reference's
109	    # param trajectory question: we keep ONE reference (clip ON) as the parity
110	    # target, plus a SEPARATE clip-OFF control model to show the clip matters.
111	    g2, c2, m_ref, data2, dev2 = _build_cell(model)
112	    c2 = _clip(c2)
113	    named_ref = [(n, p) for n, p in m_ref.named_parameters() if p.requires_grad]
114	    assert torch.equal(_flat(named_k), _flat(named_ref)), "init mismatch (seed)"
115	    opt_ref = _grokadamw_factory(g2, m_ref.parameters(), c2)   # grad_clip (real or forced)
116	
117	    # Clip-OFF control (proves mechanism (ii)): same init, same fed grads + same
118	    # signal cadence as the reference, but grad_clip disabled. Independent model.
119	    g3, c3, m_ctl, data3, dev3 = _build_cell(model)
120	    named_ctl = [(n, p) for n, p in m_ctl.named_parameters() if p.requires_grad]
121	    c3_off = dict(c3)
122	    c3_off["grokadamw_grad_clip"] = 1e30   # effectively no clip (norm never exceeds)
123	    opt_ctl = _grokadamw_factory(g3, m_ctl.parameters(), c3_off)
124	
125	    # Static-α control (proves mechanism (iii)): same init, same fed grads + clip,
126	    # but the grokking signal is NEVER set → α stays at α_init for all steps. If
127	    # this diverges from the adapted reference once the signal fires, the adaptive-α
128	    # is load-bearing; the kernel matching the ADAPTED reference proves it adapts.
129	    g4, c4, m_sa, data4, dev4 = _build_cell(model)
130	    c4 = _clip(c4)
131	    named_sa = [(n, p) for n, p in m_sa.named_parameters() if p.requires_grad]
132	    opt_sa = _grokadamw_factory(g4, m_sa.parameters(), c4)
133	
134	    # Alpha-update cadence (mirror the race: train_grokadamw alpha_update_freq=50).
135	    ALPHA_FREQ = int(c.get("grokadamw_alpha_update_freq", 50))
136	
137	    cache = {}
138	    worst_param = worst_m = worst_v = worst_ema = 0.0
139	    clip_fired_step = None
140	    clip_ctl_div = 0.0       # clip-OFF vs reference  (proves (ii))
141	    alpha_ctl_div = 0.0      # static-α vs reference  (proves (iii))
142	    alpha_fired_step = None  # first step the adapted α actually differs from α_init
143	
144	    for step in range(1, N_STEPS + 1):
145	        # GROKKING SIGNAL (iii): on the cadence, feed BOTH the kernel-driving opt_ref
146	        # AND the clip-OFF control the SAME (train_loss, val_loss) signal BEFORE the
147	        # kernel reads scalars — so the kernel's α (via _opt_scalars_from →
148	        # opt_ref._alpha_for_group) and the eager reference's α match this step (the
149	        # ordering trap: set the signal pre-launch). The static-α control is NOT fed.
150	        step_kw = {}
151	        if step % ALPHA_FREQ == 0:
152	            # A synthetic but monotone signal: use the kernel's current loss as the
153	            # "train" loss and a slightly larger "val" loss so the gap (and thus the
154	            # α decay) is nonzero — this exercises α_init·exp(-κ·signal) ≠ α_init.
155	            tl = float(loss_prev) if step > 1 else 4.7
156	            vl = tl + 0.5
157	            for o in (opt_ref, opt_ctl):
158	                o._grok_signal = o._grokking_signal(tl, vl)
159	                o._signal_active = True
160	            step_kw = dict(train_loss=tl, val_loss=vl)
161	            a_now = opt_ref._alpha_for_group(opt_ref.param_groups[0])
162	            if alpha_fired_step is None and abs(a_now - opt_ref.param_groups[0]["alpha"]) > 1e-9:
163	                alpha_fired_step = step
164	
165	        # (1) ONE real TC megakernel step (real fwd+bwd+grokadamw tail), wgmma. The
166	        #     kernel reads α via _opt_scalars_from(opt_ref) — the LIVE adapted α.
167	        loss, grad = fused_train_step(canon, opt, m_k, opt_ref, tx, ty,
168	                                      state_cache=cache, step=step,
169	                                      return_grad=True, gemm_impl="wgmma")
170	        loss_prev = loss
171	        gnorm = grad.norm().item()
172	        clip_thr = float(c.get("grokadamw_grad_clip", 1.0))
173	        if clip_fired_step is None and gnorm > clip_thr:
174	            clip_fired_step = step
175	
176	        # (2) eager reference (clip ON, α adapts) fed the SAME reduced grad + signal.
177	        _inject_grad(named_ref, grad)
178	        opt_ref.step(**step_kw)
179	
180	        # (3) clip-OFF control (α adapts identically; ONLY the clip differs).
181	        _inject_grad(named_ctl, grad)
182	        opt_ctl.step(**step_kw)
183	
184	        # (4) static-α control (clip ON; α NEVER adapts — no signal fed).
185	        _inject_grad(named_sa, grad)
186	        opt_sa.step()
187	
188	        # (5) compare kernel params/state vs the clip-ON + α-adapting reference.
189	        p_k = _flat(named_k)
190	        p_ref = _flat(named_ref)
191	        worst_param = max(worst_param, _rel(p_k, p_ref))
192	
193	        kstate = cache[canon]["state"]
194	        k_m = kstate[0:total]
195	        k_v = kstate[total:2 * total]
196	        k_ema = kstate[2 * total:3 * total]
197	        r_m, r_v, r_ema = _gather_state(opt_ref, named_ref, total, dev)
198	        worst_m = max(worst_m, _rel(k_m, r_m))

214	    print(f"  kernel-vs-eager(clip ON, α-adapt):  param={worst_param:.3e} "

279	def _verify_race_alpha_path(model="decoder"):
280	    """Drive the REAL train_grokadamw through the race entry for > alpha_freq steps;
281	    confirm wgmma every step and that the live α_t handed to the kernel adapted."""
282	    import wiring_check as wc
283	    import grokking_optimizers.dispatch as dispatch
284	    g = wc._g()
285	    ALPHA_FREQ = 10            # small so the cadence fires within the run
286	    STEPS = ALPHA_FREQ + 12    # run past one cadence step
287	
288	    # Instrument _opt_scalars_from to record the α passed to the kernel per call.
289	    seen_alpha = []
290	    _orig = dispatch._opt_scalars_from
291	
292	    def _spy(optimizer, step):
293	        out = _orig(optimizer, step)
294	        # only GrokAdamW carries both alpha+lamb+_alpha_for_group
295	        if hasattr(optimizer, "_alpha_for_group") and "alpha" in out:
296	            seen_alpha.append((step, float(out["alpha"])))
297	        return out
298	    dispatch._opt_scalars_from = _spy
299	    # The race fn imports _opt_scalars_from indirectly via fused_train_step (same
300	    # module object), so patching the module attribute is sufficient.
301	
302	    seen_engines = []
303	    _orig_l3 = g._try_fused_train_step
304	
305	    def _wrap_l3(*a, **k):
306	        r = _orig_l3(*a, **k)
307	        if r is not None and g.LAST_L3_ENGINE:
308	            seen_engines.append(g.LAST_L3_ENGINE["engine"])
309	        return r
310	    g._try_fused_train_step = _wrap_l3
311	
312	    err = None
313	    try:
314	        import torch
315	        data, init = wc._data_init(model)
316	        c = wc._cfg("grokadamw", model, STEPS)
317	        c["grokadamw_alpha_update_freq"] = ALPHA_FREQ
318	        c["eval_every"] = 10 ** 9
319	        torch.manual_seed(42)
320	        g.train_grokadamw(c, init, *data, torch.device("cuda"), bp=0)
321	        torch.cuda.synchronize()
322	    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
323	        import traceback
324	        traceback.print_exc()
325	        err = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"
326	    finally:
327	        dispatch._opt_scalars_from = _orig
328	        g._try_fused_train_step = _orig_l3
329	
330	    all_wgmma = len(seen_engines) >= STEPS - 1 and all(e == "wgmma" for e in seen_engines)
331	    alphas = [a for _, a in seen_alpha]
332	    alpha_init = alphas[0] if alphas else None
333	    # α must adapt off α_init at some step (the cadence step sets the signal).
334	    adapted = alpha_init is not None and any(abs(a - alpha_init) > 1e-9 for a in alphas)
335	    adapt_step = next((s for s, a in seen_alpha if abs(a - alpha_init) > 1e-9), None) \
336	        if alpha_init is not None else None
337	
338	    print("\n[grokadamw-race-path] (iii) production α-cadence verification:", flush=True)
339	    print(f"  race steps fused as wgmma: {len(seen_engines)} "
340	          f"(engines: {sorted(set(seen_engines))})", flush=True)
341	    print(f"  α handed to kernel: init={alpha_init} "
342	          f"adapted={adapted} (first off-init at step {adapt_step})", flush=True)
343	    if err:
344	        print(f"  RACE-PATH ERROR: {err}", flush=True)
345	    race_ok = (err is None and all_wgmma and adapted)
346	    print(f"  RACE-PATH (train_grokadamw → wgmma + α adapts): "
347	          f"{'PASS' if race_ok else 'FAIL'}", flush=True)
348	    return race_ok

1	"""Multi-step parity for the CONVERTED decoder×prodigy L3-TC cell.
2	
3	WHY THIS EXISTS (the honest-registration gate): the single-step state-aware
4	tail_gate is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT for prodigy. At step 1 the trajectory
5	anchor param_init == params, so r = Σ d²·<g, p0−p> = 0 ⇒ the d-estimate stays at
6	d0=1e-6 (matching eager _d_lr=d0) and the apply is a plain d0-scaled Adam step.
7	The DEFINING prodigy mechanism — the adaptive learning rate d that grows from the
8	cumulative parameter trajectory — does NOT fire until step≥2. So the single-step
9	gate is BLIND to it, exactly as grokadamw's single-step gate is blind to the clip.
10	
11	This test closes the gap: it runs the REAL TC megakernel and an eager Prodigy
12	reference SIDE-BY-SIDE for ~80 steps, feeding BOTH the kernel's own TC-reduced
13	grad each step (so the optimizer TAIL is isolated across steps), and asserts the
14	kernel's params + [m|v|s_track] state AND the adaptive d track eager to fp32-
15	reorder tolerance the WHOLE way. The kernel's d lives in the persisted state slot
16	(state[4*total+3]); we read it back and compare to eager opt._d_lr each step.
17	
18	CONTROL (proves the d-adaptation is load-bearing): the SAME eager grad set with
19	d_coef=0, which FREEZES d at d0 (the candidate d_coef·r/|s| = 0, so
20	max(d_prev,0)=d_prev=d0 forever). If the d-frozen eager diverges from the
21	d-adapting eager (it does, once the trajectory accumulates), that PROVES the
22	in-kernel d-estimate is load-bearing — and the kernel matching the d-ADAPTING
23	eager proves the kernel implements the estimator faithfully (not a frozen-d stub).
24	
25	Run: CUDA_MPS_PIPE_DIRECTORY=/nonexistent PYTHONPATH=. python \
26	        tuning/_prodigy_multistep_parity.py
27	"""
28	import os
29	import sys

31	sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))

36	N_STEPS = 80          # long enough that d adapts well off d0
37	# TOL must be TIGHTER than the control divergence or the gate can't fail a frozen-d
38	# kernel: the kernel-vs-eager error is fp32-reorder (~1e-6), while the d-frozen
39	# control diverges by orders of magnitude once d grows. 1e-4 passes the real kernel
40	# with margin and FAILS a dropped d-adaptation.
41	TOL = 1e-4
42	CTRL_MIN_DIVERGENCE = 1e-3   # the d-frozen control must diverge ≥ this

45	def _flat(named):
46	    return torch.cat([p.data.reshape(-1) for _, p in named])
47	
48	
49	def _inject_grad(named, flat_grad):
50	    off = 0
51	    for _, p in named:
52	        n = p.numel()
53	        p.grad = flat_grad[off:off + n].reshape(p.shape).clone()
54	        off += n

57	def _gather_state(opt, named, total, dev):
58	    """Gather eager Prodigy state: exp_avg, exp_avg_sq, s (the trajectory accum)."""
59	    m = torch.zeros(total, device=dev)
60	    v = torch.zeros(total, device=dev)
61	    s = torch.zeros(total, device=dev)
62	    off = 0
63	    for _, p in named:
64	        n = p.numel()
65	        st = opt.state.get(p, {})
66	        if "exp_avg" in st:
67	            m[off:off + n].copy_(st["exp_avg"].reshape(-1))
68	        if "exp_avg_sq" in st:
69	            v[off:off + n].copy_(st["exp_avg_sq"].reshape(-1))
70	        if "s" in st:
71	            s[off:off + n].copy_(st["s"].reshape(-1))
72	        off += n
73	    return m, v, s

76	def _rel(a, b):
77	    return (a - b).abs().max().item() / (b.abs().max().item() + 1e-30)

81	    from tests.hw.test_l3tc_tail_gate import _build_cell, _prodigy_factory

85	    opt = "prodigy"

90	    # d_coef/d0 FORCED-FIRE (d-adaptation validation for inert-at-production models):

92	    # d0=1e-6/d_coef=1.0 (the signed trajectory <g,p0−p> stays small, so the candidate
93	    # d_coef·r/|s| never exceeds d0 in 80 steps — d_grew=None, the control can't show
94	    # load-bearing, and the P2.6 d-update code is exercised by NOTHING). To validate

103	    def _mk_prodigy(gg, params, cc, d_coef=None):
104	        kw = dict(lr=cc.get("prodigy_lr", 1.0), weight_decay=cc["weight_decay"],
105	                  betas=(cc["beta1"], cc["beta2"]))
106	        if d_coef is not None:

108	        elif d_coef_override is not None:

115	    tx, ty = data[0], data[1]

117	    total = sum(p.numel() for _, p in named_k)

52	        with open(path, "r", errors="ignore") as fh:
53	            return "PYBIND11_MODULE(TORCH_EXTENSION_NAME" in fh.read()

59	    pats = ["csrc/backends/cuda/sm_90/*.cu",

113	def _build_vanilla(fast_math: bool):
114	    sources = _resolve_sources()
115	    # Pin the arch so torch's BuildExtension does NOT auto-detect and inject its
116	    # own `-gencode arch=compute_90,code=compute_90` (the non-`a` PTX target),
117	    # which makes ptxas reject the megakernel's wgmma.* PTX ("not supported on
118	    # .target 'sm_90'"). 9.0a => torch emits sm_90a/compute_90a only, matching
119	    # _GENCODE above and the production/bench builds. (setdefault is not enough —
120	    # an inherited value would leak the default; set it explicitly.)
121	    os.environ["TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST"] = "9.0a"
122	    sys.stderr.write(f"[nvcc-baseline] {len(sources)} TUs, fast_math={fast_math}, "
123	                     f"TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=9.0a\n")
124	    sys.stderr.write("[nvcc-baseline] nvcc flags: "
125	                     + " ".join(_vanilla_nvcc(fast_math)) + "\n")
126	    # name="_ops" so PYBIND11_MODULE(TORCH_EXTENSION_NAME) emits PyInit__ops,
127	    # matching what grokking_optimizers._ops expects.
128	    mod = _cpp_load(
129	        name="_ops",
130	        sources=sources,
131	        extra_cflags=_vanilla_cxx(fast_math),
132	        extra_cuda_cflags=_vanilla_nvcc(fast_math),
133	        extra_include_paths=[os.path.join(ROOT, p) for p in _INCLUDES],
134	        build_directory=_ensure_build_dir(fast_math),
135	        verbose=True,
136	    )
137	    return mod

150	def _alias_as_ops(built_module) -> None:
151	    # The cpp_extension.load() return value is already the imported module
152	    # object; evict any stale grokking_optimizers._ops (+ submodules + dispatch
153	    # + optimizers that memoize the resolved ops) so the production dispatch
154	    # binds THIS binary, then alias it.
155	    for k in [k for k in list(sys.modules)
156	              if k == "grokking_optimizers._ops"
157	              or k.startswith("grokking_optimizers._ops.")
158	              or k == "grokking_optimizers.dispatch"]:
159	        del sys.modules[k]

166	def _time_cell(model: str, opt: str, seed: int, warmup: int, iters: int,
167	               reps: int) -> dict:
168	    os.environ["GATE_SEED"] = str(seed)
169	    import tests.hw.test_l3tc_tail_gate as G
170	    from grokking_optimizers.dispatch import fused_train_step  # noqa: F401
171	    g, c, m, data, dev = G._build_cell(model)
172	    tx, ty = data[0], data[1]
173	    spec = G._CELLS[f"{opt}/{model}"]
174	    opt_obj = spec["factory"](g, m.parameters(), c)
175	
176	    def _step():
177	        fused_train_step(m, opt_obj, tx, ty)
178	
179	    for _ in range(warmup):
180	        _step()
181	    torch.cuda.synchronize()
182	    medians = []
183	    for _ in range(reps):
184	        start = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
185	        end = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
186	        start.record()
187	        for _ in range(iters):
188	            _step()
189	        end.record()
190	        torch.cuda.synchronize()
191	        medians.append(start.elapsed_time(end) / iters)
192	    return {"model": model, "opt": opt, "seed": seed,
193	            "median_ms": statistics.median(medians),
194	            "min_ms": min(medians),
195	            "walls_ms": [round(x, 4) for x in medians]}

202	# config the production cell + fp64 gate run at). "See the real difference"

205	# (csrc/fused/sm_90/mega_decoder_real_adamw_tc.cu, -DSG_DEC_BENCH_LAYOUT=1 →
206	# the _DEC_BENCH_D=2048 layout branch) compiles at d=2048. So the d=2048 leg
207	# builds THAT single TU three ways and times its tc_train_step (the SAME path
208	# tuning/decoder_bench.py uses), differing ONLY in (1) the nvcc flag set and
209	# (2) the dW split-K macro:
210	#
211	#   A  regular nvcc        : VANILLA flags (-O3 [+--use_fast_math] -arch=sm_90a
212	#                            + only the structural -D needed to compile), NO
213	#                            compile.py ptxas tuning;            split-K = 4.
214	#   B  compile.py default  : compile.py's AUGMENTED flags (NVCC_DEVICE_BASE +
215	#                            the CUDA-version-gated ptxas tuning ladder +
216	#                            grokking's --use_fast_math -DNDEBUG, exactly the
217	#                            setup.py production line);          split-K = 4.
218	#   C  compile.py tuned    : same augmented flags + the TUNED knob (the
219	#                            in-source default);                 split-K = 2.

222	# B→C isolates the autotuner's knob benefit; A→C is the total. fast-math is
223	# held IDENTICAL across A/B/C (production B uses it — see setup.py:643), so

232	    "-DSG_DEC_SCALAR_MEGAKERNEL=0",  # gate off the legacy scalar megakernel
233	                                     # (its smem grows with d and ptxas

242	    """Variant A — what a competent dev would hand-write: -O3 [+--use_fast_math]
243	    -arch=sm_90a + the structural defines. Explicitly NONE of compile.py's
244	    ptxas micro-tuning (no --register-usage-level / --def-load-cache /
245	    --def-store-cache / --extra-device-vectorization / -Xfatbin -compress-all /

253	def _augmented_bench_nvcc() -> list:
254	    """Variants B/C — the EXACT production compile.py flag line for this single
255	    TU on this toolchain: NVCC_DEVICE_BASE + the CUDA-version-gated ptxas
256	    tuning ladder (probed live) + grokking's project flags (--use_fast_math
257	    -DNDEBUG -lineinfo), exactly as setup.py composes it. fast-math ON to match
258	    A (and production)."""
259	    from grokking_optimizers.compile import (NVCC_DEVICE_BASE,
260	                                             _newer_compiler_flags)
261	    base = list(NVCC_DEVICE_BASE)
262	    # The CUDA-version-gated additions (register-usage-level=10 on 12.3+,
263	    # def-load-cache=ca, def-store-cache=wb, --threads, --diag-suppress, …) —
264	    # the SAME ladder the production/autotuner device compile uses.
265	    # _newer_compiler_flags returns (extra_host, extra_device); take device.
266	    try:
267	        _host, gated = _newer_compiler_flags("sm_90")
268	    except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover - never block the comparison
269	        sys.stderr.write(f"[nvcc-baseline] WARN: _newer_compiler_flags failed "
270	                         f"({exc}); proceeding with NVCC_DEVICE_BASE only\n")
271	        gated = []
272	    # grokking project flags (setup.py:643) + bench structural + gencode.
273	    return (base + list(gated) + ["--use_fast_math", "-DNDEBUG", "-lineinfo"]
274	            + _BENCH_GENCODE + _BENCH_STRUCTURAL)

302	def _time_bench_seed(DB, mod, d: int, batch: int, seed: int,
303	                     reps: int, warmup: int, iters: int):
304	    """Median step-ms for ONE seed: inputs reseeded per-seed (params/tokens from
305	    a per-seed generator — the genuine 3-seed coverage, vs decoder_bench.measure
306	    which hardcodes seed 42). Shapes/work are identical across seeds, so this is
307	    the protocol's timing-variance probe at the d=2048 roofline (correctness +
308	    determinism are the SEPARATE fp64 gate). Mirrors roofline_bench.time_seed."""
309	    import time as _t
310	    dev = torch.device("cuda")
311	    total = int(mod.TOTAL)
312	    vocab, seq = int(mod.VOCAB), int(mod.SEQ)
313	    g = torch.Generator(device=dev).manual_seed(seed)
314	    params = (torch.randn(total, generator=g, device=dev) * 0.02).contiguous()
315	    tokens = torch.randint(0, vocab, (batch, seq), generator=g,
316	                           device=dev).to(torch.int32).contiguous()
317	    targets = torch.randint(0, vocab, (batch,), generator=g,
318	                            device=dev).to(torch.int32).contiguous()
319	    state = torch.zeros(3 * total, dtype=torch.float32, device=dev)
320	    lr, beta1, beta2, eps, wd = 1e-3, 0.9, 0.98, 1e-8, 0.0
321	    bc1, bc2 = 1.0 - beta1, 1.0 - beta2
322	
323	    def call():
324	        return mod.tc_train_step(params, tokens, targets, state, lr, beta1,
325	                                 beta2, eps, wd, bc1, bc2, 1, 0)
326	
327	    for _ in range(warmup):
328	        call()
329	    torch.cuda.synchronize()
330	    walls = []
331	    for _ in range(reps):
332	        torch.cuda.synchronize()
333	        t0 = _t.perf_counter()
334	        for _ in range(iters):
335	            call()
336	        torch.cuda.synchronize()
337	        walls.append((_t.perf_counter() - t0) / iters * 1e3)
338	    return statistics.median(walls), [round(w, 4) for w in walls]

341	def _run_d2048_3point(args) -> int:
342	    """A/B/C build + 3-seed median step-ms + TF/s + deltas at d=2048."""
343	    import tuning.decoder_bench as DB
344	    import time as _time
345	    fast_math = not args.strict_math
346	    d, batch = 2048, args.batch
347	    assert batch % 16 == 0, "B must be divisible by 16"
348	
349	    variants = [
350	        ("A", "regular-nvcc (vanilla flags, split-K=4)",
351	         _vanilla_bench_nvcc(fast_math), 4),
352	        ("B", "compile.py-default (augmented flags, split-K=4)",
353	         _augmented_bench_nvcc(), 4),
354	        ("C", "compile.py-tuned (augmented flags, split-K=2)",
355	         _augmented_bench_nvcc(), 2),
356	    ]
357	    seeds = [int(s) for s in args.seeds.split(",") if s.strip()]
358	    results = {}
359	    for label, desc, nvcc_flags, splitk in variants:
360	        sys.stderr.write(f"\n[nvcc-baseline] ===== variant {label}: {desc} =====\n")
361	        t0 = _time.perf_counter()
362	        mod = _build_bench_variant(label, nvcc_flags, splitk, fast_math,
363	                                   args.verbose_build)
364	        build_s = _time.perf_counter() - t0
365	        assert int(mod.D) == d, f"variant {label} compiled D={int(mod.D)} != {d}"
366	        flops = DB._decoder_gemm_flops_per_step(
367	            d, batch, int(mod.LAYERS), int(mod.SEQ), int(mod.VOCAB))
368	        per_seed, per_seed_walls = {}, {}
369	        for s in seeds:
370	            med_s, walls = _time_bench_seed(DB, mod, d, batch, s, args.reps,
371	                                            args.warmup, args.iters)
372	            per_seed[s] = med_s
373	            per_seed_walls[s] = walls
374	        med = statistics.median(per_seed.values())
375	        tf_s = flops / (med / 1e3) / 1e12
376	        rec = {"variant": label, "desc": desc, "split_k": splitk,
377	               "fast_math": fast_math, "d": d, "B": batch,
378	               "total_params": int(mod.TOTAL), "build_s": round(build_s, 1),
379	               "per_seed_median_ms": {s: round(per_seed[s], 4) for s in seeds},
380	               "per_seed_walls_ms": per_seed_walls,
381	               "across_seed_median_ms": round(med, 4),
382	               "achieved_tf_s": round(tf_s, 3),
383	               "pct_roofline": round(100.0 * tf_s / 989.0, 3)}
384	        results[label] = rec
385	        sys.stdout.write("VARIANT " + json.dumps(rec) + "\n")
386	        sys.stdout.flush()
387	
388	    # Deltas (negative = faster). A→B = pipeline/flags; B→C = autotuner; A→C = total.
389	    a, b, c = (results[k]["across_seed_median_ms"] for k in "ABC")
390	    deltas = {
391	        "A_to_B_pipeline_flags_pct": round(100.0 * (b - a) / a, 3),
392	        "B_to_C_autotuner_pct": round(100.0 * (c - b) / b, 3),
393	        "A_to_C_total_pct": round(100.0 * (c - a) / a, 3),
394	    }
395	    sys.stdout.write("DELTAS " + json.dumps(deltas) + "\n")
396	    sys.stdout.flush()
397	    return 0

13	
14	1b. RE-INLINE detection (Phase 5 WS3): #include alone is not enough — a consumer
15	   could keep the #include yet still LOCALLY RE-INLINE the Adam moment-update /
16	   bias-corrected apply instead of CALLING the canonical step. That silently
17	   re-introduces drift while passing the structural check. So each includable
18	   CUDA consumer (kernels/sm_90/<opt>_sm90.cuh and the fused
19	   csrc/fused/sm_90/opt_components.cuh) is scanned for the Adam moment-update +
20	   apply expressions (`beta1 * exp_avg…`, `beta2 * exp_avg_sq…`, the
21	   `(m / bc1) / (sqrtf(v / bc2) + eps)` apply). Any match in a consumer FAILS —
22	   the math must come from a call into csrc/algorithms/<opt>.h, not be re-typed
23	   in the .cuh. The canonical algorithms/*.h headers themselves are NOT scanned
24	   (they are the single source and MUST contain the math); the gfx942/TPU
25	   re-expressions are the sanctioned transcriptions guarded by check (2).
26	
27	2. CONTENT-HASH manifest (drift detection for the necessary RE-EXPRESSIONS that
28	   cannot #include the C header — gfx942 transcription, TPU JAX): a committed
29	   manifest scripts/optimizer_math_manifest.json records the normalized hash of
30	   each canonical csrc/algorithms/<opt>.h. This guard recomputes the hashes and
31	   FAILS if any differs from the manifest. So editing the canonical math forces
32	   a DELIBERATE `--update-manifest` (which is the acknowledgement "I changed the
33	   canonical math and synced the gfx942/TPU re-expressions") — silent drift is
34	   impossible.
35	
36	Modes:
37	  python3 scripts/check_math_single_source.py                 # verify (exit 0/1)
38	  python3 scripts/check_math_single_source.py --update-manifest  # re-record hashes
39	The compile.py --self-test section `math_drift_guard` runs the verify path AND a
40	prove-it-triggers test (perturb canonical math in-memory → guard must flag).
41	"""

93	def _strip_comments_ws(src: str) -> str:
94	    """Normalize C/C++ source to its semantic content: drop // and /* */
95	    comments and all whitespace, so reformatting/comment edits do NOT trip the
96	    hash but any change to the actual math expressions does."""
97	    src = re.sub(r"/\*.*?\*/", "", src, flags=re.DOTALL)
98	    src = re.sub(r"//[^\n]*", "", src)
99	    src = re.sub(r"\s+", "", src)
100	    return src

103	def _extract_function_body(src: str, fn_name: str) -> str:
104	    """Return the full text of `fn_name`'s definition (signature .. matching `}`).
105	
106	    Finds the DEFINITION line — a return type (`void`, `std::tuple<...>`, or
107	    `std::vector<...>`) at the start of a line followed by `fn_name(` — so a
108	    pybind `m.def("fn_name", &sg::fn_name)` registration or a forward call site
109	    is NOT mistaken for the body. Then walks from the first `{` after the
110	    signature, brace-matching (skipping braces inside // and /* */ comments and
111	    "…"/'…' literals) to the matching close. Returns "" if not found.
112	    """
113	    sig = re.compile(
114	        r"(?:^|\n)[ \t]*(?:void|std::tuple<[^>]*>|std::vector<[^>]*>)[ \t]+"
115	        + re.escape(fn_name) + r"[ \t]*\(")
116	    m = sig.search(src)
117	    if not m:
118	        return ""
119	    start = m.start() if src[m.start()] != "\n" else m.start() + 1
120	    # Find the opening brace of the body (the first '{' after the ')' that
121	    # closes the parameter list — but simply scanning for the first top-level
122	    # '{' from the signature start is sufficient here because the parameter
123	    # list contains no '{').
124	    i = m.end()
125	    n = len(src)
126	    while i < n and src[i] != "{":
127	        i += 1
128	    if i >= n:
129	        return ""
130	    depth = 0
131	    j = i
132	    in_line_comment = False
133	    in_block_comment = False
134	    in_str = None  # '"' or "'" while inside a literal
135	    while j < n:
136	        c = src[j]
137	        nxt = src[j + 1] if j + 1 < n else ""
138	        if in_line_comment:
139	            if c == "\n":
140	                in_line_comment = False
141	        elif in_block_comment:
142	            if c == "*" and nxt == "/":
143	                in_block_comment = False
144	                j += 1
145	        elif in_str is not None:
146	            if c == "\\":
147	                j += 1  # skip escaped char
148	            elif c == in_str:
149	                in_str = None
150	        elif c == "/" and nxt == "/":
151	            in_line_comment = True
152	            j += 1
153	        elif c == "/" and nxt == "*":
154	            in_block_comment = True
155	            j += 1
156	        elif c == '"' or c == "'":
157	            in_str = c
158	        elif c == "{":
159	            depth += 1
160	        elif c == "}":
161	            depth -= 1
162	            if depth == 0:
163	                return src[start:j + 1]
164	        j += 1
165	    return ""  # unbalanced — treated as "not found"
166

168	def _binding_region_hash(fn_name: str) -> str:
169	    """SHA-256 of the comment/whitespace-stripped binding-function body. Empty
170	    string hashes to a sentinel so a vanished function is DETECTED as drift
171	    (not silently skipped)."""
172	    body = _extract_function_body(_read(BINDINGS_CPP), fn_name)
173	    return hashlib.sha256(_strip_comments_ws(body).encode()).hexdigest()

180	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
181	# Phase 5 WS3 — re-inline detection.
182	#
183	# The Adam moment-update + bias-corrected decoupled-WD apply is the math that
184	# MUST live once in csrc/algorithms/<opt>.h and reach every includable CUDA
185	# consumer via a CALL (e.g. adamw_step / <opt>_adam_tail), never by being
186	# re-typed locally. These regexes match the *moment-update / apply* expressions
187	# specifically (not merely the names `beta1`/`exp_avg`, which legitimately
188	# appear as function arguments passed INTO the canonical call).
189	#
190	# Patterns (whitespace-flexible):
191	#   beta1 * exp_avg[...]        -> m  = b1*ea + (1-b1)*g   first moment update
192	#   beta2 * exp_avg_sq[...]     -> v  = b2*eas + (1-b2)*g*g second moment update
193	#   beta1 * ea... / beta2 * eas -> the quantized-state variant (ea_val/eas_val)
194	#   (... / bc1) / (sqrtf(... / bc2) ... ) -> the bias-corrected apply
195	_REINLINE_PATTERNS = [
196	    re.compile(r"beta1\s*\*\s*exp_avg\b"),
197	    re.compile(r"beta2\s*\*\s*exp_avg_sq\b"),
198	    re.compile(r"beta1\s*\*\s*ea(?:_val)?\b"),
199	    re.compile(r"beta2\s*\*\s*eas(?:_val)?\b"),
200	    re.compile(r"/\s*bc1\s*\)\s*/\s*\(\s*sqrtf\s*\(.*?/\s*bc2"),
201	]
