203	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
204	# SG11 cosine-GATE re-inline detection (drift guard for the cos(grad,momentum)
205	# signal).
206	#
207	# The SG11 gate's cosine reduction — num+=g·m; den_g+=g·g; den_m+=m·m — is the
208	# canonical Sweep A (algorithms/supergrok11.h::sg11_sweep_a_step). The L3-TC staged
209	# precompute (csrc/fused/sm_90/opt_stages_precompute.cuh) MUST obtain it by CALLING
210	# sg11_sweep_a_step, never by re-inlining the per-element accumulation in its own
211	# loop. A re-inlined reduction is EXACTLY how the historical cos(grad,mu) bug crept
212	# in (the loop hard-coded `den_m += u*u` with u=mu, no momentum operand). So we scan
213	# the precompute consumer for a loop-body `den_m += <x>*<x>` / `den_g += <x>*<x>`
214	# accumulation; any match FAILS — the cosine math must come from the canonical call.
215	# (The local `float num=0, den_g=0, den_m=0;` declarations + the three
216	# block_reduce_sum_f32(...) finalizers are NOT accumulations and do not match.)
217	_COSINE_REINLINE_PATTERNS = [
218	    re.compile(r"\bden_m\s*\+=\s*[\w.\[\]]+\s*\*"),
219	    re.compile(r"\bden_g\s*\+=\s*[\w.\[\]]+\s*\*"),
220	]
221	
222	
223	def _cosine_consumer_headers() -> list:
224	    """Headers that compute the SG11 cosine gate and MUST route the reduction
225	    through the canonical sg11_sweep_a_step (never re-inline it)."""
226	    return ["csrc/fused/sm_90/opt_stages_precompute.cuh"]

229	def scan_reinlined_cosine(path: str) -> list:
230	    """Return list of (lineno, pattern, line) for a re-inlined SG11 cosine-gate
231	    reduction in `path` (comments stripped first, so the doc lines that DESCRIBE
232	    the canonical `den_m += m·m` are ignored)."""
233	    body = _read(path)
234	    if not body:
235	        return []
236	    hits = []
237	    for lineno, raw in enumerate(body.splitlines(), 1):
238	        code = re.sub(r"//.*$", "", raw)
239	        for pat in _COSINE_REINLINE_PATTERNS:
240	            if pat.search(code):
241	                hits.append((lineno, pat.pattern, raw.strip()))
242	                break
243	    return hits

371	def check(structural_only: bool = False) -> list:
372	    """Return a list of failure strings (empty = OK)."""
373	    failures = []
374	
375	    # (1) [Task #10] The eager per-op kernels/sm_90/<opt>_sm90.cuh consumers were
376	    # REMOVED (production is now a pure L3-TC megakernel, or hard-fail). Single-
377	    # source is enforced instead by (1a) the fused-consumer structural check
378	    # (opt_components.cuh #includes AND calls every canonical apply symbol), (1b)
379	    # the re-inline scan, and the canonical-math manifest hashes below — not by
380	    # per-op header inclusion. The old per-op loop is therefore intentionally gone.
381	    # (1a) fused-consumer structural hardening (WS-F5): the single fused
382	    # optimizer-tail consumer MUST #include every consumed optimizer's canonical
383	    # header AND call its apply symbol. FAIL LOUDLY if the consumer is
384	    # missing/empty (the old `if fused and …` silently disabled the whole check).
385	    fused = _read(FUSED_CONSUMER)
386	    # Comment-stripped view of the consumer for the apply-SYMBOL assertion: a
387	    # symbol name that appears ONLY inside a // or /* */ comment (e.g.
388	    # `grokadamw_step` is named in a doc comment, but the real call is
389	    # grokadamw_adam_tail) must NOT satisfy the "calls its apply symbol" check —
390	    # otherwise a dead include could be masked by a comment that merely mentions
391	    # the symbol. The #include check below still scans the raw text (an #include
392	    # is never inside a comment when active). _strip_comments_ws also drops
393	    # whitespace, which is fine: we only do substring containment on tokens.
394	    fused_code = _strip_comments_ws(fused) if fused else ""
395	    if not fused:
396	        failures.append(
397	            f"[structural] fused consumer {FUSED_CONSUMER} is missing/empty — "
398	            f"the fused optimizer-tail single-source check is disabled. Restore "
399	            f"the file.")
400	    else:
401	        for opt in OPTS:
402	            if opt == SG2_SEPARATE_PATH:
403	                # Architectural exception (separate launch path) — WARN, do not
404	                # FAIL. TODO(post-refactor): fold SG2 into this assertion once
405	                # opt_components.cuh consumes its tail.
406	                if _canonical_header(opt) not in fused:
407	                    _emit_warning(
408	                        f"{FUSED_CONSUMER} does not #include "
409	                        f"{_canonical_header(opt)} — EXPECTED: SuperGrok2's "
410	                        f"fused tail uses the separate launch_csa_hca path, not "
411	                        f"opt_components.cuh. (SG2 single-source is still "
412	                        f"covered by the per-op kernel + canonical-math + "
413	                        f"binding-region hashes.) TODO: unify post-refactor.")
414	                continue
415	            if _canonical_header(opt) not in fused:
416	                failures.append(
417	                    f"[structural] {FUSED_CONSUMER} does NOT #include the "
418	                    f"canonical {_canonical_header(opt)} (the fused tail would "
419	                    f"reimplement '{opt}' → drift). Add the #include.")
420	            # Apply-symbol assertion: include without a call is a dead include.
421	            # HARD FAIL (#19b): the in-flight opt_components.cuh refactor has
422	            # LANDED — apply_optimizer<Opt> now makes a real, distinct
423	            # algo::<sym> call for every one of the 10 non-SG2 optimizers, and
424	            # _FUSED_APPLY_SYMBOL was re-pointed to match current reality
425	            # (notably grokadamw -> grokadamw_adam_tail). So a missing call is a
426	            # genuine dead include — the fused tail silently routing '{opt}'
427	            # through a different path while the #include sits there unused — and
428	            # must break the build, not merely warn. The match is against the
429	            # COMMENT-STRIPPED consumer (fused_code) so a symbol named only in a
430	            # comment cannot satisfy this (a true-positive gate, not a textual
431	            # coincidence). The SG2 exemption above stays a WARN (separate
432	            # launch_csa_hca path).
433	            sym = _FUSED_APPLY_SYMBOL.get(opt)
434	            if sym and sym not in fused_code:
435	                failures.append(
436	                    f"[structural] {FUSED_CONSUMER} #includes "
437	                    f"{_canonical_header(opt)} but does NOT CALL its apply "
438	                    f"symbol `{sym}` (a dead include — the fused tail routes "
439	                    f"'{opt}' through a different/renamed path while the include "
440	                    f"sits unused → the single-source invariant is not actually "
441	                    f"enforced for '{opt}'). Restore the call or re-point "
442	                    f"_FUSED_APPLY_SYMBOL to the symbol the tail now calls.")
443	
444	    # (1b) re-inline detection: a consumer must CALL the canonical step, never
445	    # re-type the Adam moment-update / apply locally.
446	    for path in _consumer_headers():
447	        for lineno, pat, line in scan_reinlined_math(path):
448	            failures.append(
449	                f"[re-inline] {path}:{lineno} re-inlines canonical Adam math "
450	                f"(matched /{pat}/): `{line}`. This expression MUST come from a "
451	                f"call into csrc/algorithms/<opt>.h (e.g. <opt>_step / "
452	                f"<opt>_adam_tail), not be re-typed in the consumer.")
453	
454	    # (1c) SG11 cosine-gate re-inline detection: the staged precompute consumer MUST
455	    # obtain the cos(grad,momentum) reduction from the canonical sg11_sweep_a_step,
456	    # never re-inline `den_m += x*x` in its own loop (the path the cos(grad,mu) bug
457	    # took). Also assert it #includes the canonical supergrok11.h.
458	    for path in _cosine_consumer_headers():
459	        if _canonical_header("supergrok11") not in _read(path):
460	            failures.append(
461	                f"[structural] {path} does NOT #include the canonical "
462	                f"{_canonical_header('supergrok11')} (the SG11 cosine gate would "
463	                f"reimplement the reduction → drift). Add the #include.")
464	        for lineno, pat, line in scan_reinlined_cosine(path):
465	            failures.append(
466	                f"[cosine-re-inline] {path}:{lineno} re-inlines the SG11 cosine-gate "
467	                f"reduction (matched /{pat}/): `{line}`. The cos(grad,MOMENTUM) "
468	                f"accumulation MUST come from a call into algo::sg11_sweep_a_step "
469	                f"(csrc/algorithms/supergrok11.h), not be re-typed in the consumer "
470	                f"(re-inlining is exactly how the cos(grad,mu) bug crept in).")
471	
472	    if structural_only:
473	        return failures
474	
475	    # (2) content-hash manifest drift detection.
476	    if not os.path.exists(MANIFEST):
477	        failures.append(f"[manifest] {MANIFEST} missing — run --update-manifest.")
478	        return failures
479	    manifest_data = json.load(open(MANIFEST))
480	    recorded = manifest_data.get("hashes", {})
481	    cur = current_hashes()
482	    for opt in OPTS:
483	        if opt not in recorded:
484	            failures.append(f"[manifest] no recorded hash for {opt}.")
485	        elif recorded[opt] != cur[opt]:
486	            failures.append(
487	                f"[manifest] DRIFT: canonical csrc/algorithms/{opt}.h math "
488	                f"changed (hash {cur[opt][:12]} != recorded {recorded[opt][:12]}). "
489	                f"If intentional: sync the gfx942 transcription "
490	                f"(opt_components.hip.hpp) + TPU path, then --update-manifest.")
491	
492	    # (2b) binding-region drift detection (WS-F4): the pybind entrypoints in
493	    # bindings.cpp own the boundary guards + bias-correction + argument plumbing.
494	    recorded_bindings = manifest_data.get("binding_regions", {})
495	    cur_bindings = current_binding_hashes()
496	    for fn in BINDING_FUNCS:
497	        if fn not in recorded_bindings:
498	            failures.append(
499	                f"[binding] no recorded hash for {fn} — run --update-manifest.")
500	            continue
501	        # A vanished/renamed entrypoint hashes its empty body; surface that as a
502	        # distinct, louder message than a normal edit-drift.
503	        if not _extract_function_body(_read(BINDINGS_CPP), fn):
504	            failures.append(
505	                f"[binding] entrypoint {fn} not found in {BINDINGS_CPP} "
506	                f"(removed/renamed?). If intentional, update BINDING_FUNCS and "
507	                f"--update-manifest.")
508	        elif recorded_bindings[fn] != cur_bindings[fn]:
509	            failures.append(
510	                f"[binding] DRIFT: {BINDINGS_CPP}::{fn} changed "
511	                f"(hash {cur_bindings[fn][:12]} != recorded "
512	                f"{recorded_bindings[fn][:12]}). The binding owns the boundary "
513	                f"guards / bias-correction / list plumbing each launcher reads; "
514	                f"if the edit is intentional, --update-manifest.")
515	    return failures
516	
517	
518	def main(argv=None) -> int:
519	    argv = argv if argv is not None else sys.argv[1:]
520	    if "--update-manifest" in argv:
521	        return update_manifest()
522	    failures = check()
523	    print("=== optimizer-math drift guard (WS2, ENFORCED) ===")
524	    print(f"canonical: csrc/algorithms/<opt>.h  ({len(OPTS)} optimizers)")
525	    print(f"manifest:  {os.path.relpath(MANIFEST, ROOT)}")
526	    if failures:

531	    print("\nOK — single-source structural invariant holds AND no canonical-math "
532	          "drift vs the manifest.")

1	"""scripts/roofline_bench.py — 3-seed roofline timer for the d-scaled bench variants.
2	
3	Wraps tuning/{decoder,vit,mamba}_bench.py's build_variant() so the kernel-opt ratchet
4	(feedback-patch-protocol) gets PROTOCOL-COMPLIANT 3-seed median step-ms at the roofline
5	scale WITHOUT editing the bench drivers or any kernel file. It:
6	  * builds the coexisting bench variant ONCE (own module name + build dir + sccache —
7	    never touches the production _ops.so or the 33/33 gate),
8	  * optionally applies hill-climb -D KEY=VAL overrides (e.g. -D SG_TUNED_DEC_DW_SPLITK=8),
9	  * times `reps` timed windows per seed across `--seeds` (random params/tokens reseeded
10	    per seed; shapes/work identical so this is a timing-variance probe, the protocol's
11	    3-seed guard), and reports the per-seed median ms + the across-seed median.
12	
13	The candidate KEEP rule (owner ratchet): faster on >=3 seeds (every seed) AND the fp64
14	parity gate stays green. This harness produces the timing leg; the gate is run separately
15	on the production _ops.so at the toy d=128 config (the correctness oracle).
16	
17	USAGE
18	  PYTHONPATH=. python scripts/roofline_bench.py --model decoder --d 2048 --B 16384 \
19	      --seeds 42,7,123 --reps 3
20	  PYTHONPATH=. python scripts/roofline_bench.py --model decoder --d 2048 --B 16384 \
21	      --seeds 42,7,123 --reps 3 -D SG_TUNED_DEC_DW_SPLITK=8
22	"""
23	from __future__ import annotations
24	
25	import argparse
26	import json
27	import statistics
28	import sys
29	import time
30	from pathlib import Path
31	
32	ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
33	sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
34	
35	import torch  # noqa: E402
36	
37	
38	def _import_bench(model: str):
39	    if model == "decoder":
40	        import tuning.decoder_bench as B
41	        return B
42	    if model == "vit":
43	        import tuning.vit_bench as B
44	        return B
45	    if model == "mamba":
46	        import tuning.mamba_bench as B
47	        return B
48	    raise ValueError(f"unknown model {model!r}")
49	
50	
51	def _build(model: str, B, d: int, defines, verbose: bool):
52	    # decoder_bench.build_variant has a distinct (d, profile, ...) signature; vit/mamba
53	    # are (d, ...). Normalize.
54	    if model == "decoder":
55	        return B.build_variant(d, profile=False, verbose=verbose, defines=defines)
56	    return B.build_variant(d, verbose=verbose, defines=defines)
57	
58	
59	def _inputs(model: str, mod, d: int, batch: int, seed: int, dev):
60	    """Reproduce each bench's measure() input construction, reseeded per `seed`."""
61	    total = int(mod.TOTAL)
62	    g = torch.Generator(device=dev).manual_seed(seed)
63	    params = (torch.randn(total, generator=g, device=dev) * 0.02).contiguous()
64	    state = torch.zeros(3 * total, dtype=torch.float32, device=dev)
65	    if model == "decoder":
66	        vocab, seq = int(mod.VOCAB), int(mod.SEQ)
67	        tok = torch.randint(0, vocab, (batch, seq), generator=g, device=dev).to(torch.int32).contiguous()
68	        tgt = torch.randint(0, vocab, (batch,), generator=g, device=dev).to(torch.int32).contiguous()
69	        return params, tok, tgt, state
70	    if model == "vit":
71	        from tests.hw.vit_oracle import NUM_PATCHES, PATCH_DIM, VOCAB
72	        x = torch.randn(batch, NUM_PATCHES, PATCH_DIM, generator=g, device=dev).to(torch.float32).contiguous()
73	        tgt = torch.randint(0, VOCAB, (batch,), generator=g, device=dev).to(torch.int32).contiguous()
74	        return params, x, tgt, state
75	    if model == "mamba":
76	        from tests.hw.mamba_oracle import VOCAB, P_HEAD, SEQ
77	        tok = torch.randint(0, VOCAB, (batch, SEQ), generator=g, device=dev).to(torch.int32).contiguous()
78	        tgt = torch.randint(0, P_HEAD, (batch,), generator=g, device=dev).to(torch.int32).contiguous()
79	        return params, tok, tgt, state
80	    raise ValueError(model)
81	
82	
83	def _flops(model: str, B, mod, d: int, batch: int) -> float:
84	    if model == "decoder":
85	        return B._decoder_gemm_flops_per_step(d, batch, int(mod.LAYERS), int(mod.SEQ), int(mod.VOCAB))
86	    # vit/mamba compute flops inline in measure(); recompute here from exposed attrs.
87	    if model == "vit":
88	        from tests.hw.vit_oracle import VOCAB
89	        layers, seq, dff = int(mod.LAYERS), int(mod.SEQ), 4 * d
90	        T = batch * seq
91	        fwd = 0.0
92	        for _ in range(layers):
93	            fwd += 2.0 * T * (3 * d) * d + 2.0 * T * d * d + 2.0 * T * dff * d + 2.0 * T * d * dff
94	        fwd += 2.0 * batch * VOCAB * d
95	        return 3.0 * fwd
96	    if model == "mamba":
97	        from tests.hw.mamba_oracle import P_HEAD
98	        layers, seq = int(mod.LAYERS), int(mod.SEQ)
99	        di, dtr, st = int(mod.DINNER), int(mod.DTRANK), int(mod.STATE)
100	        dbc = dtr + 2 * st
101	        T = batch * seq
102	        fwd = 0.0
103	        for _ in range(layers):
104	            fwd += 2.0 * T * (2 * di) * d + 2.0 * T * dbc * di + 2.0 * T * di * dtr + 2.0 * T * d * di
105	        fwd += 2.0 * batch * P_HEAD * d
106	        return 3.0 * fwd
107	    raise ValueError(model)
108	
109	
110	def time_seed(model, mod, args, seed, dev):
111	    params, a, b, state = _inputs(model, mod, args.d, args.B, seed, dev)
112	    lr, beta1, beta2, eps, wd = 1e-3, 0.9, 0.98, 1e-8, 0.0
113	    bc1, bc2 = 1.0 - beta1, 1.0 - beta2
114	    ncta = 0
115	
116	    def call():
117	        return mod.tc_train_step(params, a, b, state, lr, beta1, beta2, eps, wd, bc1, bc2, 1, ncta)
118	
119	    for _ in range(args.warmup):
120	        call()
121	    torch.cuda.synchronize()
122	    walls = []
123	    for _ in range(args.reps):
124	        torch.cuda.synchronize()
125	        t0 = time.perf_counter()
126	        for _ in range(args.iters):
127	            call()
128	        torch.cuda.synchronize()
129	        walls.append((time.perf_counter() - t0) / args.iters)
130	    return statistics.median(walls), [w * 1e3 for w in walls]
131	
132	
133	def main():
134	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
135	    ap.add_argument("--model", required=True, choices=["decoder", "vit", "mamba"])
136	    ap.add_argument("--d", type=int, required=True)
137	    ap.add_argument("--B", type=int, default=16384)
138	    ap.add_argument("--seeds", default="42,7,123")
139	    ap.add_argument("--reps", type=int, default=3)
140	    ap.add_argument("--warmup", type=int, default=8)
141	    ap.add_argument("--iters", type=int, default=15)
142	    ap.add_argument("--verbose-build", action="store_true")
143	    ap.add_argument("-D", dest="defines", action="append", default=[], metavar="KEY=VAL")
144	    args = ap.parse_args()
145	    assert args.B % 16 == 0, "B must be %16==0"
146	    seeds = [int(s) for s in args.seeds.split(",") if s.strip()]
147	
148	    B = _import_bench(args.model)
149	    t0 = time.perf_counter()
150	    mod = _build(args.model, B, args.d, args.defines, args.verbose_build)
151	    build_s = time.perf_counter() - t0
152	    assert int(mod.D) == args.d, f"TU compiled at D={int(mod.D)}, expected {args.d}"
153	    dev = torch.device("cuda")
154	    flops = _flops(args.model, B, mod, args.d, args.B)
155	
156	    per_seed = {}
157	    for s in seeds:
158	        med, walls = time_seed(args.model, mod, args, s, dev)
159	        per_seed[s] = {"median_ms": med * 1e3, "walls_ms": [round(w, 4) for w in walls],
160	                       "tf_s": flops / med / 1e12}
161	    across = statistics.median([per_seed[s]["median_ms"] for s in seeds])
162	    out = {
163	        "model": args.model, "d": args.d, "B": args.B,
164	        "total_params": int(mod.TOTAL), "defines": args.defines,
165	        "build_s": round(build_s, 1),
166	        "per_seed_median_ms": {s: round(per_seed[s]["median_ms"], 4) for s in seeds},
167	        "across_seed_median_ms": round(across, 4),
168	        "achieved_tf_s": round(flops / (across / 1e3) / 1e12, 3),
169	        "pct_roofline": round(100.0 * (flops / (across / 1e3) / 1e12) / 989.0, 3),
170	        "per_seed_walls_ms": {s: per_seed[s]["walls_ms"] for s in seeds},
171	    }
172	    print("ROOFLINE " + json.dumps(out), flush=True)
173	    return out
174	
175	
176	if __name__ == "__main__":
177	    main()

1	"""scripts/time_cell.py — median step-time of a production L3-TC cell.
2	
3	Times `dispatch.fused_train_step(model, opt, ...)` end-to-end (the production race
4	path) with CUDA events: `warmup` un-timed steps, then `iters` timed steps repeated
5	`reps` times; reports the median per-step wall-ms (and steps/s). Built for the
6	register-pressure patch ratchet (P3/P4/P5): the SAM-coupled cells (looksam/
7	supergrok11/supergrok15/supergrok2) run the tile fwd+bwd TWICE, which is exactly
8	what the `__noinline__` outlining patches target, so we force the SAM path on.
9	
10	Usage:
11	  python scripts/time_cell.py --model vit --opts looksam,supergrok11,supergrok15,supergrok2 \
12	                              --seed 42 --warmup 10 --iters 30 --reps 5
13	Prints one JSON line per (opt) so a caller can diff baseline-vs-patched across seeds.
14	"""
15	import argparse, json, statistics, os
16	import torch
17	
18	from grokking_optimizers.dispatch import fused_train_step, canonicalize_model
19	import tests.hw.test_l3tc_tail_gate as G
20	
21	
22	def _build(model, opt, seed):
23	    """Reuse the gate's exact cell construction (model + config + data + optimizer)
24	    so timing matches what the parity gate validated."""
25	    os.environ["GATE_SEED"] = str(seed)
26	    g, c, m, data, dev = G._build_cell(model)
27	    tx, ty = data[0], data[1]
28	    spec = G._CELLS[f"{opt}/{model}"]
29	    opt_obj = spec["factory"](g, m.parameters(), c)
30	    return g, c, m, data, dev, tx, ty, opt_obj
31	
32	
33	def time_cell(model, opt, seed, warmup, iters, reps):
34	    g, c, m, data, dev, tx, ty, opt_obj = _build(model, opt, seed)
35	    canon = canonicalize_model(model)
36	    state_cache = {}
37	
38	    def step():
39	        # force the SAM path on (looksam_sam=1) for SAM-coupled cells so the double
40	        # tile pass the outlining patches optimize is exercised every timed step.
41	        fused_train_step(canon, opt, m, opt_obj, tx, ty, state_cache=state_cache,
42	                         step=1, gemm_impl="wgmma")
43	
44	    for _ in range(warmup):
45	        step()
46	    torch.cuda.synchronize()
47	    walls = []
48	    for _ in range(reps):
49	        ev0 = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
50	        ev1 = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
51	        ev0.record()
52	        for _ in range(iters):
53	            step()
54	        ev1.record()
55	        torch.cuda.synchronize()
56	        walls.append(ev0.elapsed_time(ev1) / iters)   # ms/step
57	    return {
58	        "model": model, "opt": opt, "seed": seed,
59	        "median_ms": statistics.median(walls),
60	        "min_ms": min(walls),
61	        "walls_ms": [round(w, 4) for w in walls],
62	    }
63	
64	
65	def main():
66	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
67	    ap.add_argument("--model", required=True)
68	    ap.add_argument("--opts", required=True, help="comma-separated optimizer keys")
69	    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=42)
70	    ap.add_argument("--warmup", type=int, default=10)
71	    ap.add_argument("--iters", type=int, default=30)
72	    ap.add_argument("--reps", type=int, default=5)
73	    args = ap.parse_args()
74	    for opt in args.opts.split(","):
75	        opt = opt.strip()
76	        if not opt:
77	            continue
78	        try:
79	            r = time_cell(args.model, opt, args.seed, args.warmup, args.iters, args.reps)
80	            print("TIMING " + json.dumps(r), flush=True)
81	        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
82	            print(f"TIMING_ERROR {opt}/{args.model} seed={args.seed}: "
83	                  f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}", flush=True)
84	
85	
86	if __name__ == "__main__":
87	    main()

28	    k_sharp = kstate[3*total+1: 4*total+1].clone()
29	    scalars = _opt_scalars_from(opt_obj, 1)
30	    rho = float(scalars.get("rho", 0.05))
31	    sam_on = float(scalars.get("looksam_sam", 0.0))
32	    print(f"  looksam_sam (SAM-step gate @ step1) = {sam_on}   rho = {rho}")
33	    assert sam_on != 0.0, "SAM 2nd backward did NOT fire at step 1 -- diagnostic would be vacuous"
34	    g_r, c_r, m_ref, data_r, dev_r = G._build_cell(model)
35	    named_ref = [(n, p) for n, p in m_ref.named_parameters() if p.requires_grad]
36	    sharp_bf = G._sg_bf16_sharpness_oracle(model, named_ref, tx, ty, grad, rho, total, dev)
37	    B = int(tx.shape[0]); B16 = B - (B % 16)
38	    a0 = tx[:B16].detach().cpu().to(torch.long); a1 = ty[:B16].detach().cpu().to(torch.long)
39	    named_d = {n: p.detach().cpu().double() for n, p in named_ref}
40	    _lo, go64 = _pure_fp64_oracle(named_d, a0, a1)
41	    gn = torch.sqrt(sum((v.double()**2).sum() for v in go64.values())).item()
42	    ron = rho / gn
43	    off = 0; named_pert = {}
44	    for n_, p in named_ref:
45	        k = p.numel()
46	        named_pert[n_] = (p.detach().cpu().double()
47	                          + ron * grad[off:off+k].reshape(p.shape).cpu().double())
48	        off += k
49	    _lo2, go64p = _pure_fp64_oracle(named_pert, a0, a1)
50	    sharp_fp = torch.cat([((go64p[n_] - go64[n_]).reshape(-1).double())**2
51	                          for n_, _ in named_ref]).float().to(dev)
52	
53	    def relmax(a, b):
54	        return (a-b).abs().max().item() / (b.abs().max().item() + 1e-30)
55	    print(f"  REF sharpness max|.|  : bf16-faithful = {sharp_bf.abs().max().item():.4e}   pure-fp64 = {sharp_fp.abs().max().item():.4e}")
56	    print(f"  kernel sharpness max|.|= {k_sharp.abs().max().item():.4e}")
57	    sh_abs = (k_sharp - sharp_bf).abs().max().item()
58	    print(f"  [GATE]   abs d (kernel - bf16faithful) = {sh_abs:.4e}   sharp_rel = {relmax(k_sharp, sharp_bf):.4e}   (tol 2e-2)")
59	    r_k_fp = relmax(k_sharp, sharp_fp)
60	    r_bf_fp = relmax(sharp_bf, sharp_fp)
61	    print(f"  [CLASS]  kernel vs pure-fp64       = {r_k_fp:.4e}")
62	    print(f"  [CLASS]  bf16faithful vs pure-fp64 = {r_bf_fp:.4e}   (== design bf16 FLOOR on sharpness^2)")
63	    print(f"  [CLASS]  (kernel-vs-fp64)/(floor)  = {r_k_fp/(r_bf_fp+1e-30):.3f}   --> ~1 => (a) ON floor/BENIGN ; >>1 => (b) REAL gap")
64	    off = 0; perlayer = {}
65	    for n_, p in named_ref:
66	        k = p.numel()
67	        r = relmax(k_sharp[off:off+k], sharp_fp[off:off+k])
68	        lk = n_.split(".")[1] if n_.startswith("layers.") else n_
69	        perlayer[lk] = max(perlayer.get(lk, 0.0), r); off += k
70	    show = {k: round(v, 4) for k, v in perlayer.items() if k in ("0", "1")}
71	    print(f"  [STRUCT] per-layer worst kernel-vs-fp64 rel (layer0 vs layer1): {show}  (layer0 >> layer1 => real compounding bug)")
72	
73	
74	for cell in ("supergrok11/mamba", "supergrok15/mamba"):
75	    classify(cell)
76	print("\nDONE.")

1	# Diagnostic: classify the neuralgrok/decoder (1a) FAIL at GATE_SEED=123 as
2	#   (a) benign-within-bf16  vs  (b) real kernel-tail gap.
3	# READ-ONLY harness reuse: builds the SAME cell the gate builds, runs ONE real
4	# L3-TC step (kernel-under-test, megakernel apply_optimizer<NeuralGrok>, H=16),
5	# the SAME eager reference the gate uses (opt_ref.step() -> per-op
6	# neuralgrok_fused_step), AND a FULL-fp64 recomputation of the neuralgrok update
7	# on the kernel's own reduced grad with the TRUE H=16 amplifier. Prints, for the
8	# single worst-Δ coordinate: param name, abs Δ(kernel vs eager), reference
9	# magnitude there, and BOTH kernel & eager vs the fp64 oracle. The fp64 oracle is
10	# the arbiter: if the KERNEL matches it to bf16 roundoff while the EAGER does not,
11	# the kernel is correct and the FAIL is the gate's reference (classification (a),
12	# the 1e-4 pure-rel tol with no abs floor). If the KERNEL diverges from the fp64
13	# oracle, that is a real tail bug (classification (b)).
14	#
15	#   Run:  cd /workspace/SuperGrok1.5 && GATE_SEED=123 PYTHONPATH=. python - < scripts/diag_neuralgrok_seed123.py
16	#   (or:  GATE_SEED=123 PYTHONPATH=. python scripts/diag_neuralgrok_seed123.py)
17	import os
18	os.environ.setdefault("GATE_SEED", "123")   # the failing seed (also try 7; 42 passes)
19	
20	import torch
21	from tests.hw.test_l3tc_tail_gate import _build_cell, _neuralgrok_factory
22	from grokking_optimizers.dispatch import (canonicalize_model, fused_train_step,
23	                                          has_l3_real, gemm_impl_for_cell)
24	
25	MODEL = "decoder"
26	SEED = int(os.environ["GATE_SEED"])
27	print(f"=== neuralgrok/{MODEL} (1a) diagnostic @ GATE_SEED={SEED} ===")
28	
29	
30	def _flat_named(m):
31	    named = [(n, p) for n, p in m.named_parameters() if p.requires_grad]
32	    return named, sum(p.numel() for _, p in named)
33	
34	
35	def _psi_fp64_H16(abs_g, W1, b1, W2, b2):
36	    """The EXACT psi the deployed kernel (kPsiHidden=16) computes, in fp64:
37	       psi = sum_{j<16} W2[j]*relu(W1[j]*|g| + b1[j]) + b2.
38	    W1=[16,1], b1=[16], W2=[1,16], b2=[1] (the amplifier's get_weights layout)."""
39	    H = 16
40	    w1 = W1.reshape(-1).double()          # [16]
41	    bb1 = b1.reshape(-1).double()         # [16]
42	    w2 = W2.reshape(-1).double()          # [16]
43	    bb2 = float(b2.reshape(-1)[0])
44	    hid = torch.relu(abs_g.unsqueeze(1) * w1.reshape(1, H) + bb1.reshape(1, H))  # [N,16]
45	    return (hid * w2.reshape(1, H)).sum(1) + bb2                                  # [N]
46	
47	
48	def _neuralgrok_fp64_params(p_before, grad, opt_obj):
49	    """FULL-fp64 neuralgrok step-1 update on the kernel's reduced grad, TRUE H=16
50	    psi (the algorithm's documented contract — neuralgrok.h, kPsiHidden=16). Zero-
51	    init moments. Returns p_after_fp64 (flat fp64). This is the ARBITER both kernel
52	    and eager are scored against."""
53	    grp = opt_obj.param_groups[0]
54	    alpha = float(grp["alpha"]); beta = float(grp["beta"])
55	    b1, b2 = float(grp["betas"][0]), float(grp["betas"][1])
56	    lr = float(grp["lr"]); eps = float(grp["eps"]); wd = float(grp["weight_decay"])
57	    bc1 = 1.0 - b1 ** 1; bc2 = 1.0 - b2 ** 1
58	    W1, b1w, W2, b2w = opt_obj.amplifier.get_weights()
59	    g = grad.double()
60	    psi = _psi_fp64_H16(g.abs(), W1.to(g.device), b1w.to(g.device),
61	                        W2.to(g.device), b2w.to(g.device))
62	    g_amp = (psi * alpha + beta) * g
63	    m = (1.0 - b1) * g_amp
64	    v = (1.0 - b2) * g_amp * g_amp
65	    update = (m / max(bc1, 1e-30)) / (torch.sqrt(v / max(bc2, 1e-30)) + eps)
66	    p = p_before.double()
67	    return p - lr * (update + wd * p), g_amp
68	
69	
70	# ── 1) KERNEL-UNDER-TEST: one production L3-TC step (megakernel, H=16). ──────
71	g, c, m, data, dev = _build_cell(MODEL, seed=SEED)
72	canon = canonicalize_model(MODEL)
73	assert has_l3_real(canon, "neuralgrok"), "neuralgrok/decoder not L3-REAL"
74	assert gemm_impl_for_cell(canon, "neuralgrok", "bf16") == "wgmma"
75	tx, ty = data[0], data[1]
76	opt_obj = _neuralgrok_factory(g, m.parameters(), c)
77	named0, total = _flat_named(m)
78	p_before = torch.cat([p.data.reshape(-1) for _, p in named0]).clone()
79	cache = {}
80	loss, grad = fused_train_step(canon, "neuralgrok", m, opt_obj, tx, ty,
81	                              state_cache=cache, step=1, return_grad=True,
82	                              gemm_impl="wgmma")
83	p_after_kernel = torch.cat([p.data.reshape(-1) for _, p in named0]).clone()
84	
85	# global grad-norm clip inertness (the gate asserts this; report it, do not abort)
86	gclip = float(opt_obj.param_groups[0].get("grad_clip", 0.0))
87	gnorm = grad.detach().double().norm().item()
88	print(f"loss={loss:.5f}  global grad-norm={gnorm:.4f}  grad_clip={gclip}  "
89	      f"clip {'INERT' if (gclip <= 0 or gnorm <= gclip) else 'WOULD FIRE'}")
90	
91	# ── 2) EAGER REFERENCE: the gate's reference — fresh model, same init, inject the
92	#       kernel's reduced grad, copy opt_obj's amplifier, one opt_ref.step() (per-op
93	#       neuralgrok_fused_step kernel, which is compiled at NG_H=64). ─────────────
94	g_r, c_r, m_ref, data_r, dev_r = _build_cell(MODEL, seed=SEED)
95	named_ref, _ = _flat_named(m_ref)
96	p_ref_before = torch.cat([p.data.reshape(-1) for _, p in named_ref])
97	assert torch.equal(p_ref_before, p_before), "ref init != kernel init (seed mismatch)"
98	opt_ref = _neuralgrok_factory(g_r, m_ref.parameters(), c_r)
99	opt_ref.amplifier.load_state_dict(opt_obj.amplifier.state_dict())
100	opt_ref.mark_amplifier_dirty()
101	off = 0
102	for _, p in named_ref:
103	    n = p.numel(); p.grad = grad[off:off + n].reshape(p.shape).clone(); off += n
104	torch.cuda.synchronize()
105	opt_ref.step()
106	p_after_eager = torch.cat([p.data.reshape(-1) for _, p in named_ref]).clone()
107	
108	# ── 3) FULL-fp64 ARBITER: neuralgrok step-1 on the kernel's reduced grad, H=16. ─
109	p_after_fp64, g_amp_fp64 = _neuralgrok_fp64_params(p_before, grad, opt_obj)
110	
111	# ── Locate the offending coordinate = argmax|kernel - eager| (the gate's metric).
112	d_ke = (p_after_kernel.double() - p_after_eager.double()).abs()
113	i = int(torch.argmax(d_ke).item())
114	# Map flat index i -> (param name, local idx).
115	off = 0; off_name = None; off_local = None
116	for n_, p in named0:
117	    k = p.numel()
118	    if off <= i < off + k:
119	        off_name = n_; off_local = i - off; break
120	    off += k
121	
122	abs_ke = d_ke[i].item()
123	ref_mag_global = p_after_eager.double().abs().max().item()
124	rel_gate = abs_ke / (ref_mag_global + 1e-30)
125	print(f"\n[(1a) gate metric] max|Δp(kernel,eager)| = {abs_ke:.3e}  "
126	      f"rel = {rel_gate:.3e}  (tol 1e-4 -> {'FAIL' if rel_gate>1e-4 else 'PASS'})")
127	print(f"[offending coord]  name={off_name!r}  local_idx={off_local}  "
128	      f"flat_idx={i}")
129	print(f"                   |p_ref| at that coord = {abs(p_after_eager[i].item()):.4f}  "
130	      f"(reference magnitude there)")
131	
132	# Per-coordinate breakdown at the worst index: kernel vs eager vs fp64 oracle.
133	pk = p_after_kernel[i].item(); pe = p_after_eager[i].item(); po = p_after_fp64[i].item()
134	gi = grad[i].item(); gampi = g_amp_fp64[i].item()
135	print(f"\n[coord {i}] grad={gi:+.6e}  g_amp(fp64,H16)={gampi:+.6e}  "
136	      f"sign(g_amp)={'+' if gampi>=0 else '-'}")
137	print(f"           p_before        = {p_before[i].item():+.8f}")
138	print(f"           p_after KERNEL  = {pk:+.8f}   (Δ vs before {pk-p_before[i].item():+.3e})")
139	print(f"           p_after EAGER   = {pe:+.8f}   (Δ vs before {pe-p_before[i].item():+.3e})")
140	print(f"           p_after FP64    = {po:+.8f}   (Δ vs before {po-p_before[i].item():+.3e})  <-- ARBITER (H=16)")
141	
142	# ── THE CLASSIFIER: score kernel and eager against the fp64 H=16 oracle. ─────────
143	# bf16 relative ulp ~ 2^-8 ~ 3.9e-3; the reduced grad rounds at bf16 storage points
144	# in the wgmma backward, so a kernel/eager that AGREES with the fp64-H16 update to
145	# ~bf16 roundoff is "within bf16 precision". A SIGN FLIP of g_amp (psi*alpha+beta
146	# crossing zero) makes the AdamW step jump by 2*lr — that is NOT roundoff.
147	def _score(p_after, tag):
148	    d = (p_after.double() - p_after_fp64).abs()
149	    j = int(torch.argmax(d).item())
150	    rel = d.max().item() / (p_after_fp64.abs().max().item() + 1e-30)
151	    print(f"  {tag:26s} vs fp64-H16 oracle: max|Δ|={d.max().item():.3e}  "
152	          f"rel={rel:.3e}  worst_flat_idx={j}")
153	    return d.max().item(), rel
154	
155	print("\n[ARBITER scores — both implementations vs the FULL-fp64 H=16 update on the "
156	      "kernel's own reduced grad]")
157	k_abs, k_rel = _score(p_after_kernel, "KERNEL (megakernel,H=16)")
158	e_abs, e_rel = _score(p_after_eager, "EAGER  (per-op,NG_H=64)")
159	
160	# bf16 floor for an O(|p|) param under this update: |Δp| ~ lr*(1+wd*|p|); a roundoff
161	# difference is <~ bf16_ulp * that. A 2*lr jump is the sign-flip signature.
162	lr = float(opt_obj.param_groups[0]["lr"])
163	two_lr = 2.0 * lr
164	bf16_ulp = 2.0 ** -8
165	print(f"\n  2*lr (one-coord sign-flip signature) = {two_lr:.3e}")
166	print(f"  0.05*lr (legacy zero-grad eps-noise floor) = {0.05*lr:.3e}")
167	
168	print("\n=== VERDICT ===")
169	KERNEL_BF16_OK = k_abs <= max(8.0 * bf16_ulp * (1.0 + abs(p_after_fp64).max().item()),
170	                              0.05 * lr)
171	if KERNEL_BF16_OK and e_abs > 0.5 * two_lr:
172	    print("(a)-variant: KERNEL matches the fp64-H16 oracle to within bf16 roundoff; the "
173	          "EAGER reference diverges (≈2*lr sign-flip). The kernel-under-test is CORRECT. "
174	          "The (1a) FAIL is the GATE's eager reference computing psi at the WRONG width "
175	          "(per-op neuralgrok kernel NG_H=64 vs the deployed/megakernel kPsiHidden=16 — "
176	          "reads 48 floats OOB per weight array; the OOB garbage is seed/allocation-"
177	          "dependent and at seeds 123/7 flips sign(g_amp) for one coord). FIX is the gate, "
178	          "NOT the kernel: anchor (1a) to the fp64-H16 oracle (like (1b) already is) and/or "
179	          "add the standard 0.05*lr abs floor; the H=64 per-op reference must not gate the "
180	          "H=16 kernel. (The per-op NG_H=64 width is itself a real, separate, out-of-scope "
181	          "kernel defect.)")
182	elif not KERNEL_BF16_OK and k_abs >= 0.5 * two_lr:
183	    print("(b): KERNEL DIVERGES from the fp64-H16 oracle by ~2*lr (a real g_amp sign flip in "
184	          "the kernel tail). This is a REAL bf16 accuracy gap/bug in the neuralgrok kernel "
185	          "tail — FIX the kernel, not the tolerance.")
186	else:
187	    print(f"INDETERMINATE: kernel rel={k_rel:.2e}, eager rel={e_rel:.2e}. Inspect the per-"
188	          f"coord block above; compare seed 42 (passes) vs 123/7 (fail) to confirm the "
189	          f"sign-flip is reference-side.")
190

1	"""Quiet baseline: measure the vit L3-TC megakernel (tc_train_step) roofline
2	fraction at the SM-saturation batch, using the SAME FLOP/AI/ceiling logic as
3	tuning/roofline.py. Run MPS-isolated (CUDA_MPS_PIPE_DIRECTORY=/nonexistent).
4	
5	Reports achieved TF/s, ceiling, fraction, wall/step, and the scalar/TC ratio.
6	This is the optimization metric for the vit cells (the converted-3 share this
7	fwd+bwd+reduce megakernel; the opt tail is a negligible fraction of the wall).
8	"""
9	import sys
10	from pathlib import Path
11	
12	ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
13	sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
14	
15	import torch  # noqa: E402
16	import tuning.roofline as R  # noqa: E402
17	
18	
19	def main():
20	    B = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 16384
21	    model = "vit"
22	    # FLOPs/step + n_params from the eager-profiled adamw pipeline (path-independent
23	    # GEMM count). We run the cheap profile pass of measure_pipeline to grab it.
24	    data, init, n_params = R._data_init(model)
25	    eager_B_full = data[0].shape[0]
26	    # Tile the data to B for the FLOP basis (FLOPs linear in B; measure_tc_cell
27	    # rescales by B/eager_B_full, so pass the eager profile's native B + flops).
28	    # Use measure_pipeline's profiler to get eager flops at native B.
29	    import torch.profiler as tp
30	    g = R._g()
31	    dev = torch.device("cuda")
32	    c = R._cfg("adamw", model, 10, 10 ** 9)
33	    c["matmul_precision"] = "bf16"; c["use_amp"] = False
34	    c["use_fused"] = False
35	    c["max_steps"] = 20; c["early_stop_max_steps"] = 20
36	    torch.manual_seed(42)
37	    with tp.profile(activities=[tp.ProfilerActivity.CUDA, tp.ProfilerActivity.CPU],
38	                    with_flops=True) as prof:
39	        g.train_adamw(c, init, *data, dev, bp=0)
40	    flops_total = sum(getattr(e, "flops", 0) or 0 for e in prof.key_averages())
41	    eager_flops_full = flops_total / 20.0
42	    print(f"[baseline] eager FLOPs/step @ B={eager_B_full}: {eager_flops_full:.4e}", flush=True)
43	
44	    dc = R._cfg("adamw", model, 10, 10 ** 9)
45	    seq = dc.get("num_patches", 16)
46	    dim = dc.get("dim_model", 128)
47	    layers = dc.get("num_layers", 2)
48	
49	    # Tile FLOP basis to the requested measurement batch B (measure_tc_cell uses
50	    # eager_B_full to rescale, so we feed it the native eager flops + B and let it
51	    # scale to its own B%16). To measure at B, we pass eager_B_full=B by rescaling:
52	    flops_at_B = eager_flops_full * (B / float(eager_B_full))
53	
54	    rows = R.measure_tc_cell(model, flops_at_B, B, n_params, seq, dim, layers)
55	    print("\n[baseline] vit TC + scalar rows:", flush=True)
56	    for r in rows:
57	        print(f"  path={r['path']:38s} prec={r['precision']:7s} "
58	              f"B={r['tc_batch']} wall/step={r['wall_per_step_ms']:.4f}ms "
59	              f"achieved={r['achieved_flops_per_s']/1e12:.2f}TF/s "
60	              f"ceiling={r['roofline_ceiling_flops_per_s']/1e12:.2f}TF/s "
61	              f"frac={r['fraction_of_roofline']:.4f} "
62	              f"AI={r['arithmetic_intensity']:.1f} bound={r['bound_regime_at_AI']}",
63	              flush=True)
64	    tc = next((r for r in rows if r["path_family"] == "tc"), None)
65	    if tc:
66	        print(f"\n[VIT-TC-BASELINE] B={tc['tc_batch']} achieved={tc['achieved_flops_per_s']/1e12:.3f} TF/s "
67	              f"frac_of_roofline={tc['fraction_of_roofline']:.4f} "
68	              f"wall/step={tc['wall_per_step_ms']:.4f}ms", flush=True)
69	
70	
71	if __name__ == "__main__":
72	    main()

1	"""Minimal single-launch driver for ncu profiling of the vit TC megakernel.
2	Builds the vit TC TU, runs ONE tc_train_step at a small batch (enough to fill
3	the grid: >= 132 tiles → B*kSeq/1088 >= 132 → B >= 8448; use B=8704 = 512*17
4	which gives exactly 136 tiles, >132 SMs, so every SM gets >=1 tile but the run
5	is short). ncu wraps this; we want warp-stall reasons + SOL + tensor-pipe %.
6	
7	NOTE: grid-barrier persistent kernels DEADLOCK under ncu default kernel-replay;
8	the caller MUST pass --replay-mode application.
9	"""
10	import sys
11	from pathlib import Path
12	
13	ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
14	sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
15	
16	import torch  # noqa: E402
17	import tuning.roofline as R  # noqa: E402
18	
19	
20	def main():
21	    B = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 8704  # 512 samples → 8704 rows? no: 512*17=8704
22	    dev = torch.device("cuda")
23	    mod, params, inp, tgt, total = R._tc_inputs("vit", B, dev)
24	    state = torch.zeros(3 * total, dtype=torch.float32, device=dev)
25	    beta1, beta2 = 0.9, 0.98
26	    bc1, bc2 = 1.0 - beta1, 1.0 - beta2
27	    lr, eps, wd = 1e-3, 1e-8, 0.0
28	    # warmup once (build caches / one-time) OUTSIDE the profiled region is not
29	    # possible with ncu launch-count=1 capturing the first launch; ncu --launch-skip
30	    # handles that. Here we just issue exactly the calls; caller controls skip/count.
31	    for _ in range(int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 3):
32	        mod.tc_train_step(params.clone(), inp, tgt, state, lr, beta1, beta2,
33	                          eps, wd, bc1, bc2, 1, 0)

1	"""Build the vit TC TU with -DSG_VIT_PROFILE and read the per-phase clock64
2	breakdown (P1 fwd, P1 bwd, P2 dW+reduce, P3 opt tail) at B=16384. Run quiet.
3	
4	Picks the dominant phase → tells us which structural lever to pull next.
5	"""
6	import os
7	import sys
8	from pathlib import Path
9	
10	ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
11	sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
12	
13	import torch  # noqa: E402
14	from torch.utils.cpp_extension import load  # noqa: E402
15	
16	
17	def main():
18	    B = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 16384
19	    os.environ["TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST"] = "9.0a"
20	    dev = torch.device("cuda")
21	    tu = str(ROOT / "csrc/fused/sm_90/mega_vit_real_adamw_tc.cu")
22	    mod = load(
23	        name="mega_vit_real_adamw_tc_PROF",
24	        sources=[tu],
25	        extra_include_paths=[str(ROOT)],
26	        extra_cuda_cflags=["-O3", "-std=c++17", "--expt-relaxed-constexpr",
27	                           "-gencode=arch=compute_90a,code=sm_90a",
28	                           "-DSG_VIT_PROFILE=1"],
29	        extra_cflags=["-O3", "-std=c++17", "-DSG_VIT_PROFILE=1"],
30	        verbose=False,
31	    )
32	    assert getattr(mod, "HAS_PROFILE", False), "profile build missing"
33	    total = int(mod.TOTAL)
34	    from tests.hw.vit_oracle import NUM_PATCHES, PATCH_DIM, VOCAB
35	    gpar = torch.Generator(device=dev).manual_seed(42)
36	    params = (torch.randn(total, generator=gpar, device=dev) * 0.02).contiguous()
37	    gin = torch.Generator(device=dev).manual_seed(7)
38	    inp = torch.randn(B, NUM_PATCHES, PATCH_DIM, generator=gin, device=dev).to(torch.float32)
39	    tgt = torch.randint(0, VOCAB, (B,), generator=gin, device=dev).to(torch.int32)
40	    state = torch.zeros(3 * total, dtype=torch.float32, device=dev)
41	    beta1, beta2 = 0.9, 0.98
42	    bc1, bc2 = 1.0 - beta1, 1.0 - beta2
43	    lr, eps, wd = 1e-3, 1e-8, 0.0
44	
45	    def call():
46	        return mod.tc_train_step(params.clone(), inp, tgt, state, lr, beta1, beta2,
47	                                 eps, wd, bc1, bc2, 1, 0)
48	    # warmup
49	    for _ in range(5):
50	        call()
51	    torch.cuda.synchronize()
52	    mod.tc_profile_read()  # reset
53	    # measured: a few steps, then read the max-across-CTAs per phase
54	    import time
55	    t0 = time.perf_counter()
56	    N = 20
57	    for _ in range(N):
58	        call()
59	    torch.cuda.synchronize()
60	    wall_ms = (time.perf_counter() - t0) / N * 1e3
61	    cyc = mod.tc_profile_read()  # [P1fwd, P1bwd, P2dW, P3opt] cycles (max over CTAs, over N steps? no—reset each? )
62	    # NOTE: g_vit_prof_max accumulates the MAX across all launches since reset (not
63	    # summed). Since every step has ~identical work, the max == one step's per-phase
64	    # critical-path cycles. Convert with the SM clock (~1.98 GHz boost on H100).
65	    sm_ghz = 1.98
66	    names = ["P1_fwd", "P1_bwd", "B1_barrier_wait", "P2_dW_GEMM",
67	             "P2_grad_assembly", "P3_opt_tail"]
68	    tot = sum(cyc) or 1
69	    print(f"[vit-phase] B={B} wall/step={wall_ms:.2f}ms  (clock64 critical-path per phase, 1 step)", flush=True)
70	    for n, c in zip(names, cyc):
71	        ms = c / (sm_ghz * 1e9) * 1e3
72	        print(f"   {n:14s}: {c:>14d} cyc  ~{ms:8.3f} ms  {100.0*c/tot:5.1f}% of summed-phase cyc", flush=True)
73	    print(f"   {'SUM':14s}: {tot:>14d} cyc  ~{tot/(sm_ghz*1e9)*1e3:8.3f} ms", flush=True)
74	    print(f"[vit-phase] DOMINANT = {names[cyc.index(max(cyc))]} ({100.0*max(cyc)/tot:.1f}%)", flush=True)
75	    if hasattr(mod, "tc_profile_head_read"):
76	        head = mod.tc_profile_head_read()
77	        hf = head[0] / (sm_ghz * 1e9) * 1e3
78	        hb = head[1] / (sm_ghz * 1e9) * 1e3
79	        print(f"[vit-phase] per-sample HEAD/CE loops (SUBSET of P1): "
80	              f"fwd_head ~{hf:.3f}ms (of P1_fwd {cyc[0]/(sm_ghz*1e9)*1e3:.1f}ms), "
81	              f"bwd_head ~{hb:.3f}ms (of P1_bwd {cyc[1]/(sm_ghz*1e9)*1e3:.1f}ms)", flush=True)
82	
83	
84	if __name__ == "__main__":
85	    main()

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Stage-5 AMDGCN device-code compile gate (no hipcc / no ROCm device-libs).
3	#
4	# clang 18's AMDGPU backend compiles free-standing gfx942 device code, which
5	# catches real builtin-signature / DPP-control / MFMA-register-type bugs that
6	# structural review misses. Caught during Stage 5 bring-up:
7	#   * the bf16 MFMA `_1k` builtins take bf16x4 (short4), NOT u32x4 (the former
8	#     in-repo reference was wrong and would not have compiled on hipcc);
9	#   * cvt_f32_fp8 / mov_dpp / ds_swizzle / sched_group_barrier byte-select /
10	#     dpp-ctrl / mask args must be COMPILE-TIME CONSTANTS.
11	#
12	# It gates the DEVICE intrinsics, not the ATen/torch host glue (the `.hip.cpp`
13	# thin TUs go through the host compiler; full link is hardware-gated on MI300X).
14	#
15	# Usage:
16	#   scripts/amdgcn_check.sh --header <device_header.hip.hpp>   # compile a header
17	#   scripts/amdgcn_check.sh <free_standing_snippet.cpp>        # compile a snippet
18	set -u
19	ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"; cd "$ROOT"
20	
21	# Minimal HIP stubs so device headers that #include <hip/...> resolve under the
22	# free-standing amdgcn target (these only provide __device__/__forceinline__
23	# and uint32_t; the real types come from ROCm on a hipcc build).
24	STUB="$(mktemp -d)/hip"; mkdir -p "$STUB"
25	cat > "$STUB/hip_runtime.h" <<'EOF'
26	#pragma once
27	typedef unsigned int uint32_t;
28	#ifndef __device__
29	#define __device__
30	#endif
31	#ifndef __forceinline__
32	#define __forceinline__ inline __attribute__((always_inline))
33	#endif
34	EOF
35	printf '#pragma once\n' > "$STUB/hip_bf16.h"
36	printf '#pragma once\n' > "$STUB/hip_fp16.h"
37	# Minimal hip_fp16/bf16 type + cstdint/cmath shims so the pre-existing
38	# common_gfx942.hip.hpp (which uses real ROCm __half/__hip_bfloat16 types) can
39	# also be parsed by the free-standing gate. Under real hipcc these come from
40	# ROCm; here we provide just enough surface for the device code to type-check.
41	cat >> "$STUB/hip_fp16.h" <<'EOF'
42	struct __half { unsigned short x; __half()=default; __device__ __half(float f){ x=(unsigned short)(__builtin_bit_cast(unsigned,f)>>16); } __device__ operator float() const { return __builtin_bit_cast(float, (unsigned)x << 16); } };
43	static inline __attribute__((always_inline)) float __half2float(__half h){ return __builtin_bit_cast(float, (unsigned)h.x << 16); }
44	static inline __attribute__((always_inline)) __half __float2half(float f){ __half h; h.x = (unsigned short)(__builtin_bit_cast(unsigned, f) >> 16); return h; }
45	static inline __attribute__((always_inline)) __half __float2half_rn(float f){ return __float2half(f); }
46	EOF
47	cat >> "$STUB/hip_bf16.h" <<'EOF'
48	struct __hip_bfloat16 { unsigned short x; __hip_bfloat16()=default; __device__ __hip_bfloat16(float f){ x=(unsigned short)(__builtin_bit_cast(unsigned,f)>>16); } __device__ operator float() const { return __builtin_bit_cast(float, (unsigned)x << 16); } };
49	typedef __hip_bfloat16 hip_bfloat16;  // older ROCm spelling used by some headers
50	static inline __attribute__((always_inline)) float __bfloat162float(__hip_bfloat16 h){ return __builtin_bit_cast(float, (unsigned)h.x << 16); }
51	static inline __attribute__((always_inline)) __hip_bfloat16 __float2bfloat16(float f){ __hip_bfloat16 h; h.x = (unsigned short)(__builtin_bit_cast(unsigned, f) >> 16); return h; }
52	EOF
53	# common_gfx942.hip.hpp includes the longer spelling <hip/hip_bfloat16.h>.
54	cp "$STUB/hip_bf16.h" "$STUB/hip_bfloat16.h"
55	# cstdint/cmath are absent on the free-standing target; provide a tiny subset.
56	mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STUB")/_cxx"
57	cat > "$(dirname "$STUB")/_cxx/cstdint" <<'EOF'
58	#pragma once
59	typedef unsigned char uint8_t; typedef signed char int8_t;
60	typedef unsigned short uint16_t; typedef short int16_t;
61	typedef unsigned int uint32_t; typedef int int32_t;
62	typedef unsigned long long uint64_t; typedef long long int64_t;
63	EOF
64	cat > "$(dirname "$STUB")/_cxx/cmath" <<'EOF'
65	#pragma once
66	static inline float sqrtf(float x){ return __builtin_sqrtf(x); }
67	static inline float expf(float x){ return __builtin_expf(x); }
68	static inline float fabsf(float x){ return __builtin_fabsf(x); }
69	static inline float fmaxf(float a,float b){ return __builtin_fmaxf(a,b); }
70	static inline float fminf(float a,float b){ return __builtin_fminf(a,b); }
71	static inline float tanhf(float x){ return __builtin_tanhf(x); }
72	static inline float copysignf(float a,float b){ return __builtin_copysignf(a,b); }
73	static inline float truncf(float x){ return __builtin_truncf(x); }
74	static inline float floorf(float x){ return __builtin_floorf(x); }
75	EOF
76	
77	FLAGS=(--target=amdgcn-amd-amdhsa -mcpu=gfx942 -nogpulib -std=c++17
78	       -Wno-unused-function -I"$(dirname "$STUB")" -I"$(dirname "$STUB")/_cxx" -I.
79	       "-D__hip_atomic_fetch_add(a,b,c,d)=__atomic_fetch_add(a,b,c)"
80	       "-D__hip_atomic_load(a,b,c)=__atomic_load_n(a,b)"
81	       -D__HIP_MEMORY_SCOPE_AGENT=0 -D__HIP_MEMORY_SCOPE_WORKGROUP=0)
82	
83	LOG="$(mktemp)"
84	if [ "${1:-}" = "--header" ]; then
85	  HDR="${2:?usage: amdgcn_check.sh --header <header>}"
86	  clang "${FLAGS[@]}" -c "$HDR" -o /dev/null 2> "$LOG"
87	elif [ "${1:-}" = "--cell" ]; then
88	  # Full fused .hip cell: clang infers HIP language from the .hip extension and
89	  # then errors ("unsupported architecture amdgcn for host compilation"). Force
90	  # C++ language mode so the amdgcn device pass type-checks the forced template
91	  # instantiation block (the host hipLaunchKernelGGL block is #if'd out under
92	  # the bare amdgcn target — __HIPCC__ is undefined here).
93	  CELL="${2:?usage: amdgcn_check.sh --cell <cell.hip>}"
94	  clang "${FLAGS[@]}" -x c++ -c "$CELL" -o /dev/null 2> "$LOG"
95	elif [ "${1:-}" = "--emit-obj" ]; then
96	  # Emit a REAL gfx942 ELF object (NOT a PCH) for emitted-ISA profiling:
97	  # disassemble with llvm-objdump for v_mfma / DPP, read VGPR/SGPR/LDS from the
98	  # kernel descriptor with llvm-readobj. -x c++ forces a translation unit so a
99	  # .hip.hpp header emits its __global__ kernels as code, not a precompiled
100	  # header. -O3 so the matrix builtins lower to real v_mfma.
101	  SRC="${2:?usage: amdgcn_check.sh --emit-obj <src> <out.o>}"
102	  OUT="${3:?usage: amdgcn_check.sh --emit-obj <src> <out.o>}"
103	  clang "${FLAGS[@]}" -x c++ -O3 \
104	    -Wno-pragma-once-outside-header -Wno-unknown-attributes \
105	    -c "$SRC" -o "$OUT" 2> "$LOG"
106	else
107	  SRC="${1:?usage: amdgcn_check.sh <snippet.cpp> | --header <h> | --cell <c.hip>}"
108	  clang "${FLAGS[@]}" -c "$SRC" -o /dev/null 2> "$LOG"
109	fi
110	RC=$?
111	if [ "$RC" -ne 0 ]; then echo "AMDGCN_FAIL rc=$RC ${2:-$1}"; head -40 "$LOG";
112	else echo "AMDGCN_OK ${2:-$1}"; fi
113	rm -f "$LOG"; exit "$RC"
114

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# One-shot restore of the full working env on a FRESH runpod instance.
3	#
4	# The /workspace NFS volume is PERSISTENT; the container root (/usr, pip
5	# site-packages, /usr/local/bin, /dev/shm) is EPHEMERAL and wiped on restart.
6	# This script rebuilds the ephemeral pieces FROM the volume so a restart is one
7	# command back to working. Idempotent: warm-volume steps are no-ops on re-run.
8	#
9	#   usage:  bash /workspace/SuperGrok1.5/scripts/bootstrap_env.sh
10	#           then open a new shell (or: source ~/.supergrok_env)
11	set -euo pipefail
12	
13	VENV=/workspace/venv
14	PROJ=/workspace/SuperGrok1.5
15	SCCACHE_BIN_DIR=/workspace/.local/bin
16	export PIP_CACHE_DIR=/workspace/.cache/pip
17	mkdir -p "$PIP_CACHE_DIR" "$SCCACHE_BIN_DIR"
18	
19	# (1) Persistent venv on the volume, inheriting the image's torch/CUDA/numpy.
20	#     --system-site-packages keeps the image torch 2.4.1+cu124 that _ops.so is
21	#     ABI-linked against; new deps install into the venv (on the volume).
22	if [[ ! -x "$VENV/bin/python" ]]; then
23	  echo "bootstrap: creating venv (--system-site-packages) at $VENV"
24	  python3 -m venv --system-site-packages "$VENV"
25	fi
26	# shellcheck disable=SC1091
27	source "$VENV/bin/activate"
28	python -m pip install --quiet --upgrade pip
29	
30	# (2) Sanity: inherited torch MUST be the image's CUDA build, untouched.
31	python - <<'PY'
32	import torch, numpy
33	assert torch.__version__.startswith("2.4.1+cu124"), torch.__version__
34	assert numpy.__version__ == "1.26.3", numpy.__version__
35	print("inherited torch/cuda/numpy OK:", torch.__version__, "| cuda", torch.cuda.is_available(), "| numpy", numpy.__version__)
36	PY
37	
38	# (3) Reinstall pip-added deps INTO the venv (fast: warm pip cache on the volume).
39	bash "$PROJ/scripts/install_deps.sh"
40	
41	# (4) sccache binary on the volume (compile.py's _sccache_env wraps nvcc + host CC).
42	if ! command -v sccache >/dev/null 2>&1 && [[ ! -x "$SCCACHE_BIN_DIR/sccache" ]]; then
43	  echo "bootstrap: fetching sccache to $SCCACHE_BIN_DIR"
44	  ver=v0.8.2; pkg=sccache-$ver-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl
45	  curl -fsSL "https://github.com/mozilla/sccache/releases/download/$ver/$pkg.tar.gz" \
46	    | tar xz -C /tmp && install -m755 "/tmp/$pkg/sccache" "$SCCACHE_BIN_DIR/sccache"
47	fi
48	export PATH="$SCCACHE_BIN_DIR:$PATH"
49	
50	# (5) Build/runtime env vars (recreates ephemeral /dev/shm scratch dirs).
51	#     SCCACHE_DIR stays on /dev/shm by design (fast; sccache-on-NFS locking is
52	#     unsafe). Warm incremental rebuilds come from TORCH_EXTENSIONS_DIR (on volume).
53	source "$PROJ/.regpressure/env.sh"
54	
55	# (6) Ensure the extension imports; rebuild in-place ONLY if the .so is gone.
56	#     (build/ + _ops.so persist on the volume, so this is normally a no-op.)
57	cd "$PROJ"
58	if ! python -c "from grokking_optimizers import _ops" 2>/dev/null; then
59	  echo "bootstrap: _ops missing -> rebuilding in-place (pip install -e .)"
60	  pip install -e . --no-build-isolation
61	fi
62	
63	# (7) Convenience: auto-activate in new shells (re-established each bootstrap;
64	#     ~/.bashrc is ephemeral, so the authoritative copy is this script on the volume).
65	cat > ~/.supergrok_env <<EOF
66	source $VENV/bin/activate
67	export PATH="$SCCACHE_BIN_DIR:\$PATH"
68	source $PROJ/.regpressure/env.sh
69	EOF
70	grep -q supergrok_env ~/.bashrc 2>/dev/null || echo "source ~/.supergrok_env" >> ~/.bashrc
71	
72	echo "bootstrap complete: venv active, deps present, sccache on PATH, _ops importable."
73

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# SuperGrok1.5 -- COMPREHENSIVE dependency installer. NOTHING here is optional:
3	# every dependency the codebase references (verified by a line-by-line audit of
4	# all 393 source files) is installed -- or, for the AMD/TPU runtimes that cannot
5	# physically run on this NVIDIA H100 box, documented as a target-conditional
6	# section so the file is complete for ANY hardware.
7	#
8	# Persistence model (runpod): /workspace is PERSISTENT; the container root
9	# (/usr, system pip site-packages, /usr/local/bin, /dev/shm) is EPHEMERAL.
10	#   - pip packages   -> the /workspace venv (scripts/bootstrap_env.sh creates it) so they persist
11	#   - sccache binary -> /workspace/.local/bin (persists)
12	#   - apt system tools -> ephemeral root (this script re-installs them on a fresh instance)
13	# Run INSIDE the /workspace venv (bootstrap_env.sh activates it first).
14	set -euo pipefail
15	
16	PIP_CACHE_DIR="${PIP_CACHE_DIR:-/workspace/.cache/pip}"; export PIP_CACHE_DIR; mkdir -p "$PIP_CACHE_DIR"
17	SCCACHE_BIN_DIR="${SCCACHE_BIN_DIR:-/workspace/.local/bin}"; mkdir -p "$SCCACHE_BIN_DIR"
18	
19	# ── 1. SYSTEM build/inspection tools (apt; ephemeral root) ───────────────────
20	#   ccache    : host C/C++ compile cache (compile.py _sccache_env CC/CXX masquerade)
21	#   cmake     : compile.py CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL + general build glue
22	#   clang+llvm: RUNS scripts/amdgcn_check.sh (gfx942 device-code gate via LLVM's
23	#               AMDGPU target -- compiles on NVIDIA, no AMD GPU needed); provides
24	#               llvm-objdump / llvm-readobj; backs the libclang polyhedral layer
25	#   lld       : LLVM linker used by the amdgcn gate
26	if command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then
27	  export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
28	  apt-get update -qq || true
29	  apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ccache cmake clang lld llvm || true
30	fi
31	
32	# ── 2. sccache (Rust binary; compile.py wraps nvcc + host CC for cross-build caching) ──
33	#   REQUIRED for build performance: autotune sweeps recompile many variants.
34	if ! command -v sccache >/dev/null 2>&1 && [[ ! -x "$SCCACHE_BIN_DIR/sccache" ]]; then
35	  ver=v0.8.2; pkg=sccache-$ver-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl
36	  curl -fsSL "https://github.com/mozilla/sccache/releases/download/$ver/$pkg.tar.gz" \
37	    | tar xz -C /tmp && install -m755 "/tmp/$pkg/sccache" "$SCCACHE_BIN_DIR/sccache"
38	fi
39	export PATH="$SCCACHE_BIN_DIR:$PATH"
40	
41	# ── 3. PIP -- everything the codebase imports (into the active venv) ──────────
42	#   numpy is FROZEN to torch 2.4.1's build version; NEVER reinstall torch/torchvision.
43	python -m pip install --no-input "numpy==1.26.3" "ninja>=1.11" \
44	  "optuna>=3.4,<5" "tqdm>=4.66,<5" "matplotlib>=3.7,<4" \
45	  "xgboost>=2.0,<3" "scikit-learn>=1.5,<2" "joblib>=1.3" "pynvml>=11.5,<12" "prodigyopt" \
46	  "psutil>=5.9" "requests>=2.31" "PyYAML>=6" "jinja2>=3.1,<4" \
47	  pytest codespell ruff yamllint
48	
49	# compile.py advanced codegen routes (NVRTC / polyhedral / CUTLASS-python autotune):
50	#   cuda-python pinned to 12.x toolkit; libclang+islpy = polyhedral; nvidia-cutlass PINNED to
51	#   3.6.0 to match the v3.6.0 C++ submodule (provides compile.py's `import cutlass`; 4.x renamed it cutlass_library).
52	python -m pip install --no-input "cuda-python>=12.2,<13" "libclang>=16,<19" islpy "nvidia-cutlass==3.6.0" \
53	  || echo "WARN: a codegen extra failed (cuda-python/libclang/islpy/nvidia-cutlass) -- verify individually below"
54	
55	# distributed support probed by grokking_optimizers/distributed.py (heavy; probe-only -> non-fatal):
56	python -m pip install --no-input deepspeed \
57	  || echo "WARN: deepspeed install failed (non-fatal; only probed via find_spec, never imported)"
58	
59	# Pallas (TPU) parity test runs in JAX interpret mode -> CPU jaxlib suffices.
60	# NEVER install jax[cuda]/jaxlib-cuda: it shadows torch's bundled CUDA 12.4 and breaks _ops.
61	python -m pip install --no-input "jax[cpu]>=0.4,<0.5"
62	
63	# ── 4. HARDWARE-GATED runtimes -- RETAINED in the codebase, NOT runnable on this
64	#      NVIDIA H100 box. Install on the matching hardware target:
65	#
66	#   AMD/ROCm (gfx942 / MI300X) HIP RUNTIME -- only on an AMD-GPU instance (~GBs):
67	#     apt-get install -y rocm-hip-sdk rocblas hipcub rocprim rocthrust amd-smi-lib rocprofiler
68	#     pip install hip-python composable-kernel        # hipRTC bindings + CK GEMM emitter
69	#     # (clang/llvm in section 1 already runs the compile-only amdgcn_check.sh gate here.)
70	#
71	#   Google TPU (v6e / v5p) -- only on a TPU host:
72	#     pip install "jax[tpu]" -f https://storage.googleapis.com/jax-releases/libtpu_releases.html
73	#
74	#   Nsight Systems (nsys, system profiler) -- via the CUDA repo / NVIDIA installer:
75	#     apt-get install -y nsight-systems-cli      # (ncu/Nsight Compute already ships in the toolkit)
76	
77	echo "comprehensive deps installed. torch/numpy untouched; sccache+ccache+clang present."

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Stage 0 verification gate: every sm_90 TU must compile to object, self-test
3	# must stay 156/0 (or better), ruff clean. Prints one PASS/FAIL line per check.
4	set -u

464	def record_screen_gate(model: str, context: str, screen_verdict: str, gate_verdict: str,
465	                       *, candidate_defines: list[str] | None = None,
466	                       baseline_defines: list[str] | None = None,
467	                       note: str = "", ledger_path: Path = AGREEMENT_LEDGER) -> dict:
468	    """Append ONE row to the screen-vs-gate agreement JSONL ledger.
469	
470	    CALL THIS whenever a screen-SURVIVOR later clears (or fails) the full fp64+3-seed gate,
471	    from whichever context ran the screen (model-triage / compile.py / Level-2). It is the
472	    standing record of whether the cheap screen AGREED with the authoritative gate.
473	
474	      screen_verdict : the SCREEN's directional call — "better" | "worse" | "neutral"
475	                       (fast_triage's verdict_wall) | "irrelevant".
476	      gate_verdict   : the full gate's authoritative call — "kept" | "reverted"
477	                       (parity-clean + faster on 3 seeds => kept; else reverted) | "failed"
478	                       (parity/determinism RED — a correctness fail the screen cannot see).
479	
480	    `agreed` is TRUE iff the screen's direction matched the gate's outcome:
481	        screen 'better'  agrees with gate 'kept';
482	        screen 'worse'/'neutral'/'irrelevant' agrees with gate 'reverted'/'failed'.
483	    A screen-said-better that the gate REVERTED/FAILED is a FALSE POSITIVE (the costly error
484	    this screen exists to bound). Returns the row dict (also appended to the JSONL).
485	
486	    NOTE ON FALSE NEGATIVES: this ledger naturally captures only SURVIVORS (screen passed →
487	    gate ran), so it estimates the FALSE-POSITIVE rate well but UNDER-counts FALSE NEGATIVES
488	    (screen-said-worse that the gate would have KEPT). Estimating the false-negative rate
489	    requires occasionally GATING A SCREEN-REJECT on purpose and recording it here too."""
490	    screen_verdict = str(screen_verdict).lower()
491	    gate_verdict = str(gate_verdict).lower()
492	    agreed = ((screen_verdict == "better" and gate_verdict == "kept") or
493	              (screen_verdict in ("worse", "neutral", "irrelevant")
494	               and gate_verdict in ("reverted", "failed")))
495	    false_positive = (screen_verdict == "better" and gate_verdict in ("reverted", "failed"))
496	    row = {
497	        "ts": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
498	        "model": model,
499	        "context": context,
500	        "screen_verdict": screen_verdict,
501	        "gate_verdict": gate_verdict,
502	        "agreed": agreed,
503	        "false_positive": false_positive,
504	        "candidate_defines": candidate_defines or [],
505	        "baseline_defines": baseline_defines or [],
506	        "note": note,
507	    }
508	    ledger_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
509	    with open(ledger_path, "a") as f:
510	        f.write(json.dumps(row) + "\n")
511	    return row

531	    """Summarise running screen fidelity per (model, context) from the agreement ledger:
532	    sample count, AGREEMENT rate, and FALSE-POSITIVE rate (screen-said-better, gate-said-
533	    worse — the costly error). A rising disagreement rate for a context = the screen is
534	    DRIFTING there → surfaced. Prints a table; returns the per-key summary dict."""

560	        for key in sorted(summ):

562	            ar = f"{100*s['agreement_rate']:.0f}" if s["agreement_rate"] is not None else "—"
563	            fp = f"{100*s['false_positive_rate']:.0f}" if s["false_positive_rate"] is not None else "—"
564	            print(f"  {key:28s} {s['n']:>4d} {ar:>7s}% {fp:>6s}%", flush=True)
565	        print("\n  Rising disagreement (falling agree%) for a context = the screen is "
566	              "DRIFTING there → re-calibrate that (model,context).", flush=True)
567	        print("  NOTE: this ledger sees SURVIVORS, so FP% is well-estimated but the "
568	              "false-NEGATIVE rate is under-counted (gate a screen-reject to estimate it).",
569	              flush=True)
570	    out = {"ledger": str(ledger_path), "n_total": len(rows), "by_context": summ}

577	#    time it, print a single TRIAGE_RESULT JSON line. Driven via `python -c`, the
578	#    tune_optimizers.py:645 persistent-subprocess idiom (one warm context per variant).
579	#    `{bench}` is the coexisting bench module (tuning.decoder_bench | tuning.vit_bench |
580	#    tuning.mamba_bench). decoder/vit expose build_variant(d, profile=True, defines=…)/
581	#    measure(…, profile=True, ncta_cap=…)->res["phase_cycles"]; the WALL-ONLY Mamba bench
582	#    (`{wall_only}=True`) has the plainer build_variant(d, defines=…)/measure(mod,d,B,reps,
583	#    warmup,iters) with NO profiler — the worker branches on `{wall_only}` to call the right
584	#    signature and emits phase_cycles=None (direction-only). `{profile_macro}` labels the
585	#    HAS_PROFILE assert message (per-phase models only).
586	_WORKER = r"""
587	import json, sys
588	from pathlib import Path
589	ROOT = Path({root!r})
590	sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
591	import {bench} as db
592

595	wall_only = {wall_only}

597	    if wall_only:

599	        mod = db.build_variant(d, defines=defines)
600	        assert int(mod.D) == d, "TU D=%d != %d" % (int(mod.D), d)
601	        res = db.measure(mod, d, B, reps=reps, warmup=warmup, iters=iters)
602	        phase_cycles = None
603	    else:
604	        mod = db.build_variant(d, profile=True, defines=defines)
605	        assert int(mod.D) == d, "TU D=%d != %d" % (int(mod.D), d)
606	        assert getattr(mod, "HAS_PROFILE", False), "variant built without -D{profile_macro}"
607	        res = db.measure(mod, d, B, reps=reps, warmup=warmup, iters=iters,
608	                         profile=True, ncta_cap=ncta)
609	        phase_cycles = res.get("phase_cycles")
610	    out = {{
611	        "ok": True,
612	        "wall_ms": res["wall_ms"],
613	        "walls_ms": res.get("walls_ms", []),
614	        "achieved_tf_s": res["achieved_tf_s"],
615	        "phase_cycles": phase_cycles,
616	        "total_params": res["total_params"],
617	        "tile_n": int(getattr(mod, "TILE_N", 0)),
618	    }}
619	except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001

743	              f"({wall_delta:+.1f}%, {wall_v};  {wall_speedup:.3f}× speedup)", flush=True)
744	        print(f"\n  TRIAGE: step {wall_v} by {abs(wall_delta):.1f}% ({wall_speedup:.2f}×) "

746	              f"the wall is the sole signal).", flush=True)
747	        print("  NOTE: triage only — NOT a KEEP. The fp64 parity + A/A/A gate + 3-seed "
748	              "timing remain the arbiter.", flush=True)

765	    bp = base["phase_cycles"]

767	    bt, ct = sum(bp) or 1, sum(cp) or 1
768	    print(f"  params={base['total_params']:,}  TILE_N={base.get('tile_n', '?')}", flush=True)
769	    print(f"  baseline wall={base['wall_ms']:.3f} ms ({base['achieved_tf_s']:.3f} TF/s)   "

793	    # phase-share = the targeted phase's fraction of the profiled step. The STEP can move

796	    #   max plausible step gain = −phase_share          (phase → 0)

798	    # its local Δ looks (the canonical trap: vec4-AdamW was bench-faster on a P3 tail that

813	                                f"{projected_step_pct:+.1f}% → likely hurt another phase")

816	          f"({phase_delta:+.1f}%, {phase_v})", flush=True)
817	    print(f"  total step (wall):         {base['wall_ms']:.3f} -> {cand['wall_ms']:.3f} ms  "
818	          f"({wall_delta:+.1f}%, {wall_v};  {wall_speedup:.3f}× speedup)", flush=True)
819	    print(f"  RELEVANCE: {phase} = {b_share:.1f}% of step (floor {relevance_floor:.1f}%) → "

823	    if not consistent:
824	        print(f"  ⚠ INCONSISTENT: {consistency_note}.", flush=True)
825	
826	    # REPRESENTATIVENESS ASSERTION (additive) — assert this run measures the SAME problem
827	    # the calibration was taken on (real scale + phase-share drift), FLAG loudly on drift.
828	    # Only runs when the caller threaded `args` in; legacy callers skip it untouched.
829	    representativeness = None
830	    if args is not None:
831	        representativeness = _assert_representative(base, cand, phase, phase_names, args, calib)
832	
833	    # one-line verdict — STEP-LEVEL first (the decision), gated by relevance; the phase
834	    # delta is the mechanism, not the verdict. Lower ms = better; negative Δ% = improvement.
835	    if not relevant:
836	        headline = (f"TRIAGE: IRRELEVANT — {phase} is only {b_share:.1f}% of the step; "
837	                    f"its {phase_delta:+.1f}% projects to ≤{abs(max_step_gain_pct):.1f}% step. "
838	                    f"Not worth a full cycle (wall {wall_v} {abs(wall_delta):.1f}%).")
839	    else:
840	        headline = (f"TRIAGE: step {wall_v} by {abs(wall_delta):.1f}% ({wall_speedup:.2f}×); "
841	                    f"{phase} {phase_v} {abs(phase_delta):.1f}% [{b_share:.0f}% of step → "
842	                    f"projects {projected_step_pct:+.1f}%]"
843	                    + ("" if consistent else "  ⚠ wall<projected: side-effect"))
844	    print(f"\n  {headline}", flush=True)
845	    print("  NOTE: triage only — NOT a KEEP. The fp64 parity + A/A/A gate + 3-seed "
846	          "d=2048 timing remain the arbiter.", flush=True)
847	
848	    return {
849	        "verdict_phase": phase_v, "verdict_wall": wall_v,
850	        "targeted_phase": phase,
851	        "phase_share_pct": round(b_share, 2),
852	        "projected_step_pct": round(projected_step_pct, 2),

871	def _validate_entry(entry: dict, args, phase_names: list[str]) -> dict:
872	    """Run ONE calibration entry and judge whether the screen reproduced its recorded
873	    ground-truth. Returns {entry, faithful, direction_ok, magnitude_ok, magnitude_checked,
874	    summary, reason}. Faithful iff the recorded wall DIRECTION reproduces AND (where the
875	    entry has a per-phase ground-truth) the targeted-phase direction reproduces AND (at the
876	    measured scale) the wall speedup lands in the entry's magnitude window. A wall-only
877	    entry (phase=None) is judged on the WALL direction alone — no per-phase claim made."""
878	    model, context = entry["model"], entry["context"]
879	    phase = entry.get("phase")           # None => wall-only entry (no per-phase claim)
880	    wall_only = phase is None or _is_wall_only(model)
881	    expect_faster = entry.get("expect_wall_dir", "faster") == "faster"
882	    mag_window = entry.get("mag_window")
883	
884	    print("-" * 78, flush=True)
885	    print(f"[validate] {model}/{context}: {entry.get('desc','(no desc)')}", flush=True)
886	    print(f"  baseline  = {entry['baseline_defines'] or '(prod defaults)'}", flush=True)
887	    print(f"  candidate = {entry['candidate_defines'] or '(prod defaults)'}", flush=True)
888	    print(f"  expect: wall {entry.get('expect_wall_dir','faster')}"
889	          + ("" if wall_only else f", {phase} {entry.get('expect_phase_dir','faster')}")
890	          + (f", magnitude {mag_window} (only if at d>={entry['d']}/B>={entry['B']})"
891	             if mag_window else " (direction-only — no magnitude ground-truth)")
892	          + ("  [WALL-ONLY context: no per-phase claim]" if wall_only else ""),
893	          flush=True)
894	
895	    base = _run_variant(f"{model}:baseline", list(entry["baseline_defines"]), args)
896	    cand = _run_variant(f"{model}:candidate", list(entry["candidate_defines"]), args)
897	    # judge-phase for the report: the entry's phase, or a wall-anchored placeholder for
898	    # wall-only entries (P2_dW_GEMM exists in every table; its delta is reported but the
899	    # faithfulness verdict for a wall-only entry ignores it — wall is the sole arbiter).
900	    judge_phase = phase if (phase and phase in phase_names) else (
901	        "P2_dW_GEMM" if "P2_dW_GEMM" in phase_names else phase_names[0])
902	    summary = _report(base, cand, judge_phase, args.neutral_pct, args.relevance_floor,
903	                      phase_names, args=args, calib=entry)
904	
905	    if summary.get("verdict") == "BUILD_FAILED":
906	        return {"entry": entry, "faithful": None, "reason": "BUILD_FAILED",
907	                "direction_ok": None, "magnitude_ok": None, "magnitude_checked": False,
908	                "summary": summary}
909	
910	    wall_d = summary["wall_delta_pct"]
911	    speedup = summary["wall_speedup"]
912	    # DIRECTION: the wall must move the recorded way by more than the neutral band.
913	    if expect_faster:
914	        wall_dir_ok = wall_d < -args.neutral_pct
915	    else:
916	        wall_dir_ok = wall_d > args.neutral_pct
917	    # per-phase direction only where the entry makes a per-phase claim.
918	    if wall_only:
919	        phase_dir_ok = True
920	    else:
921	        phase_d = summary["phase_delta_pct"]
922	        phase_dir_ok = (phase_d < -args.neutral_pct) if (
923	            entry.get("expect_phase_dir", "faster") == "faster") else (phase_d > args.neutral_pct)
924	    direction_ok = wall_dir_ok and phase_dir_ok
925	
926	    # MAGNITUDE: only when the run is AT (or above) the scale the ground-truth was measured.
927	    mag_checked = (mag_window is not None and args.d >= entry["d"] and args.B >= entry["B"])
928	    mag_ok = True
929	    if mag_checked:
930	        lo, hi = mag_window
931	        # for a "slower" entry the recorded ratio is base/cand < 1; the window already
932	        # encodes that, so a direct containment check is correct either way.
933	        mag_ok = lo <= speedup <= hi
934	
935	    faithful = direction_ok and mag_ok
936	    return {"entry": entry, "faithful": faithful, "direction_ok": direction_ok,
937	            "magnitude_ok": mag_ok, "magnitude_checked": mag_checked,
938	            "wall_only": wall_only, "summary": summary, "reason": ""}
