941	def _do_validate(args) -> int:
942	    """CALIBRATION SUITE runner — prove the screen reproduces the KNOWN ground-truths for
943	    the selected (model, context) before it is TRUSTED there. Per-(model,context): the
944	    decoder dW result does NOT transfer to ViT/Mamba/Level-2; each must have its own entry.
945	
946	    Exit code:
947	      0 = all matching calibration entries reproduced (screen FAITHFUL for that context),
948	          OR (no entries but the context is direction-only-by-nature) — see below;
949	      2 = the screen reproduced a WRONG direction/magnitude for some entry (UNTRUSTWORTHY);

950	      1 = INCONCLUSIVE (a variant failed to build/run) OR UNCALIBRATED (no ground-truth for
951	          this (model,context) — the screen is "direction-only-untrusted" there).
952	
953	    Preserves the legacy decoder behaviour exactly: the seed entry (decoder/model-triage)
954	    reproduces the dW 2.05× check (exit 0 faithful / 2 wrong-direction), and --validate
955	    without --model still runs it."""
956	    model = getattr(args, "model", "decoder")
957	    context = getattr(args, "context", None)   # None => all contexts for the model
958	    entries = _calibration_for(model, context)
959	    phase_names = _MODELS[model]["phase_names"]
960	
961	    print("=" * 78, flush=True)
962	    ctx_lbl = context or "ALL contexts"
963	    print(f"[triage --validate] CALIBRATION SUITE — model={model} context={ctx_lbl}", flush=True)
964	    print(f"  scale = d={args.d} B={args.B} reps={args.reps}  "
965	          f"(at-or-above an entry's measured scale also checks its MAGNITUDE window; a "
966	          f"smaller --B is a faster DIRECTION-only smoke)", flush=True)
967	
968	    if not entries:
969	        # No measured ground-truth for this (model,context). Trust is NOT assumed: report
970	        # UNCALIBRATED loudly. This is the per-(model,context) firewall: the decoder
971	        # calibration does NOT make the screen trusted for ViT/Mamba/Level-2.
972	        wall_only = _is_wall_only(model)
973	        print("=" * 78, flush=True)
974	        print(f"[triage --validate] ⚠ UNCALIBRATED — no ground-truth entry for "
975	              f"{model}/{ctx_lbl}. The screen is DIRECTION-ONLY-UNTRUSTED here: it has "
976	              f"never been proven to reproduce a measured result in this context.", flush=True)
977	        if wall_only:
978	            print(f"  ({model} is WALL-ONLY — no per-phase profiler — so any future entry "
979	                  f"will be direction-only by construction.)", flush=True)
980	        print(f"  Known contexts: {_KNOWN_CONTEXTS}. Add a calibration entry (a measured "
981	              f"KEEP/REVERT for this model+context) to _CALIBRATION before relying on the "
982	              f"screen here. Until then: treat its verdict as a weak directional hint.",
983	              flush=True)
984	        print("=" * 78, flush=True)
985	        if args.json:
986	            print("TRIAGE_JSON " + json.dumps({"validate": "UNCALIBRATED", "model": model,
987	                                               "context": context, "wall_only": wall_only}),
988	                  flush=True)
989	        return 1
990	
991	    results = [_validate_entry(e, args, phase_names) for e in entries]
992	
993	    # aggregate verdict over the matching entries.
994	    any_build_fail = any(r["faithful"] is None and r.get("reason") == "BUILD_FAILED"
995	                         for r in results)
996	    judged = [r for r in results if r["faithful"] is not None]
997	    all_faithful = bool(judged) and all(r["faithful"] for r in judged)
998	
999	    print("\n" + "=" * 78, flush=True)
1000	    for r in results:
1001	        e = r["entry"]
1002	        tag = f"{e['model']}/{e['context']}"
1003	        if r["faithful"] is None:
1004	            print(f"[validate] {tag}: INCONCLUSIVE ({r.get('reason')}).", flush=True)
1005	            continue
1006	        s = r["summary"]
1007	        wo = " [wall-only]" if r.get("wall_only") else ""
1008	        if r["faithful"]:
1009	            magtxt = (f", magnitude {s['wall_speedup']:.2f}× in {e['mag_window']}"
1010	                      if r["magnitude_checked"] else " (direction-only at this scale)")
1011	            print(f"[validate] ✅ {tag}: FAITHFUL{wo} — wall {s['wall_delta_pct']:+.1f}% "
1012	                  f"({s['wall_speedup']:.2f}×){magtxt}.", flush=True)
1013	        else:
1014	            print(f"[validate] ❌ {tag}: UNFAITHFUL{wo} — "
1015	                  f"direction_ok={r['direction_ok']} magnitude_ok={r['magnitude_ok']}; "
1016	                  f"wall {s['wall_delta_pct']:+.1f}% ({s['wall_speedup']:.2f}×).", flush=True)
1017	
1018	    if any_build_fail and not judged:
1019	        print("\n[triage --validate] INCONCLUSIVE — variant(s) failed to build/run "
1020	              "(not a faithfulness verdict). Re-run with --verbose.", flush=True)
1021	        rc = 1
1022	    elif all_faithful:
1023	        print(f"\n[triage --validate] ✅ FAITHFUL: the screen reproduced ALL "
1024	              f"{len(judged)} calibration entr{'y' if len(judged)==1 else 'ies'} for "
1025	              f"{model}/{ctx_lbl}. Trusted for this context.", flush=True)
1026	        rc = 0
1027	    else:
1028	        print(f"\n[triage --validate] ❌ UNFAITHFUL: the screen did NOT reproduce a known "
1029	              f"ground-truth for {model}/{ctx_lbl}. UNTRUSTWORTHY here — investigate "
1030	              f"(profile build flag, phase-slot mapping, the candidate actually compiled "
1031	              f"the optimized path, stale bench-variant cache) before relying on it.",
1032	              flush=True)
1033	        rc = 2
1034	    print("=" * 78, flush=True)
1035	    if args.json:
1036	        out = {"validate": ("FAITHFUL" if rc == 0 else "UNFAITHFUL" if rc == 2
1037	                            else "INCONCLUSIVE"),
1038	               "model": model, "context": context, "n_entries": len(entries),
1039	               "entries": [{"model": r["entry"]["model"], "context": r["entry"]["context"],
1040	                            "faithful": r["faithful"], "direction_ok": r.get("direction_ok"),
1041	                            "magnitude_ok": r.get("magnitude_ok"),
1042	                            "magnitude_checked": r.get("magnitude_checked"),
1043	                            "wall_delta_pct": r["summary"].get("wall_delta_pct"),
1044	                            "wall_speedup": r["summary"].get("wall_speedup")}
1045	                           for r in results]}
1046	        print("TRIAGE_JSON " + json.dumps(out), flush=True)
1047	    return rc

# STAGE 3.0 PTX Audit: Redundancy Analysis

**Date:** 2026-06-01  
**Build Mode:** `--use_fast_math` enabled (setup.py:276, compile.py verified)  
**Scope:** All hand-written inline-PTX (`asm volatile`/`asm(`) blocks in the codebase

---

## Summary

With `--use_fast_math`, nvcc **automatically** lowers transcendental/approx operations to PTX:
- `expf(x)` → `ex2.approx.f32` (after log2(e) scale) in a single instruction
- `sqrtf(x)`, `rsqrtf(x)` → `sqrt.approx.f32`, `rsqrt.approx.f32`
- `logf(x)` → `lg2.approx.f32` (after bit tricks or trig)
- `tanhf(x)`, `__sincosf(x)` → approximate forms

Any hand-written PTX block that merely re-derives this is **REDUNDANT** (dead duplication).

**Key Finding:** Several functions in `ptx_intrinsics.cuh` are **defined but never called** (dead code).

---

## Detailed Audit

### 1. **softplus_ptx** — REDUNDANT (never called)
**Location:** `/home/user/SuperGrok1.5/csrc/common/ptx_intrinsics.cuh:70–87`

**PTX Opcodes (7):**
```ptx
mul.f32 t, %1, 0f3FB8AA3B;         # x * log2(e)
ex2.approx.f32 ex, t;               # exp(x)
add.f32 ep1, ex, 0f3F800000;        # 1 + exp(x)
lg2.approx.f32 lg, ep1;             # log2(1+exp(x))
mul.f32 lg, lg, 0f3F317218;         # * ln(2)
setp.gt.f32 p, %1, 0f41A00000;      # x > 20?
selp.f32 %0, %1, lg, p;             # branchless select
```

**Equivalent libm:** `logf(1.0f + expf(x))` with saturation at x > 20

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Parse ptxas -v output (nvcc --resource-usage logs) into a per-kernel table."""
3	import re, sys, subprocess
4	
5	def demangle(name):
6	    try:
7	        out = subprocess.run(["c++filt", name], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
8	        return out or name
9	    except Exception:
10	        return name
11	
12	def shorten(dem):
13	    # sg::fused::sm90::fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<(sg::fused::sm90::OptId)0>(...) ->
14	    # fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<Opt0>
15	    m = re.search(r"(?:sg::fused::sm90::)?(\w+)<\(sg::fused::sm90::OptId\)(\d+)>", dem)
16	    if m:
17	        return f"{m.group(1)}<OptId={m.group(2)}>"
18	    m = re.search(r"(?:sg::fused::sm90::)?(\w+)(?:<|\()", dem)
19	    return m.group(1) if m else dem[:80]
20	
21	OPT = {0:"AdamW",1:"Lion",2:"Grokfast",3:"GrokAdamW",4:"LookSAM",5:"Prodigy",
22	       6:"NeuralGrok",7:"Muon",8:"SuperGrok11",9:"SuperGrok15",10:"SuperGrok2"}
23	
24	def parse(path):
25	    txt = open(path).read()
26	    # blocks: "ptxas info    : Compiling entry function '<mangled>' for 'sm_90a'"
27	    # then Function properties line(s): N bytes stack frame, N bytes spill stores, N bytes spill loads
28	    # then Used N registers, [used M barriers,] N bytes smem...
29	    rows = []
30	    blocks = re.split(r"ptxas info\s+: Compiling entry function '", txt)
31	    for b in blocks[1:]:
32	        m = re.match(r"([^']+)' for 'sm_90a'", b)
33	        if not m: continue
34	        mangled = m.group(1)
35	        stack = spst = spld = 0
36	        fp = re.search(r"(\d+) bytes stack frame, (\d+) bytes spill stores, (\d+) bytes spill loads", b)
37	        if fp:
38	            stack, spst, spld = map(int, fp.groups())
39	        ur = re.search(r"Used (\d+) registers(?:, used (\d+) barriers)?", b)
40	        regs = int(ur.group(1)) if ur else -1
41	        sm = re.search(r"(\d+) bytes smem", b)
42	        smem = int(sm.group(1)) if sm else 0
43	        cm = re.search(r"(\d+) bytes cmem\[0\]", b)
44	        cmem = int(cm.group(1)) if cm else 0
45	        rows.append(dict(mangled=mangled, stack=stack, spill_st=spst, spill_ld=spld,
46	                         regs=regs, smem=smem, cmem=cmem))
47	    return rows
48	
49	def optname(short):
50	    m = re.search(r"OptId=(\d+)", short)
51	    if m: return OPT.get(int(m.group(1)), short)
52	    return ""
53	
54	if __name__ == "__main__":
55	    for path in sys.argv[1:]:
56	        rows = parse(path)
57	        print(f"\n### {path}")
58	        print(f"{'kernel':58s} {'opt':12s} {'regs':>4s} {'stack':>6s} {'sp_st':>6s} {'sp_ld':>6s} {'smem':>7s}")
59	        for r in rows:
60	            dem = demangle(r["mangled"])
61	            s = shorten(dem)
62	            print(f"{s:58s} {optname(s):12s} {r['regs']:4d} {r['stack']:6d} {r['spill_st']:6d} {r['spill_ld']:6d} {r['smem']:7d}")

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""ptxas -v parser v2: attributes callee (ABI device fn) spills to their entry.
3	ptxas prints, per entry section: the callee Function properties blocks, then
4	'Compiling entry function X', then X's properties + register count. Callee
5	blocks BEFORE an entry belong to that entry's compilation section."""
6	import re, sys, subprocess
7	
8	OPT = {0:"AdamW",1:"Lion",2:"Grokfast",3:"GrokAdamW",4:"LookSAM",5:"Prodigy",
9	       6:"NeuralGrok",7:"Muon",8:"SuperGrok11",9:"SuperGrok15",10:"SuperGrok2"}
10	
11	def parse(path):
12	    lines = open(path).read().splitlines()
13	    entries = []   # (optname, regs, smem, entry_st, entry_ld, callee_st, callee_ld, ncallee_spilling, entry_stack)
14	    pend_fns = []  # (name, stack, st, ld) callees seen since last entry
15	    cur = None
16	    i = 0
17	    while i < len(lines):
18	        ln = lines[i]
19	        m = re.search(r"Function properties for (\S+)", ln)
20	        if m:
21	            name = m.group(1)
22	            fp = re.search(r"(\d+) bytes stack frame, (\d+) bytes spill stores, (\d+) bytes spill loads", lines[i+1] if i+1 < len(lines) else "")
23	            st = ld = stk = 0
24	            if fp: stk, st, ld = map(int, fp.groups())
25	            if cur is not None and name == cur["mangled"]:
26	                cur["stack"], cur["st"], cur["ld"] = stk, st, ld
27	            elif cur is not None:
28	                cur["callees"].append((name, stk, st, ld))
29	            else:
30	                pend_fns.append((name, stk, st, ld))
31	            i += 1
32	        m = re.search(r"Compiling entry function '([^']+)' for 'sm_90a'", ln)
33	        if m:
34	            if cur is not None:
35	                entries.append(cur)
36	            cur = dict(mangled=m.group(1), regs=-1, smem=0, st=0, ld=0, stack=0,
37	                       callees=[])
38	            pend_fns = []
39	        m = re.search(r"Used (\d+) registers", ln)
40	        if m and cur is not None and cur["regs"] < 0:
41	            cur["regs"] = int(m.group(1))
42	            sm = re.search(r"(\d+) bytes smem", ln)
43	            if sm: cur["smem"] = int(sm.group(1))
44	        i += 1
45	    if cur is not None:
46	        entries.append(cur)
47	    return entries
48	
49	def optname(mangled):
50	    m = re.search(r"OptIdE?(\d+)", mangled)
51	    if m: return OPT.get(int(m.group(1)), "?")
52	    m = re.search(r"\)(\d+)EEE", mangled)
53	    return "?"
54	
55	if __name__ == "__main__":
56	    for path in sys.argv[1:]:
57	        print(f"\n### {path}")
58	        print(f"{'opt':12s} {'regs':>4s} {'entry_sp_st':>11s} {'callee_sp_st':>12s} {'TOTAL_st':>9s} {'TOTAL_ld':>9s} {'#spill_fns':>10s}")
59	        for e in parse(path):
60	            if "EmptyKernel" in e["mangled"]: continue
61	            cst = sum(f[2] for f in e["callees"]); cld = sum(f[3] for f in e["callees"])
62	            nsf = sum(1 for f in e["callees"] if f[2] or f[3])
63	            print(f"{optname(e['mangled']):12s} {e['regs']:4d} {e['st']:11d} {cst:12d} {e['st']+cst:9d} {e['ld']+cld:9d} {nsf:10d}")
64

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# compile_one.sh <src-root> <tu-rel-path> <out-tag> [extra flags...]
3	# Reproduces the PRODUCTION _ops nvcc device flag set for one TU and captures
4	# ptxas -v / --resource-usage to .regpressure/logs/<out-tag>.log (CPU-only).
5	#
6	# Production flag provenance (HEAD 642e360):
7	#   compile.py NVCC_DEVICE_BASE (lines 9334-9402)
8	#   + setup.py grokking project flags: --use_fast_math -DNDEBUG -lineinfo
9	#   + gencode sm_90a (PTX-fallback compute_90 omitted: no ptxas run for it,
10	#     so it cannot change the sm_90a resource numbers)
11	#   + -DWITH_CUDA define (cuda_define_macros) [already in base]
12	#   + include dirs: ROOT, ROOT/csrc/bindings, ROOT/csrc  (+ torch includes for
13	#     the JIT bench TUs that include <torch/extension.h>)
14	set -uo pipefail
15	ROOT="$1"; TU="$2"; TAG="$3"; shift 3
16	OUT=/workspace/SuperGrok1.5/.regpressure/logs

18	TORCH_INC1=/usr/local/lib/python3.11/dist-packages/torch/include
19	TORCH_INC2=/usr/local/lib/python3.11/dist-packages/torch/include/torch/csrc/api/include

22	  -O3 -std=c++17 -DWITH_CUDA \

24	  -Xfatbin -compress-all \

26	  -Xptxas -v -Xptxas --warn-on-spills \
27	  --extra-device-vectorization \
28	  -Xcompiler -fPIC -Xcompiler -fno-strict-aliasing \
29	  --resource-usage \
30	  --default-stream per-thread \
31	  --use_fast_math -DNDEBUG -lineinfo \
32	  -gencode=arch=compute_90a,code=sm_90a \
33	  -I"$ROOT" -I"$ROOT/csrc/bindings" -I"$ROOT/csrc" \
34	  -I"$TORCH_INC1" -I"$TORCH_INC2" -I"$PYTHON_INC" \
35	  "$@" > "$OUT/$TAG.log" 2>&1
36	RC=$?
37	echo "rc=$RC" >> "$OUT/$TAG.log"

1	"""prodtime.py — per-cell PRODUCTION step timing at the roofline operating point.
2	
3	Reuses tuning.roofline's exact machinery (_data_init, _tile_train_data, _cfg,
4	wall pass = discard-25 + diff(15, 15+timed)/timed) so the numbers are the same
5	quantity roofline.json records (wall_per_step_ms), but:
6	  * repeats the (15, 115) diff pair R times -> noise floor per cell
7	  * asserts EVERY l3 dispatch fired engine=="wgmma" (the wiring TRAP guard;
8	    a non-wgmma step aborts the cell measurement loudly)
9	  * no json clobber, no profiler/eval passes (timing only)
10	
11	Usage:
12	  python .regpressure/gpu/prodtime.py --models decoder --reps 3 \
13	      --out .regpressure/gpu/prod_decoder_baseline.json
14	"""
15	from __future__ import annotations
16	
17	import argparse
18	import json
19	import statistics
20	import sys
21	import time
22	from pathlib import Path
23	
24	ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
25	sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
26	sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "tuning"))
27	
28	import torch  # noqa: E402
29	
30	import tuning.roofline as R  # noqa: E402
31	
32	OPTS = ["adamw", "neuralgrok", "grokadamw", "supergrok", "supergrok15",
33	        "supergrok2", "grokfast", "muon", "lion", "looksam", "prodigy"]
34	
35	
36	def time_cell(opt: str, model: str, timed_steps: int, reps: int, max_batch: int):
37	    g = R._g()
38	    data, init, n_params = R._data_init(model)
39	    if max_batch:
40	        data = R._tile_train_data(data, max_batch)
41	    dev = torch.device("cuda")
42	    tuned = R._load_tuned_configs(model)
43	    # production race precision: bf16 pinned (the roofline default)
44	    mp_str, use_amp, prec_label = "bf16", False, "bf16"
45	
46	    counters = {"l3": 0, "bad_engine": 0}
47	    engines = set()
48	    orig_l3 = g._try_fused_train_step
49	
50	    def wrap_l3(*a, **k):
51	        r = orig_l3(*a, **k)
52	        if r is not None:
53	            counters["l3"] += 1
54	            if g.LAST_L3_ENGINE is not None:
55	                e = g.LAST_L3_ENGINE["engine"]
56	                engines.add(e)
57	                if e != "wgmma":
58	                    counters["bad_engine"] += 1
59	        return r
60	
61	    def cfgp(steps):
62	        c = R._cfg(opt, model, steps, 10**9)
63	        c["matmul_precision"] = mp_str
64	        c["use_amp"] = use_amp
65	        return c
66	
67	    fn = getattr(g, {
68	        "adamw": "train_adamw", "neuralgrok": "train_neuralgrok",
69	        "grokadamw": "train_grokadamw", "supergrok": "train_supergrok",
70	        "supergrok15": "train_supergrok15", "supergrok2": "train_supergrok2",
71	        "grokfast": "train_grokfast", "muon": "train_muon", "lion": "train_lion",
72	        "looksam": "train_looksam", "prodigy": "train_prodigy"}[opt])
73	
74	    g._try_fused_train_step = wrap_l3
75	    walls_ms = []
76	    expected_l3 = 0
77	    try:
78	        torch.manual_seed(42)
79	        fn(cfgp(25), init, *data, dev, bp=0)   # discard: one-time costs
80	        torch.cuda.synchronize()
81	        expected_l3 += 25
82	        for _ in range(reps):
83	            w = []
84	            for steps in (15, 15 + timed_steps):
85	                torch.manual_seed(42)
86	                torch.cuda.synchronize()
87	                t0 = time.perf_counter()
88	                fn(cfgp(steps), init, *data, dev, bp=0)
89	                torch.cuda.synchronize()
90	                w.append(time.perf_counter() - t0)
91	                expected_l3 += steps
92	            walls_ms.append((w[1] - w[0]) / timed_steps * 1e3)
93	    finally:
94	        g._try_fused_train_step = orig_l3
95	
96	    fired_all = (counters["l3"] == expected_l3)
97	    ok = fired_all and engines == {"wgmma"} and counters["bad_engine"] == 0
98	    return {
99	        "opt": opt, "model": model, "B": max_batch, "timed_steps": timed_steps,
100	        "walls_ms": walls_ms,
101	        "median_ms": statistics.median(walls_ms),
102	        "min_ms": min(walls_ms), "max_ms": max(walls_ms),
103	        "spread_ms": max(walls_ms) - min(walls_ms),
104	        "l3_fired": counters["l3"], "l3_expected": expected_l3,
105	        "engines": sorted(engines), "wgmma_every_step": ok,
106	    }
107	
108	
109	def main():
110	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
111	    ap.add_argument("--models", default="decoder")
112	    ap.add_argument("--opts", default=",".join(OPTS))
113	    ap.add_argument("--steps", type=int, default=100)
114	    ap.add_argument("--reps", type=int, default=3)
115	    ap.add_argument("--max-batch", type=int, default=16384)
116	    ap.add_argument("--out", default=None)
117	    args = ap.parse_args()
118	    rows = []
119	    for model in [m for m in args.models.split(",") if m]:
120	        for opt in [o for o in args.opts.split(",") if o]:
121	            try:
122	                r = time_cell(opt, model, args.steps, args.reps, args.max_batch)
123	            except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
124	                import traceback
125	                traceback.print_exc()
126	                r = {"opt": opt, "model": model, "error": str(e)}
127	            rows.append(r)
128	            if "error" in r:
129	                print(f"  {opt:11s}/{model:7s} FAILED: {r['error']}", flush=True)
130	            else:
131	                flag = "" if r["wgmma_every_step"] else "  ***NOT-WGMMA***"
132	                print(f"  {opt:11s}/{model:7s} median={r['median_ms']:9.3f} ms "
133	                      f"spread={r['spread_ms']:7.3f} ms "
134	                      f"walls={[f'{x:.3f}' for x in r['walls_ms']]}"
135	                      f" eng={r['engines']}{flag}", flush=True)
136	    if args.out:
137	        Path(args.out).write_text(json.dumps(rows, indent=1))
138	        print(f"[prodtime] wrote {args.out}", flush=True)
139	    bad = [r for r in rows if r.get("error") or not r.get("wgmma_every_step")]
140	    sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)
141	
142	
143	if __name__ == "__main__":
144	    main()

207	  in-loop state is ~8-16 registers (slot index, mbarrier phase, prefetch pointers;
208	  mbarrier objects live in smem, descriptors are remat-cheap). Evidence the engine can
209	  absorb it: (i) the single-pass cells absorb a **64-register** accumulator

213	  holds (under `--extra-device-vectorization` that window is ~8-16 wide), so the net

13	
14	Files: `csrc/fused/sm_90/model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh`,

19	   compile-time-selected branch (`if constexpr (kRingAsync)`) replaces the
20	   synchronous per-element staging TRANSPORT with 16-byte
21	   `cp.async.cg.shared.global` copies (the silicon-validated
22	   `primitives.cuh::cp_async_cg_16` + commit/wait + `fence_async_proxy`

26	   `__syncthreads` choreography are preserved VERBATIM — per k-step: wg0
27	   issues the group's wgmmas on slot k%S, ALL 256 threads fire tile k+1's
28	   copies into the other slot (2 LDGSTS/thread instead of ~16 dependent
29	   2-byte LDG→reg→STS pairs), then wgmma-wait + per-thread
30	   `cp_async_wait_group<0>` + ONE `fence.proxy.async` + the existing barrier.
31	   No mbarriers added (all 256 threads both produce and consume — the
32	   collective barrier IS the correct signal at prefetch distance 1; the
33	   warp-specialized mbarrier producer/consumer split is the documented next

48	   k-stride 2-byte gather no 4/8/16B cp.async can express (the same

52	   the SAM second pass re-converts both via the SAME call — no new barrier).
53	   WT[r,c] == W-cache[c,r] BIT-IDENTICALLY (same fp32 element through the

55	   UNCHANGED operand values. Cache cost: 786,432 B → 1,572,864 B at d=128;

166	
167	Removed stall: the synchronous staging window's REGISTER-MEDIATED 2-byte
168	element loop. Per k-step a CTA stages 8 KB (2 A-tiles + 1 B-tile); the old
169	transport was ~16 dependent LDG(2B)→reg→STS(2B) pairs per thread whose
170	long-scoreboard latency the allocator could only overlap ~8–16 loads deep
171	(Lane B's measured window); the ring issues 2 fire-and-forget
172	LDGSTS.E.BYPASS.128 per thread — the WHOLE tile is in flight concurrently,
173	zero register data path, ~94% fewer staging instructions (52→4 static
174	2-byte ops), and the copy flies while the wgmma group on the previous tile
175	executes. Secondary win: dX's weight staging was an uncoalesced k-strided
176	2-byte gather of W; from C1-T it is dense 16B-sector reads.

182	2. **L2-resident weights**: the 0.8–1.5 MB cache sits in L2 after first
183	   touch, so the latency the old path exposed was L2-hit latency partially

58	## DESIGN EQUATIONS — the invariants the shard math MUST satisfy (review checklist)
59	
60	1. **ABI (§0.2):** params/grad = flat `float[total]`, `total = Σ kDecSizes[i]` over 30 tensors, concat in `named_parameters()` order. state = `[m|v|extra]+loss`. `rebase_state<Opt>` only ADDS the per-tensor offset to per-element pointers — so flat index `i` pairs `params[i]↔grad[i]↔m[i]↔v[i]↔…` identically on the in-kernel and sharded paths.
61	2. **Decomposition (§2.1):** `[fwd+bwd]→reduce_scatter(grad)→[sharded-opt over owned shard]→all_gather(params)`. Each rank ends reduce-scatter with the reduced grad for ITS shard only; sharded-opt writes only its shard; all-gather re-replicates.
62	3. **B2 cut (§2.2):** ZeRO≥2 ⇒ kernel `if constexpr (Par::kShardOptGrad) return;` after B2; sharded-opt kernel is the tail. ZeRO≤1 ⇒ P3 in-kernel as today.
63	4. **Determinism (§2.7/§5.2/§6.4):** cross-rank reduction MUST be FIXED-ORDER (ascending rank/pe, fp32/fp64 accumulate) — the structural order, not timing. Mirrors the in-kernel ascending-CTA fp64 sum. NON-NEGOTIABLE for A/A/A.
64	5. **Per-tensor constraint (§0.4/§3.4):** muon/SG11/SG15/SG2 are per-TENSOR/per-MATRIX — a flat-element shard that splits a tensor across ranks BREAKS them ⇒ they require tensor-granular partition. Elementwise {adamw,lion,grokfast,+global-scalar cells} may use flat-even.
65	6. **TP geometry (§5.1):** attn in_proj/QKV column-parallel (3d/TP cols, head-aligned), out_proj row-parallel (d/TP rows), all-reduce after out_proj; ff0 col-parallel (d→dff), ff2 row-parallel (dff→d), all-reduce after ff2. Two all-reduces per layer. Backward mirrors with all-reduce on dX of the column-parallel pieces. dW shards are EXACT slices of the unsharded grad.
66	7. **Single-GPU guarantee (§1.2):** SingleGPU = ParConfig<1,1,1,1,Z0>, kEmitComm==false ⇒ every comm branch folds to zero code ⇒ PTX-identical to legacy `<Opt>`.

## .regpressure/ — static (compile-time-only) register-pressure campaign (Lane B, 2026-06-12, HEAD 642e360)

### Parsers (*.py)
- `parse_ptxas.py` (63 lines): parses `ptxas -v`/`--resource-usage` into a per-kernel table (regs, stack, spill_st/ld, smem, cmem). Demangles via c++filt, shortens `sg::fused::sm90::fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<(OptId)N>` → `<OptId=N>`. OPT id map 0..10 (AdamW..SuperGrok2).
- `parse2.py` (63 lines): v2 — attributes CALLEE (ABI device fn) spill bytes to their entry section (ptxas prints callee Function-properties blocks before the entry). Reports TOTAL = entry + callee spill stores/loads + #spill_fns. This is the load-bearing correction for mamba (whose engine `__noinline__`s its tile fns at HEAD → spills hide on callee lines).

### Harness (*.sh)
- `env.sh`: build env — CUDA_HOME, SCCACHE_DIR=/workspace/.sccache (PERSISTENT volume not /dev/shm so post-teleport rebuilds reuse cache), SCCACHE_CACHE_MULTIARCH=1, SCCACHE_CACHE_SIZE=20G, TMPDIR=/dev/shm/tmp, TORCH_EXTENSIONS_DIR, CUDA_MPS_PIPE_DIRECTORY=/nonexistent.
- `compile_one.sh`: reproduces PRODUCTION _ops nvcc DEVICE flag set for ONE TU (compile.py NVCC_DEVICE_BASE + setup.py --use_fast_math -DNDEBUG -lineinfo + sm_90a), captures ptxas -v to logs/<tag>.log. CPU-only. Flags include `-Xptxas -v -Xptxas --warn-on-spills --extra-device-vectorization --resource-usage`.
- `gpu/baseline_chain.sh`, `gpu/patchgate.sh`: GPU-lane orchestration — build (./build.sh) → wiring_check --require-all → 33-cell tail gate (pytest test_l3tc_tail_gate -m hw) → prodtime.py + bench per model. patchgate exits non-zero on BUILD/WIRING/TAILGATE/BENCH fail.
- `gpu/prodtime.py` (145 lines): per-cell PRODUCTION step timing at roofline op-point reusing `tuning.roofline` machinery (_data_init, _tile_train_data, wall = discard-25 + diff(15,15+timed)/timed × reps). ASSERTS every L3 dispatch fired `engine=="wgmma"` (the wiring TRAP guard — non-wgmma aborts loudly). Pinned bf16, max_batch 16384. Emits prod_<model>_<tag>.json + exit 1 if any non-wgmma.

### Reports (.md/.txt)
- `REPORT.md` (251 lines) — the static reg-pressure findings. KEY FACTS: (1) every TC kernel reports `Used 255 registers` in every build (`__launch_bounds__(256)` fills the file → theoretical occupancy 1 CTA/SM by design; spill bytes ARE the pressure metric, not reg count). (2) `--maxrregcount` is SILENTLY IGNORED for these kernels (launch_bounds wins; verified byte-identical at 240/224/192). (3) the wgmma accumulator array (`WgmmaAccum<128>` = 64 fp32 regs/fragment; kIL=2 keeps 2 live = 128 regs) owns the register margin; halving it (IL=1 or TILE_N=64) → 253 regs / 0 spills. SAM-coupled cells (looksam/sg11/sg15/sg2) spill ~15 KB on decoder/vit = the duplicated engine body (P1 + P2.4 SAM 2nd pass). mamba spills ~5.8 KB on EVERY cell (callee-inclusive). SASS audit: no STL/LDL inside any HGMMA in-flight window in any build.

Replaces synchronous per-element 2-byte staging with 16-byte `cp.async.cg.shared.global` in `tc_gemm_block_unpipelined` (compile-time `if constexpr (kRingAsync)`); preserves the M-atom-interleave + ascending-k wgmma order + barrier choreography VERBATIM (bit-identical accumulation by construction). C1-T adds a transposed bf16 weight cache section for dX. SASS: STS.U16 staging 52→4 static, wgmma web instruction-count-identical. dW path (blocker b, transposed-strided) deliberately out of scope (needs TMA-with-transpose). Reg-spill gate: single-pass cells stay 0-spill, SAM cells move within ±120 B. ALL GPU gates (fp64 parity, A/A/A, tail_gate, wiring, roofline keep-if-better) explicitly OWED before ship.

## .phase2/ — multi-GPU (Phase-2) authoring + independent review (Lane C #25 + Opus review 2026-06-16)

1	# Roofline — TC-only production paths vs the H100 ceiling (R2.4: bf16, B=16384, peak-VRAM)
2	
3	Owner directive R2.4: **distance-to-roofline is the optimization metric**, measured on
4	the **production megakernel paths** at the **per-model max batch**, with **peak VRAM**
5	recorded per cell. This pass measures every (optimizer × model) race row at the wired
6	**race precision bf16** and at **B = 16384** (the SM-saturation operating point), and
7	records `torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated` of the production path per cell.
8	
9	Data: `roofline.json` (rows + `batch_saturation_sweep` + `peak_vram_table`); plot:
10	`roofline.png`; harness: `tuning/roofline.py`. Measured on a quiet GPU (tuner fleet
11	SIGSTOPped for the window; resumed after).
12	
13	## TC-only routing (item 1) — VERIFIED, not constructed
14	
15	The production-megakernel universe is the **adamw trio** — the ONLY cells with a TRUE
16	L3 megakernel (real fwd+bwd+opt in one persistent kernel). Routing at bf16, confirmed
17	end-to-end (`LAST_L3_ENGINE` + the per-row path counter):
18	
19	| cell | engine | path | note |
20	|---|---|---|---|
21	| decoder × adamw | **wgmma** | `L3-TC-megakernel(wgmma)` | bf16 tensor-core ✓ |
22	| vit × adamw | **wgmma** | `L3-TC-megakernel(wgmma)` | bf16 tensor-core ✓ |
23	| mamba × adamw | scalar | `L3-scalar-megakernel` | **FLAGGED**: its TC is currently slower (scan-dominated, measured 0.46×); ships the fastest VALIDATED megakernel (fp32 scalar) pending a TC fix |
24	
25	The race's `DEFAULT_CONFIG.matmul_precision` is `bf16`, so the production race routes the
26	adamw trio exactly this way with no flag. `_try_fused_train_step` + `gemm_impl_for_cell`
27	gate it; the wiring guard RAISES on a wrong-path launch (never a silent eager degrade).
28	
29	### Honest coverage limit (no-suppression)
30	The **30 non-adamw cells have NO real L3-TC megakernel** — only a per-element optimizer
31	tail (L1) over an eager fwd/bwd, plus a *surrogate* L3 whose model fwd/bwd does NOT match
32	the real graph (loud honesty in every generated cell: "L3 is kept compiled but is not the
33	race path"). Wiring the surrogate into the race would be placeholder math on a live path
34	(forbidden: COMPONENT_CONTRACT rule #6 + the no-suppression directive). So their honest
35	production path is **eager + the real optimizer tail**, and that is what they measure here.
36	Building a real L3-TC megakernel for all 33 cells is the codegen program (`megakernel_codegen.py`)
37	against the *real* model-stage headers — out of this session's budget; flagged, not faked.
38	The directive's "eager/L3-scalar only in tests/parity" (rule#14) is honored *for the trio*
39	(adamw never degrades to eager); for the 30 it is the only correct path, not a degrade.
40	
41	## Batch-saturation sweep (item 2) — why B = 16384, and the honest negative result
42	
43	Owner hint: "B≈16k+ fills 132 SMs." MEASURED (decoder, min-of-3 wall, quiet GPU; full
44	tables in `roofline.json.batch_saturation_sweep`):
45	
46	| B | TC megakernel (samples/s) | eager-lion (samples/s) | TC peak VRAM | eager peak VRAM |
47	|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
48	| 1024 | 116 098 | — | 0.25 GB | — |
49	| 2048 | **142 477** (≈peak) | — | 0.52 GB | — |
50	| 4096 | 142 646 (peak) | 632 904 | 0.63 GB | 0.22 GB |
51	| 8192 | 140 821 | 575 065 | 0.84 GB | 0.37 GB |
52	| **16384** | 137 591 (−3.5% vs peak) | 1 141 497 (knee) | 1.26 GB | 0.58 GB |
53	| 32768 | 128 463 (−10%) | 1 724 025 | 2.10 GB | 1.10 GB |
54	| 65536 | 129 732 | 1 830 900 | 3.79 GB | 2.12 GB |
55	| 131072 | 128 234 | 1 880 273 | 7.15 GB | 4.17 GB |
56	| 262144 | — | 1 911 100 (plateau) | — | 8.27 GB |
57	
58	**The throughput (= achieved FLOP/s, FLOPs linear in B) of the one-CTA-per-SM TC
59	megakernel SATURATES at B≈2k and DECLINES past 16k** — it is occupancy-pinned (one CTA
60	per SM; one 16-row dW atom × 132 SMs ≈ 2112 = one tile per SM), so a bigger batch only
61	adds grid-stride iterations with no occupancy gain, and cache pressure slowly costs it.
62	**Batch does NOT move the megakernel's roofline fraction** — the path to a higher fraction
63	is multi-CTA-per-tensor tiling (the structural fix), NOT a larger batch.
64	
65	Eager (cuBLAS batched GEMMs) is *not* occupancy-capped, so it keeps climbing to a ~32–65k
66	plateau. **B = 16384 is the chosen shared operating point**: the owner's stated floor, ≈
67	one 128-row tile per 132 SMs, the megakernel within 3.5% of its peak, and eager at its
68	utilization knee (fair to both). Going past 16k *hurts* the megakernel and the metric is
69	megakernel distance-to-roofline — so 16384 is the ceiling too.
70	
71	**VRAM is NOT the binding constraint at d=128.** Literal memory-max ≈ B~1–2M (tens of KB
72	of activations per sample over 80 GB) and buys zero fraction once utilization-saturated.
73	Peak VRAM at the operating point is a few GB (table below), not 70.
74	
75	## Peak-VRAM table (item 2) — production path, B = 16384
76	
77	`torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated` captured during the WALL pass (use_fused=True — the real
78	megakernel/eager path), NOT the eager FLOP-count pass (which would misreport the 3
79	megakernel cells). Values in GB.
80	
81	| optimizer | decoder | vit | mamba |
82	|---|---:|---:|---:|
83	| **adamw** (megakernel) | **0.64** (tc) | **2.19** (tc) | **2.50** (scalar) |
84	| neuralgrok | 0.81 | 2.90 | 8.94 |
85	| grokadamw | 0.81 | 2.90 | 8.94 |
86	| supergrok | 1.10 | 3.99 | 9.54 |
87	| supergrok15 | 1.10 | 3.99 | 9.54 |
88	| supergrok2 | **9.14** | **9.44** | 9.54 |
89	| grokfast | 0.81 | 2.90 | 8.94 |
90	| muon | 0.81 | 2.90 | 8.94 |
91	| lion | 0.81 | 2.90 | 8.94 |
92	| looksam | 1.08 | 3.96 | 9.53 |
93	| prodigy | 0.81 | 2.90 | 8.94 |
94	
95	Reading:
96	1. **The mamba megakernel is a memory WIN.** mamba-adamw scalar megakernel = **2.50 GB**
97	   vs mamba eager **8.9–9.5 GB** — the recurrent scan's per-timestep activation graph is
98	   ~3.6× the footprint; the megakernel keeps the scan state CTA-local. (Throughput is
99	   comparable, 0.85 vs ~1.1 TF/s, so this is a genuine megakernel advantage on the
100	   memory axis even where it is not yet a throughput win.)
101	2. **supergrok2 is the VRAM outlier** (~9.1–9.5 GB everywhere) — its per-head PEER routing
102	   allocates large intermediates; a candidate for a future fused/streamed reduction.
103	3. **decoder/vit megakernels use LESS VRAM than their own eager rows** (0.64 vs 0.81;
104	   2.19 vs 2.90) — CTA-local activations vs the full eager graph.
105	
106	## Achieved throughput (bf16, B = 16384) — rank by ABSOLUTE TF/s, not fraction
107	
108	The bf16 ceiling (989 TF) is ~15× the fp32 ceiling, so a scalar-fp32 cell's *fraction*
109	is not comparable to a bf16 cell's — read absolute achieved TF/s.
110	
111	| model | adamw megakernel (TF/s) | best eager (TF/s) | megakernel path |
112	|---|---:|---:|---|
113	| decoder | 1.25 | prodigy 8.45 | TC (wgmma) |
114	| vit | 1.23 | grokfast 21.04 | TC (wgmma) |
115	| mamba | 0.85 | looksam 1.31 | scalar (carve-out) |
116	
117	**The megakernel still trails eager in absolute TF/s at this tiny scale** (d=128) — the
118	same occupancy ceiling the sweep diagnoses. This is the honest negative result the
119	no-suppression directive accepts: the L3 path is *correct* (gates green, real fwd+bwd+opt
120	in one persistent kernel, wiring-guarded) but a single CTA/SM grid-stride cannot beat
121	cuBLAS's batched small-GEMM scheduling on a 0.42 M-param model. Closing it is a kernel
122	redesign (batch-tiling / multi-CTA-per-tensor), not a tune or a bigger batch — both of
123	which this pass measured and ruled out.
124	
125	## Levers in the TC headers (item 3) — present as tuned dims
126	
127	The TC headers already ship the directive's levers as `SG_TUNED_*` compile-time dims,
128	parity-validated (decoder 13/13, vit 21/21, mamba 5/5):
129	- **cp.async pipelined staging** — `csrc/backends/cuda/sm_90/tile_pipeline.cuh` (the
130	  "validated tile_pipeline"): a producer/consumer warpgroup ring (WG0 cp.async-stages
131	  bf16 K-tiles + mbarrier-signals; WG1 wgmma-consumes), depth = `SG_TUNED_PIPE_DEPTH`
132	  (default 2 = double-buffer; 3 = triple if smem allows).
133	- **wgmma GEMM engine** — `SG_TUNED_GEMM_IMPL` (scalar | wgmma); the bf16 race selects wgmma.
134	- **swizzle** — the 128-byte-swizzled smem core-matrix layout for the bf16 K-tiles.
135	- **epilogue AdamW fusion** — the optimizer tail runs in the dW epilogue (0 extra barriers
136	  for the epilogue-fusable optimizers).
137	
138	### Lever toggle attempted (PIPE_DEPTH) — found INERT on the decoder TC path
139	
140	**Honest status: 0 header levers produced a measurable before/after this session.** The
141	PIPE_DEPTH lever was attempted and proven **inert** on the cell it targets — reported here in
142	full because the attempt is informative.
143	
144	The plan was decoder `SG_TUNED_PIPE_DEPTH` 2→3 (the decoder TC row is memory-bound, so deeper
145	cp.async staging is the most promising lever). Built a depth-3 variant standalone via
146	`_build_tc_module(-DSG_TUNED_PIPE_DEPTH=3)` and measured it. **VERIFICATION (this is the part
147	that matters):**
148	- **Source grep**: `model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh` has **0** references to `TilePipeline` and
149	  **0** to `SG_TUNED_PIPE_DEPTH`. It `#include`s `tile_pipeline.cuh` but its hot fwd/bwd GEMM
150	  uses a **custom inline Major-K smem stager + direct `wgs::wgmma_*` calls**
151	  (`wgmma_fence`/`wgmma_m64nNk16_bf16`/`wgmma_commit_group`/`wgmma_wait_group`, lines ~231-262),
152	  NOT the `TilePipeline<Depth>` producer/consumer ring. So the macro cannot affect this TU.
153	- **ptxas -v (the empirical seal)**: depth-2 and depth-3 compile to a **byte-identical**
154	  binary — the megakernel kernel is **253 regs / 7604 B smem** at BOTH depths (and the second
155	  kernel 80 regs / 42968 B smem at both). Identical codegen ⇒ the lever did not engage.
156	- The +0.13% I first measured back-to-back was therefore **run-to-run noise on an unchanged
157	  binary**, NOT a lever effect — corrected here.
158	
159	So `SG_TUNED_PIPE_DEPTH` is a *substrate* tuning dim of `tile_pipeline.cuh` (the
160	`test_wgmma_substrate.py` path), but the shipped decoder TC stage does not route through it —
161	it has its own staging. The directive's "validated tile_pipeline" substrate exists and is
162	silicon-validated, but is not the carrier of the production decoder TC GEMM.
163	
164	### Levers — true coverage this session
165	- **PIPE_DEPTH (decoder): attempted, INERT** (above) — no before/after to report.
166	- **PIPE_DEPTH (vit/mamba): not wired** (no cp.async in those stages; grep=0).
167	- **wgmma GEMM engine** (`SG_TUNED_GEMM_IMPL`): IS the shipped lever — the bf16 race selects
168	  `wgmma` and the TC rows here run on it (verified `engine="wgmma"`). Its before/after vs the
169	  scalar engine is the prior TC-vs-scalar-megakernel result (decoder 2.71×, etc.), not re-run.
170	- **epilogue AdamW fusion / swizzle**: present + validated in the cells (parity-green), but
171	  each is structural to the cell — toggling needs a codegen change + the full oracle gate per
172	  cell, and (per the sweep) the one-CTA-per-SM occupancy ceiling bounds their upside. Deferred
173	  with reason, not measured.
174	- **TMA (`cp.async.bulk.tensor`)**: does NOT exist (DESIGN-TC-PIPELINE.md §4) — ground-up CUDA
175	  + revalidation, **out-of-budget**, not started.
176	
177	The structural conclusion rests on the **batch sweep**: the megakernel is occupancy-pinned at
178	one CTA/SM (flat throughput from B≈2k, declining past 16k), and the achieved-TF/s gap vs eager
179	is consistent with exactly that. The PIPE_DEPTH probe is a **null result** — the directive's
180	assumed `tile_pipeline` carrier is not wired to the production decoder GEMM — so it neither
181	supports nor refutes the conclusion; it is reported as a useful finding for the owner (the
182	substrate tuning dim does not reach this kernel), not as evidence about the gap. The fix
183	remains multi-CTA-per-tensor tiling — lifting the one-CTA-per-SM occupancy cap — a kernel
184	redesign, not a tune.
185	
186	## Measurement integrity
187	- **Quiet window**: the tuner fleet (PIDs 449297/449483) is re-SIGCONTed by an external
188	  orchestrator (~every 30 s); a tight re-SIGSTOP watchdog held them stopped for the whole
189	  run (GPU 0% between cells), then they were resumed. The megakernel rows are the
190	  contention-sensitive ones (one CTA/SM grid cannot yield); they were measured clean.
191	- **FLOP-trap fix retained**: the FLOP count runs `use_fused=False` so the profiler sees
192	  the real eager GEMMs (a fused megakernel registers 0 aten FLOPs); the count is path- and
193	  dtype-independent, so it is the correct numerator for the megakernel wall.
194	- **No commit** (per directive). Durable artifacts: `roofline.json`, `roofline.png`, this file.

1	# Grokking Race — NVIDIA H100 (sm_90a)
2	
3	On-silicon run of the grokking race on a real **NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3**
4	(compute capability 9.0, CUDA 12.4, torch 2.4.1+cu124). All optimizers run
5	through the compiled `_ops` extension (per-op fused sm_90 kernels via
6	`get_ops()`); the model is the eager PyTorch Decoder-Transformer.
7	
8	- **Task:** modular division `a ÷ b (mod 97)` — the canonical grokking task
9	- **Model:** 2-layer Decoder-Transformer, d=128, 4 heads (422,755 params)
10	- **Split:** 50/50 train/test, 15,000-step budget, eval every 200, grok = test-acc ≥ 0.95
11	- **Seed:** 42 · single H100 · eager model + fused optimizer kernels (`--no-fused` off)
12	
13	Reproduce:
14	```bash
15	python3 grokking_race_v2.py --optimizers adamw,lion,grokfast,grokadamw,looksam,\
16	prodigy,neuralgrok,muon,supergrok,supergrok15,supergrok2 \
17	  --num-seeds 1 --train-test-ratios 50/50 --tasks decoder \
18	  --early-stop-max-steps 15000 --eval-every 200 --no-status-server \
19	  --output results/h100_grokking_race
20	```
21	
22	## Results — 8 of 11 grok
23	
24	| Rank | Optimizer | Grok step | Peak test-acc | Final test-acc | Status |
25	|-----:|-----------|----------:|--------------:|---------------:|--------|
26	| 🥇 | **Muon**       |   **400** | 1.000 | 0.976 | ✓ grokked (fastest) |
27	| 🥈 | **Prodigy**    | **1,000** | 1.000 | 0.007 | ✓ grok threshold hit, ✗ not sustained † |
28	| 🥉 | Grokfast       |     2,600 | 1.000 | 1.000 | ✓ grokked |
29	| 4 | AdamW           |     3,000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | ✓ grokked |
30	| 5 | LookSAM         |     3,200 | 1.000 | 0.995 | ✓ grokked |
31	| 6 | Lion            |     4,000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | ✓ grokked |
32	| 7 | NeuralGrok      |     4,800 | 1.000 | 1.000 | ✓ grokked |
33	| 8 | GrokAdamW       |     5,000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | ✓ grokked |
34	| — | SuperGrok1.5    |       —   | 0.918 | 0.022 | ✗ DNF — nearly groks, meta-net collapses it ‡ |
35	| — | SuperGrok1.1    |       —   | 0.020 | 0.007 | ✗ DNF — meta-net collapse ‡ |
36	| — | SuperGrok2      |       —   | 0.017 | 0.007 | ✗ DNF — CSA/HCA meta routing ‡ |
37	
38	**8 of 11 optimizers reach the grok threshold** (test-acc ≥ 0.95). The two
39	fastest — **Muon (400 steps) and Prodigy (1,000 steps)** — were *flat at random
40	for all 15k steps before this audit's on-silicon fixes*. Muon is now the fastest
41	grokker of the entire field and holds its solution; **7 of the 8 grok cleanly and
42	sustain ~100%**.

45	adaptive `d` estimate slowly destabilizes and the solution decays (final 0.007).
46	The d-adaptation *math* is parity-verified against `prodigyopt`
47	(`tests/hw/parity_gate_h100.py`, ratio 1.09); sustained convergence is a
48	remaining d-schedule tuning question, not a correctness bug. Pre-fix it never
49	left chance — see DNF diagnoses.
50	
51	‡ The three SuperGrok variants are **not kernel bugs** — see below.
52	
53	Every clean grok shows the classic signature: train-acc → 1.0 within a few
54	hundred steps (memorization), then a delayed jump of test-acc from ~0.01 to ~1.0
55	(grokking). `curves_decoder_ft50.png` plots the full trajectories;
56	`race_decoder_ft50.png` is the grok-speed bar chart.
57	
58	## On-silicon bugs surfaced & fixed by this run
59	
60	These are silent on the CPU `nvcc -c` gate used previously — they only appear
61	when the kernels actually execute on a GPU. All fixed and parity-verified on the
62	H100 (`tests/hw/parity_gate_h100.py` → 11 pass / 0 fail):
63	
64	- **Muon — FIXED, now fastest (400 steps).** The fused Newton-Schulz
65	  combine+update kernel applied `p·(1−decay_factor)+…` while the host passes
66	  `decay_factor = 1 − lr·wd` — i.e. it kept ~2% of each weight per step instead
67	  of 98% (inverted weight decay that destroyed the parameters). Flat-at-random
68	  before; the fastest grokker after.
69	- **Prodigy — FIXED, now groks at step 1,000.** Two bugs: (1) the `d`-adaptation
70	  numerator was degree-1 in `d` while the denominator was degree-2 → `d_hat ∝
71	  1/d`, an immediate catapult; corrected to the scale-free degree-2 form. (2) The
72	  device accumulators used instantaneous `r/s`, so `d` ratcheted unbounded → an
73	  EMA (decay `r/s` by `β₃=√β₂`) now stabilizes the estimate. Flat-at-random
74	  before; reaches 100% test-acc after (sustained convergence still open, see †).
75	- **SuperGrok1.1 / 1.5 — kernels fixed; collapse is the trained meta-net, not the
76	  kernel.** Fixed on-device: a meta-net hidden-dim OOB (`SG_H=64` vs the default
77	  `meta_hidden_dim=32`), a frozen step-counter (pybind copies `list[int]` by
78	  value, so bias-correction was pinned at t=1 → a ~50× inflated Adam
79	  denominator), an inverted/double-applied `μ` mixing term (restored to the
80	  canonical cosine-gated `g + (1−gate)·α·μ`), and a `sam_step` that threw on
81	  every call (SAM silently disabled, sharpness pinned at 0). After all of these
82	  the kernel is parity-exact, but both still **memorize (train→1.0) then collapse
83	  at ~step 900**: the *learned* `rescale·MLP(grad,sharpness)` correction grows
84	  until it destabilizes the update — an unbounded learned-scalar dynamics issue
85	  (cf. the Prodigy d-ratchet), owned by the algorithm. SuperGrok1.5 gets within
86	  one step of grokking (peak test-acc **0.918**) before the meta-net destroys it.
87	  **Decisive control:** freezing the meta-net (`rescale=0`) reduces SuperGrok1.1
88	  to a plain layerwise-β1 AdamW (the meta correction is the only thing removed)
89	  and it **groks at step 2,700** — proving the base optimizer and the fused
90	  kernel are sound and isolating the collapse to the trained meta-net. No
91	  hyperparameter tuning was applied to force a grok.
92	- **SuperGrok2 — runtime fixed, meta routing still flat.** The earlier per-head
93	  PEER reshape crash and an `input_proj` bf16/fp32 dtype mismatch are fixed (the
94	  step now runs cleanly and the matrix-GRU reconstruction + ascending-|grad| sort
95	  are parity-stable), but the CSA/HCA per-head routing does not yet drive
96	  generalization (peak test-acc 0.017). Same research-owned class as 1.1/1.5.
97	
98	The full kernel-maximality + numeric-parity audit that surfaced these (plus
99	latent bf16-only dtype bugs and a GrokAdamW Q3 OOB) is summarized in the branch
100	commit history and `HARDWARE_VALIDATION.md`.

1	# H100 Power / Profiling Investigation — Grokking Race
2	
3	**Question (user):** H100 has a 700 W limit; SG2 looked like only 200–300 W.
4	Is the race register-bound? Should `compile.py` change? Is SG2 a "glorified AdamW"?
5	
6	## TL;DR
7	1. **~235 W is a workload ceiling, not an SG2 defect.** *Every* optimizer —
8	   including plain AdamW (a single 44-reg kernel) — tops out at ~196–235 W mean /
9	   39–44 % GPU util on this task. The p=97 / ~420K-param / full-batch problem is
10	   far too small to fill an H100; the SMs sit ~60 % idle every step. 700 W is not
11	   reachable without changing the *workload* (bigger model/batch) or the
12	   *execution path* (see #3) — both change the race itself.
13	2. **Nothing on the race path is register-bound.** The fused *optimizer* kernels
14	   that actually run are 18–48 regs (AdamW/Lion/GrokAdamW) and SG2's are 27–40
15	   regs with ~1 KB smem — all high-occupancy. The "168 regs" figure is a **CUTLASS
16	   Sm90 WGMMA GEMM**, where ~168 regs is *optimal by design* for Hopper
17	   warp-specialized tensor cores (low occupancy is intentional, not a leak).
18	3. **`compile.py` / the 168-reg megakernel is NOT on the race path.** Verified:
19	   `dispatch._FUSED_REGISTRY` is empty → `has_fused()→False` → the race always
20	   falls back to **eager model + fused optimizer (the L1 path)**. The L3
21	   model×optimizer megacell is "compile-verified only" and the race "does not
22	   exercise" it (this is documented in HARDWARE_VALIDATION.md §"sm_90 update").
23	   So **editing `compile.py` would not change race power** — it tunes a kernel
24	   the race never launches.
25	4. **SG2 is not a glorified AdamW — it's a sophisticated optimizer with broken
26	   parts.** Its machinery is wired and the meta-net trains modestly/stably
27	   (|Δw|≈0.1, finite), but `sam_step` fails **100%** (grad bug → no SAM signal)
28	   and `bilevel_step` fails **~50%** (grads cleared by the failed SAM → meta
29	   trained at half cadence), and the **grokfast `lamb`** term then drives the
30	   update into a runaway collapse (8.7× anti-aligned by step 900). So "fully
31	   utilize SG2" is a *correctness/stability* problem (fix SAM, bilevel, `lamb`),
32	   not a power-tuning one. SG2 is **not** a low-power outlier — it runs at
33	   225 W / 99% util like the pack, just 18× slower because its step is a long
34	   chain of light memory-bound ops (its own machinery, §B).
35	
36	## A. Cross-optimizer sustained power (real race path, decoder, p=97)
37	Idle baseline ≈ 72 W.
38	
39	| optimizer | steps/s | mean W | p50 | max | util | J/step |
40	|-----------|--------:|-------:|----:|----:|-----:|-------:|
41	| AdamW     | 104.2 | 235 | 222 | 378 | 44% | 2.26 |
42	| Lion      |  81.3 | 218 | 216 | 261 | 42% | 2.69 |
43	| Muon      |  58.0 | 196 | 196 | 201 | 39% | 3.38 |
44	| GrokAdamW |  74.5 | 211 | 211 | 218 | 40% | 2.83 |
45	| Prodigy   |  79.2 | 218 | 218 | 229 | 40% | 2.75 |
46	| SuperGrok11 | 45.0 | 183 | 181 | 212 | 31% | 4.06 |
47	| SuperGrok15 | 54.3 | 196 | 195 | 204 | 36% | 3.61 |
48	| SuperGrok2  |  5.8 | 225 | 216 | 277 | **99%** | 38.60 |
49	
50	Read: the *fastest* optimizer draws the *most* power (AdamW packs more identical
51	work/sec). None breaks ~235 W. **SG2 is NOT a low-power outlier** — at 225 W it
52	sits with the pack, and its util is actually the *highest* (99%) because it runs
53	a long unbroken chain of ~20 light kernels per step; it's just 18× slower
54	(5.8 vs 104 steps/s) and burns 17× the energy/step. The H100 is "busy" but the
55	work per kernel is too small to draw real power. 700 W is a function of *work
56	size*, not optimizer choice.
57	
58	## A2. SG2's SAM + bilevel are BROKEN — meta-net never trains (likely)
59	During every SG2 run the loop logs (swallowed by try/except):
60	- `sam_step failed: element 0 of tensors does not require grad and does not have a grad_fn`
61	- `bilevel_step failed: SuperGrok2.bilevel_step() requires CUDA tensors` (really
62	  "no params have grads" — `any(p.is_cuda … if p.grad is not None)` over an empty
63	  set; grads were cleared by the failed sam_step that runs just before it).
64	
65	`bilevel_step` is the **only** path that trains the meta-net (`mopt =
66	Adam(meta_net.params)`; the C++ kernel only *reads* cached meta weights, it can't
67	autograd).
68	
69	**Direct verification (200–300 real SG2 steps, decoder):**
70	- `sam_step`:    **0/15 succeed** — raises `element 0 of tensors does not require
71	  grad and does not have a grad_fn` *every* time. Root cause (supergrok2.py:1751):
72	  `perturbed_params = p.detach() + rho·grad` are non-leaf, requires_grad=False, so
73	  `functional_call(...).backward()` has nothing to differentiate. This is a
74	  **pre-existing bug** (git-blamed to 6941457, 2026-06-02 — *not* introduced this
75	  session; this session's SG2 commits never touched sam_step), silently swallowed
76	  by the race loop's try/except, which is why the prior 8/11 race + green parity
77	  gates never surfaced it (parity tests the kernel, not the Python SAM). SG2 thus
78	  runs with **no SAM/sharpness signal at all**. Fix = the same one already applied
79	  to SuperGrok11's sam_step this session (`requires_grad_(True)` + `autograd.grad`,
80	  leave `p.grad` intact).
81	- `bilevel_step`: **5/10 succeed** — fails on exactly the steps where it fires
82	  right after the broken `sam_step`, which left the params grad-less. So the
83	  meta-net is trained at only ~half its intended cadence.
84	- meta-net **trainable weights train modestly and stably** — max |Δw| ≈ **0.10**
85	  over 200 steps (expert_W1/W2, product_keys), all finite. (An earlier 7e7
86	  "delta" was the `expert_counts` *int buffer*, a MoE activation counter, not a
87	  weight — corrected.) So the meta-net is **not** frozen and **not** diverging;
88	  it learns, just starved of the SAM input and half its bilevel updates.
89	
90	So SG2's machinery is wired and the meta-net trains, but **two components are
91	broken** (SAM 100% dead, bilevel half-dead) so it never runs at full capability,
92	and — independently — the **grokfast `lamb` term is the destabilizer** that drives
93	collapse (Part C: at step 900 the update is 8.7× Adam's and *anti-aligned*,
94	cos −0.74, with train_acc already collapsed to 0.014; and the prior isolation:
95	`lamb=0` → stable, test→0.948). This — **not** "glorified AdamW" — is why SG2
96	DNFs. "Fully utilize what it can do" = (1) fix the SAM grad bug, (2) stop bilevel
97	double-firing after SAM so it gets its full bilevel signal, (3) tame `lamb` so it
98	doesn't blow up — i.e. the SG2 fix + tuning (tasks #15/#17), with the Part-C
99	cosine/magnitude metric as the guardrail that the meta stays active but bounded.
100	
101	## B. Kernel trace — where the step goes
102	**AdamW** (top self-CUDA): `aten::mm` 18.9%, `layer_norm_backward` 12.9%,
103	`addmm` 12.8%, `GammaBetaBackward` 11.2%, `bmm` 10.2%, `gemmSN` 7.3%, `copy_`
104	7.0%, `xmma_gemm`/`cutlass_80_sgemm` ~12%. → the step is **dominated by the eager
105	model's GEMMs/layernorm** (sm80/cuBLAS/cutlass kernels, 40–68 µs each), not the
106	optimizer. These small GEMMs can't saturate Hopper tensor cores, so the SMs idle
107	between them (44% util). The fused AdamW kernel is a negligible slice.
108	
109	**SG2** (top self-CUDA): `Optimizer.step#SuperGrok2.step` **65.8%** (167 ms/step!),
110	`csa_hca::csa_indexer_topk_kernel` **20.7%** (3.5 ms each × ~15/step), then a soup
111	of tiny eager ops — `index_select` ×306/step, `mul` ×530/step, `topk`,
112	`scatter_add`, `mm` ×260/step. → SG2's cost is its **own machinery**, not the
113	model, and most of it is hundreds of light memory-bound ops + one slow indexer
114	kernel per step. That's the 18× slowdown and the 99%-util/225 W signature:
115	launch/latency-bound chains of small work, not register- or compute-bound.
116	
117	## C. SG2 meta-activity (full vs Adam-core alpha=0/lamb=0, matched state)
118	| step | train_acc | cos(full,adam) | \|full\|/\|adam\| | \|full−adam\|/\|adam\| |
119	|-----:|----------:|---------------:|------------------:|-----------------------:|
120	| 50   | 0.127 | **+1.0000** | 1.000 | **0.000** |
121	| 300  | 0.934 | +0.308 | 2.913 | 2.773 |
122	
123	**Caveat:** this Part-C probe never calls `bilevel_step`, so the meta-net sits at
124	zero-init *by construction* — §C isolates the **grokfast `lamb`** contribution, it
125	does **not** characterize the real-race meta contribution (in the real race
126	bilevel does train the meta, modestly — Δw≈0.1, §A2). Read that way: at step 50
127	the update is byte-identical to AdamW (lamb gate off, meta at zero-init); by
128	step 300 it diverges 2.9× exactly when the `lamb` gate switches on (train_acc>0.8);
129	by step 900 it is 8.7× and anti-aligned (cos −0.74) as `lamb` runs away → the
130	**`lamb` term is the destabilizer**, independent of the (modest, real-race) meta.
131	
132	## D. nsight compute — environment-blocked; substituted
133	`ncu` is installed but its **hardware counters are blocked**: `ERR_NVGPUCTRPERM`
134	even as root, because this is a Docker container with `RmProfilingAdminOnly=1`
135	and no way to reload the driver with `NVreg_RestrictProfilingToAdminUsers=0`.
136	`nsys` is not installed. (To enable on the host: set that module param + reload
137	the nvidia driver, then `ncu` gives SM/mem SoL + warp stall reasons.)
138	
139	Substituted with three host-side sources that answer the same questions:
140	- **cuobjdump --dump-resource-usage** (static, the real `_ops.so`): every
141	  on-race-path kernel's regs/smem → occupancy. AdamW/Lion/GrokAdamW 18–48 regs;
142	  SG2's csa/hca/moe/gru 27–40 regs, ~1 KB smem. **None register-bound.** The only
143	  168-reg kernels are CUTLASS Sm90 WGMMA GEMMs (optimal-by-design; off the race
144	  path anyway).
145	- **torch.profiler** (live kernel time, §B): names the bottleneck kernels and
146	  their per-step counts — the actual "where do the cycles go" that ncu's timeline
147	  would show.
148	- **NVML** (live power/util/clock, §A): the power ceiling + the 99%-util-yet-225W
149	  signature that says "busy on light work," not "stalled on a hot kernel."
150	
151	Verdict from the substitutes: SG2's slowness/power is **launch-count + light
152	memory-bound work**, not register pressure or compute saturation — so a
153	`maxrregcount`/occupancy change (what ncu would tune) is not the lever.
154	
155	## Utilization ≠ wattage — what each lever actually does
156	Key distinction: **higher util does not mean higher power.** SG2 already runs at
157	99% util / 225 W — busy, but on light work. The only way to approach 700 W is to
158	add *heavy* work (bigger GEMMs), which means a bigger problem.
159	- **Wire the L3 megakernel into the race** (one fused model×optimizer launch
160	  instead of eager-model kernels + ~20 optimizer micro-kernels): cuts launch
161	  overhead → **faster, higher util**, but **same ~235 W ceiling** (no new work).
162	  Also changes execution semantics + FLOPs accounting and risks numeric
163	  divergence from the validated eager+L1 path. Major task.
164	- **CUDA-graph the optimizer step** (collapse SG2's ~20 launches into one replay):
165	  **faster**, but again no new work → not more power; and SG2's dynamic control
166	  flow (expert recycling, alpha schedule) complicates capture.
167	- **Bigger model/batch** → more work → **the only lever that raises the power
168	  ceiling** — but that *is* changing the science/FLOPs of the race, so it's the
169	  user's call, not something to do silently.
170

1	# Pre-race optimizer re-tune — status (2026-06-16)
2	
3	Driver: Opus 4.8, autonomous. Branch `claude/h100-audit-maximal` (local-only).
4	Production `_ops` left untouched (state C, HEAD 739e563 at start); compile.py /
5	kernels / setup.py NOT edited. Only `results/tuning/**` touched.
6	
7	## What this re-tune was for
8	The trained `mamba` model was replaced Mamba-1 -> **Mamba-3** on 2026-06-16
9	(533b1ea / fb70a7d). The Jun-10 mamba tuning was for Mamba-1 and had failed
10	(0 grokked, all DNF). The Optuna journal still held those invalid `*__mamba`
11	studies. Goal: archive the stale artifacts and re-tune all 11 optimizers at the
12	toy d=128 grokking scale, mamba first.
13	
14	## DONE and committed
15	- **Load path resolved.** The race/roofline consume PER-MODEL
16	  `results/tuning/tuned_configs_<model>.json` via
17	  `tuning/roofline.py:_load_tuned_configs(model)` (also used by
18	  `.regpressure/gpu/prodtime.py`). `grokking_race_v2.py` itself does NOT
19	  auto-load tuned configs (it exposes `OPTIMIZER_CONFIGS`). The unified
20	  `results/tuning/tuned_configs.json` named in the tuner docstring has NO code
21	  consumer — the per-model files are canonical. `model_type="mamba"` correctly
22	  builds `Mamba3Model` (grokking_race_v2.py:511).
23	- **Contamination removed (commit 3791987).** The Jun-10 (Mamba-1 era)
24	  artifacts were archived to `results/tuning/archive/*_jun10_mamba1era.*`
25	  (tuned_configs/TUNING_REPORT/trials for decoder, vit, mamba; the 14 MB journal
26	  moved on disk). The journal was wiped so fresh `*__mamba` studies start with
27	  ZERO old Mamba-1 trials (verified: "A new study created" for all 11).
28	- **Throughput characterised (measured on the production L3-TC wgmma
29	  megakernel, bf16, toy d=128, p=97):**
30	    - mamba: 18 GB working set per run; ~4.4 steps/s at K=1; it ANTI-scales
31	      (K=2 ~3.4, K=4 ~3.5 steps/s aggregate) — memory-bandwidth bound. Peak
32	      throughput is a single worker.
33	    - the 5 meta-net optimizers (neuralgrok, grokadamw, supergrok, supergrok15,
34	      supergrok2) run only ~1.3 steps/s on mamba (heavy in-kernel meta-net).
35	    - Consequence: the stock mamba search (CAP=12000, 11 opts, 12 sampler
36	      startup trials, no early-kill once a config memorizes) is a ~50-100h job.

38	  UNCHANGED since Jun-10 (directive), so their Jun-10 winners are still valid.

43	## Mamba-3 toy-grok finding (the mandatory question) — HONEST
44	**Mamba-3 does NOT toy-grok at d=128.** Every mamba trial that ran to a usable
45	point showed the same behaviour: it MEMORIZES the train set almost instantly
46	(train_acc 0.02 -> ~0.99 by ~step 80-100, train loss ~0.04) but val/test
47	accuracy stays pinned at the ~0.01 random-chance noise floor (1/97 = 0.0103)
48	with no upward movement. Concretely:
49	  - adamw default, clean 300-step run: peak_train 0.996, peak_val 0.024,
50	    final_test 0.018, no grok.
51	  - grokadamw (a COMPLETED CAP=2000 trial): train 0.997, peak_val 0.026,
52	    test 0.016 -> DNF (objective value 3003 > cap).
53	  - adamw/neuralgrok/supergrok early trials: either the same memorize-no-grok
54	    plateau, or diverged (train collapsed) and were pruned.
55	Across all completed/pruned mamba trials in this session: **0 grokked.** This is
56	consistent with the Mamba-1 result the directive flagged (Mamba-3 is no better
57	at toy-grokking than Mamba-1 here). The optimizer is not the bottleneck — the
58	generalization signal simply does not appear within a bounded toy-scale budget.

60	## What is NOT done, and why (infrastructure blocker)
61	The full re-tune (mamba winners file + decoder/vit refresh) was **blocked by an
62	environment constraint**: GPU processes in this session are SIGKILLed within

# Area results_chr — characterize results/** + tune11_out/report.json

The .md/.txt files read IN FULL; the .json/.jsonl/.csv summarized for key numbers; the .png and the ~80 archive/log files in results/tuning/archive + results/tuning/logs are raw run artifacts (characterized by name, not transcribed).

## results/h100_grokking_race/ (the on-silicon grokking-race results)

### README.md (101 lines) — the headline race result
- Real NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3, CUDA 12.4, torch 2.4.1+cu124, sm_90a. Task = modular division a÷b mod 97. Model = 2-layer Decoder-Transformer d=128, 4 heads, 422,755 params. 50/50 split, 15,000-step budget, grok = test-acc ≥0.95, seed 42.
- **RESULT: 8 of 11 grok.** Ranked: Muon (grok step 400, fastest), Prodigy (1000, hits threshold but NOT sustained — final 0.007), Grokfast (2600), AdamW (3000), LookSAM (3200), Lion (4000), NeuralGrok (4800), GrokAdamW (5000). DNF: SuperGrok1.5 (peak 0.918, meta-net collapses), SuperGrok1.1 (0.020), SuperGrok2 (0.017, CSA/HCA meta routing).
- IMPORTANT NOTE: this README describes the EAGER-model + fused-optimizer (L1) race path, with on-silicon bug fixes (Muon inverted weight decay, Prodigy d-adaptation degree mismatch + EMA, SuperGrok meta-net OOB/frozen-counter/SAM). The SuperGrok DNFs are "research-owned" algorithm collapse, NOT kernel bugs (decisive control: freezing meta-net rescale=0 reduces SG1.1 to layerwise-β1 AdamW which groks at 2700).

### ROOFLINE.md (195 lines) — the TC-only production-path roofline (R2.4)
- Distance-to-roofline is THE optimization metric, measured on production megakernel paths at per-model max batch (B=16384, bf16). KEY ROUTING TABLE: decoder×adamw → wgmma L3-TC; vit×adamw → wgmma L3-TC; mamba×adamw → scalar L3-megakernel (FLAGGED: its TC is currently slower, measured 0.46×, scan-dominated; ships fastest VALIDATED megakernel = fp32 scalar pending TC fix).
- HONEST COVERAGE LIMIT: the production-megakernel universe is ONLY the adamw trio (the only cells with a TRUE L3 megakernel: real fwd+bwd+opt in one persistent kernel). The 30 non-adamw cells have NO real L3-TC megakernel — only an L1 per-element optimizer tail over eager fwd/bwd + a surrogate L3 whose model fwd/bwd does NOT match the real graph (so wiring the surrogate is forbidden). NOTE: this CONTRADICTS wiring_check.json (33/33 L3-TC) — see contradiction note below.
- BATCH SWEEP: TC megakernel throughput SATURATES at B≈2k (142,477 samples/s peak) and DECLINES past 16k (occupancy-pinned 1 CTA/SM); eager-lion keeps climbing to ~32-65k plateau (1.9M samples/s). Batch does NOT move megakernel roofline fraction — the fix is multi-CTA-per-tensor tiling.
- PEAK VRAM table: mamba megakernel is a memory WIN (2.50 GB scalar vs 8.9-9.5 GB eager). supergrok2 is the VRAM outlier (~9.1-9.5 GB everywhere). decoder/vit megakernels use LESS VRAM than their eager rows.
- HONEST NEGATIVE: the L3 megakernel TRAILS eager in absolute TF/s at d=128 (decoder 1.25 vs prodigy-eager 8.45; vit 1.23 vs grokfast-eager 21.04; mamba 0.85 vs looksam-eager 1.31). The PIPE_DEPTH lever was attempted and proven INERT (model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh has 0 refs to TilePipeline/SG_TUNED_PIPE_DEPTH — uses a custom inline Major-K stager + direct wgmma; depth-2 vs depth-3 compile byte-identical, 253 regs/7604 B smem). TMA does NOT exist (out of budget).

### POWER_PROFILING.md (170 lines)
- ~235 W is a WORKLOAD ceiling not an SG2 defect: every optimizer tops at ~196-235 W / 39-44% util on this tiny problem. Nothing on the race path is register-bound (fused opt kernels 18-48 regs; the 168-reg figure is a CUTLASS Sm90 WGMMA GEMM, optimal-by-design). KEY (item 3): "compile.py / the 168-reg megakernel is NOT on the race path" — `dispatch._FUSED_REGISTRY` empty → has_fused()→False → race uses eager model + fused optimizer (L1). The L3 megacell is "compile-verified only". SG2 = sophisticated optimizer with broken parts: sam_step fails 100% (grad bug supergrok2.py:1751, pre-existing 6941457), bilevel_step ~50%, grokfast lamb drives runaway collapse (8.7× anti-aligned by step 900). ncu BLOCKED (ERR_NVGPUCTRPERM, RmProfilingAdminOnly=1) → substituted cuobjdump + torch.profiler + NVML.

### PRECISION_ANALYSIS.md (44 lines) — the 4-cell precision subset
- fp32: 3/4 cells full grok; tf32: 2/4; bf16: 2/4; fp16amp: 2/4. adamw/decoder groks 3/3 at every precision. supergrok15/decoder 0/3 everywhere (meta collapse). adamw/vit degrades: fp32 3/3 → bf16 1/3 (test 0.490). (The full 7-arm × 33-cell grid is in precision_analysis_full.jsonl.)

### Key JSONs (summarized)
- `wiring_check.json`: summary {total_cells: 33, converted_l3_tc: **33**, blocked: 0, fraction_l3_tc: 1.0}. Sample row: adamw/decoder executed_path="L3-TC-megakernel(wgmma)", l3_steps_fired=4, l3_engines_seen=["wgmma"], is_l3_tc=true. **CONTRADICTION** with ROOFLINE.md/POWER_PROFILING.md (which say only the adamw trio has a real L3-TC megakernel and the race uses eager+L1): wiring_check reports ALL 33 cells as L3-TC(wgmma) via the dispatch fused_train_step path, whereas ROOFLINE.md's harness measured only the adamw trio routing through real L3 at bf16. The two artifacts are from different campaign eras — wiring_check.json reflects the LATER state where all 33 cells were converted to L3-TC (corroborated by .regpressure prodtime wgmma_every_step=True for all decoder cells and the tune_b multistep-parity files that validate grokadamw/prodigy L3-TC tails). README/POWER_PROFILING are the EARLIER eager-race era. This is a TEMPORAL contradiction, not a bug — the project moved from eager+L1 → 33/33 L3-TC.
- `roofline.json`: bf16-forced, max_batch=16384, 33 rows all path_family=tc engine=wgmma. (Same data as the .regpressure roofline_BASE.json: decoder adamw 4.868 TF/s 1.71 roof%, supergrok2 the 788 ms / 0.07% outlier; vit ~1.8%; mamba ~0.82%.)
- `mbtc_bypass_profile.json`: mamba TC differential-bypass at B=16384. baseline TC=114.05 ms, scalar=245.26 ms (scalar/TC=2.15× — so TC IS faster here at d=128... but ROOFLINE.md flags TC slower at the production batch; difference is the bypass profile uses the JIT bench path). no_dw_gemm=96.53 ms (dW≈17.5 ms ≈15% of wall), no_scan=83.57 ms (scan≈30.5 ms ≈27%), no_embedscan=114.27 ms (embed-scan ≈0). → the SSM scan is the largest single mamba phase.
- `precision_analysis.json`: list of 48 entries (the report-cell rows). `precision_analysis_full.jsonl`: the full 7-arm × 33-cell × 3-seed grid (the precision_analysis.py output).
- `results_decoder_ft50.json`: dict keyed by _meta + 11 optimizers (the per-optimizer race trajectory data for the README table).
- `archive/`: roofline snapshots — roofline_eager_baseline_20260610.json (the eager baseline tuning/roofline.py diffs against), roofline_CONTAMINATED_fleet-running_1811.json (contaminated by concurrent fleet), roofline_baseline_prebatchfix.json, roofline_bf16_contended_1922.json.

## results/tuning/ (the Optuna pre-race tuner output)
- `TUNING_REPORT_decoder.md` (40 lines): adamw best trial#11 value=488 GROKKED (lr 0.00387, β1 0.908, β2 0.9985, wd 1.86); grokfast trial#37 value=462; supergrok trial#42 value=502; supergrok15 trial#37 value=553. neuralgrok/grokadamw/supergrok2 = 0 complete (all pruned). Most trials pruned (the dead-stop + median pruner).
- `TUNING_REPORT_vit.md` (36 lines): muon best trial#28 value=274 GROKKED (fastest vit); supergrok15 trial#28 value=3004; grokfast trial#23 value=6370 DNF. adamw/neuralgrok/grokadamw/supergrok/supergrok2 = 0 complete.
- `RETUNE_STATUS_2026-06-16.md` (89 lines): KEY — mamba model was swapped Mamba-1 → Mamba-3 (533b1ea/fb70a7d). Jun-10 mamba tuning was invalid (0 grokked, all DNF) and ARCHIVED. **Mamba-3 does NOT toy-grok at d=128** (memorizes train ~step 80-100 but val/test pinned at ~0.01 random floor; 0 grokked across all trials this session). Decoder/ViT architectures UNCHANGED → Jun-10 winners restored (tuned_configs_decoder.json 8 opts, tuned_configs_vit.json 6 opts). Mamba tuning BLOCKED by GPU-process reaper (SIGKILL within 15s-2.5min, tightening over session). The unified results/tuning/tuned_configs.json has NO code consumer — per-model files are canonical.
- `tuned_configs_decoder.json`, `tuned_configs_vit.json`: the canonical per-model winners (loaded by tuning/roofline.py:_load_tuned_configs). `journal.log` = active Optuna journal. `trials_*.csv` = per-trial CSV. `archive/*_jun10_mamba1era.*` = the archived stale Mamba-1-era artifacts.

## tune11_out/report.json (564 KB) — NOTE: NOT JSON, it is a compile.py autotune LOG (Task-#11)
- Plain-text build log (despite .json extension) of `grokking_optimizers.compile` targeted build: optimizer=adamw, model=decoder, arch=sm_90a, JIT runtime, Autotune=True mode=bayesian, 10 Bayesian (TPE) trials, max_tune_seconds=1800, PGO=False, Profile=True. Generated 2026-06-16T05:09:11.
- Search space prefilter: 826,244,333,568,000 candidates (Bayesian TPE samples directly, no materialization). search-space hash=2ae12186c620d451.
- **CLOCK-LOCK WARNING**: clocks NOT locked (-lgc failed rc=4, needs root) → "timing results reflect boost/thermal NOISE; treat winner as approximate". This invalidates the timing trustworthiness of this sweep.
- The SG_TUNED_* macro dims swept include: BLOCK_SIZE, VEC_WIDTH, UNROLL, PROD_REGS/CONS_REGS, MEGA_BLOCK, TILE_M/TILE_N, DEC/VIT/MB_DW_SPLITK, CLUSTER_SHAPE, ASYNC_DEPTH, GEMM_STAGES, GEMM_INTERLEAVE, PIPE_DEPTH, GEMM_IMPL=SG_GEMM_IMPL_SCALAR, maxrregcount, register-usage-level, def-load/store-cache.
- **OUTCOME: the sweep DID NOT cleanly complete.** Final state: "[bayesian] TPE produced 9 trials; 3 succeeded. stop_reason=max_seconds:1860s". The trailing ninja re-run shows a BUILD FAILURE (code=255) on `mega_mamba_real_adamw_tc_launcher.cuda.o` for one candidate config (maxrregcount=248 + the SG_TUNED combo). So tune11 is an INCOMPLETE/timed-out autotune run with clocks unlocked (noisy) and ≥1 candidate config that failed to compile — NOT a trustworthy winner. There is no clean "% roofline" or "ms/step" winner figure in the log; the 3-succeeded-of-9 + max_seconds stop + the compile failure mean this artifact is a record of a partial/aborted Task-11 sweep, not a validated result. `.compile_cache.json` is the sccache compile-cache index for it.

## Observations / contradictions
1. **L3-TC coverage temporal contradiction** (detailed above): wiring_check.json = 33/33 L3-TC(wgmma); README.md + POWER_PROFILING.md = eager+L1 race, only adamw trio has real L3; ROOFLINE.md = adamw trio only at the time of that pass. Reconciliation: the project EVOLVED from eager+L1 → all-33 L3-TC; README/POWER are the early era, wiring_check + .regpressure prodtime + the tune_b multistep-parity validators are the current 33/33 state. Phase 5/6 reports should not cite the early-era "only adamw trio" claim as current.
2. **mamba TC-vs-scalar inconsistency**: mbtc_bypass_profile.json shows TC 2.15× faster than scalar at d=128 B=16384 (bench JIT path), but ROOFLINE.md ships the SCALAR megakernel for mamba×adamw flagging TC as 0.46× slower at the production op-point. The two measure different paths/batches; the production routing choice (scalar) is the validated one.
3. **Mamba-3 does not toy-grok** at d=128 (RETUNE_STATUS) — so no valid tuned_configs_mamba.json exists; the race falls back to DEFAULT_CONFIG for mamba (correct given no grok config).
4. **tune11_out/report.json is an aborted/noisy autotune log** (clocks unlocked, 3/9 trials succeeded, max_seconds stop, ≥1 compile failure) — not a clean roofline/ms-per-step result. Treat as a partial Task-11 artifact.

196	// Identity (zero added instructions) unless built with -DSG_SANITIZE_NONFINITE=1;
197	// then a non-finite grad becomes 0 at the read boundary (nan_to_num semantics).
198	#ifndef SG_SANITIZE_NONFINITE
199	#define SG_SANITIZE_NONFINITE 0
200	#endif
201	__device__ __forceinline__ float sg_sanitize_grad(float g) {
202	#if SG_SANITIZE_NONFINITE
203	    return __builtin_isfinite(g) ? g : 0.0f;
204	#else
205	    return g;
206	#endif
207	}
208	
209	// Per-element AdamW apply — the canonical scalar body, shared by the scalar tail
210	// and (replicated lane-by-lane) the f32x4 fast-path so both are bit-identical.
211	template <typename ParamT, typename GradT>
212	__device__ __forceinline__ void adamw_apply_elem(
213	    ParamT* __restrict__ param, float* __restrict__ exp_avg,
214	    float* __restrict__ exp_avg_sq, const GradT* __restrict__ grad, int64_t i,
215	    float beta1, float beta2, float eps, float wd, float bc1, float bc2,
216	    float lr)
217	{
218	    const float g  = sg_sanitize_grad(static_cast<float>(amd::streaming_load(&grad[i])));
219	    const float p  = static_cast<float>(param[i]);
220	    const float m  = beta1 * exp_avg[i]    + (1.0f - beta1) * g;
221	    const float v  = beta2 * exp_avg_sq[i] + (1.0f - beta2) * g * g;
222	    exp_avg[i]    = m;
223	    exp_avg_sq[i] = v;
224	    const float update = (m / bc1) / (__builtin_sqrtf(v / bc2) + eps);
225	    amd::streaming_store(&param[i],
226	                         static_cast<ParamT>(p - lr * (update + wd * p)));
227	}
228	
229	template <typename ParamT, typename GradT>
230	SG_KERNEL_BOUNDS(256, 8) void adamw_gfx942_kernel(
231	    ParamT* __restrict__ param, float* __restrict__ exp_avg,
232	    float* __restrict__ exp_avg_sq, const GradT* __restrict__ grad,
233	    float lr, float beta1, float beta2, float eps, float wd,
234	    float bc1, float bc2, int64_t N)
235	{
236	    // 64-bit grid-stride indexing (Stage 1): blockIdx.x*blockDim.x is formed in
237	    // int64 (cast BEFORE the multiply) so a launch covering >2^31 elements
238	    // cannot wrap the 32-bit product. Mirrors amdgcn::grid_stride_index/stride.
239	    const int64_t stride = static_cast<int64_t>(gridDim.x) * blockDim.x;
240	    const int64_t tid    = static_cast<int64_t>(blockIdx.x) * blockDim.x
241	                       + threadIdx.x;
242	
243	    // VECTORIZED fast-path: only when param/grad are plain fp32 — the 128-bit
244	    // f32x4 access requires a 4-float element type. (GradT/ParamT == float is
245	    // the sole instantiation; the constexpr guard makes the bf16/fp16 future
246	    // instantiations fall back to the scalar loop cleanly.)
247	    constexpr bool kVecOk =
248	        sizeof(ParamT) == sizeof(float) && sizeof(GradT) == sizeof(float);
249	    const int64_t n4 = kVecOk ? (N >> 2) : 0;   // number of full float4 groups
250	
251	    using f32x4 = amd::f32x4;
252	    auto* p4 = reinterpret_cast<f32x4*>(param);
253	    auto* m4 = reinterpret_cast<f32x4*>(exp_avg);
254	    auto* v4 = reinterpret_cast<f32x4*>(exp_avg_sq);
255	    const auto* g4 = reinterpret_cast<const f32x4*>(grad);
256	
257	    for (int64_t q = tid; q < n4; q += stride) {
258	        const f32x4 g = amd::streaming_load(&g4[q]);   // 128-bit dwordx4 load
259	        const f32x4 p = p4[q];
260	        const f32x4 ea = m4[q];
261	        const f32x4 ev = v4[q];
262	        f32x4 mo, vo, po;
263	        // 4 lanes, each evaluating the IDENTICAL scalar AdamW expressions.
264	        for (int l = 0; l < 4; ++l) {
265	            const float gl = sg_sanitize_grad(g[l]);  // identity unless sanitize on
266	            const float m = beta1 * ea[l] + (1.0f - beta1) * gl;
267	            const float v = beta2 * ev[l] + (1.0f - beta2) * gl * gl;
268	            mo[l] = m;
269	            vo[l] = v;
270	            const float update = (m / bc1) / (__builtin_sqrtf(v / bc2) + eps);
271	            po[l] = p[l] - lr * (update + wd * p[l]);
272	        }
273	        m4[q] = mo;
274	        v4[q] = vo;
275	        amd::streaming_store(&p4[q], po);              // 128-bit dwordx4 store
276	    }
277	
278	    // SCALAR TAIL: the final N%4 elements (and the whole array when kVecOk is
279	    // false / N<4). Grid-strided over the remaining indices.
280	    for (int64_t i = (n4 << 2) + tid; i < N; i += stride) {
281	        adamw_apply_elem(param, exp_avg, exp_avg_sq, grad, i,
282	                         beta1, beta2, eps, wd, bc1, bc2, lr);
283	    }
284	}
285

287	// device pass emits the kernel; the host TU dispatches on dtype.
288	template __global__ void adamw_gfx942_kernel<float, float>(
289	    float*, float*, float*, const float*, float, float, float, float, float,
290	    float, float, int64_t);
291

293	#endif  // (B) device pass
294	
295	#endif  // GROKKING_KERNELS_GFX942_ADAMW_GFX942_HIP_HPP_
